content:
AIT 和 TECRO 通过新的台湾奖学金计划加强美国与台湾的伙伴关系 PR-2631 2026 年 11 月 11 日 AIT 和 TECRO 通过新的台湾奖学金计划加强美国与台湾的伙伴关系 2026 年 11 月 10 日，美国在台协会 (AIT) 华盛顿董事总经理 Ingrid Larson 和台北驻美国经济文化代表处 (TECRO) 代表 Alexander Tah-Ray Yui 签署了一份建立台湾奖学金计划（TFP）的谅解备忘录（MOU）。 《台湾奖学金法案》在两党广泛支持下获得国会通过并签署成为法律。今天，AIT 和 TECRO 签署了谅解备忘录，并与国务院教育和文化事务局协调，启动了该计划的实施。该计划的主要目标是扩大和加强美台伙伴关系，并加强美国官员在台湾和海峡两岸问题上的专业知识。 TFP 将在台湾各地建立一批具有语言技能、文化知识和持久工作关系的联邦专业人士。根据该奖学金计划，美国联邦雇员将花费长达一年的时间进行强化普通话培训和地区研究。培训完成后，研究员预计将在台湾议会办公室、部委、其他机构或办公室或台湾公共部门以外的组织工作最长一年。
Members of Congress and representatives from the U.S.Department of State, TECRO, and AIT attended the signing ceremony in Arlington, Virginia, where attendees praised the program’s role in strengthening the U.S.-Taiwan partnership and building U.S. government expertise on Taiwan. “TFP reflects strong bipartisan support for the U.S.-Taiwan relationship and a shared commitment to the people-to-people ties at its core,” said AIT Managing Director Ingrid Larson. 《AIT 和 TECRO 通过新台湾奖学金计划加强美台伙伴关系》一文首先发表在美国在台协会上。

【原文 English Original】
AIT and TECRO Strengthen U.S.-Taiwan Partnership Through New Taiwan Fellowship Program PR-2631 November 11, 2026 AIT and TECRO Strengthen U.S.-Taiwan Partnership Through New Taiwan Fellowship Program   On November 10, 2026, American Institute in Taiwan (AIT) Washington Managing Director Ingrid Larson and the Taipei Economic and Cultural Representative Office in the United States (TECRO) Representative Alexander Tah-Ray Yui signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) to establish the Taiwan Fellowship Program (TFP).   The Taiwan Fellowship Act was passed by Congress and signed into law with broad bipartisan support. Today’s signing of the MOU between AIT and TECRO initiates the program’s implementation, in coordination with the Department of State’s Bureau of Educational and Cultural Affairs. The main objectives of the Program are to expand and strengthen the U.S.-Taiwan partnership, as well as strengthen U.S. officials’ expertise regarding Taiwan and cross-Strait issues. TFP will build a group of federal professionals with language skills, cultural knowledge, and lasting working relationships across Taiwan.   Under the fellowship program, U.S. federal employees will spend up to one year in intensive Mandarin language training and area studies. Upon completion of training, the Fellows are expected to work, for up to one year, in Taiwan parliamentary offices, ministries, other agencies or offices, or organizations outside the public sector in Taiwan.   Members of Congress and representatives from the U.S. Department of State, TECRO, and AIT attended the signing ceremony in Arlington, Virginia, where attendees praised the program’s role in strengthening the U.S.-Taiwan partnership and building U.S. government expertise on Taiwan.   “TFP reflects strong bipartisan support for the U.S.-Taiwan relationship and a shared commitment to the people-to-people ties at its core,” said AIT Managing Director Ingrid Larson. 随着五角大楼最终完成对美国在欧洲的军事态势的审查，一项相对较小的承诺值得避免预算削减：即在北约科索沃部队服役的约 600 名美国士兵。他们几乎没有参与关于旅和数十亿美元项目的辩论，但他们在巴尔干地区保持了来之不易的和平，将他们撤出几乎什么也挽救不了，同时让莫斯科获得了廉价的战略胜利。驻科部队于 1999 年 6 月在北约指挥下部署，此前北约轰炸了南斯拉夫，以制止斯洛博丹·米洛舍维奇领导的塞尔维亚军队对阿尔巴尼亚人的暴力行为。科索沃于2008年宣布独立，但塞尔维亚在俄罗斯和中国的支持下仍然拒绝承认。欧洲态势评估是一项合法的活动。在多年来敦促欧洲盟国承担更多常规防御之后，特朗普政府正确地提出了一些尖锐的问题，即美国军队在哪些方面可以增加独特的价值，以及在适当的时间发展其能力和能力的情况下欧洲可以在哪些方面加强。但驻科部队是一项美国角色不易被取代的任务，因为它既是政治性的，也是军事性的，而且错误的决定可能会导致欧洲东南侧的不稳定。从威胁开始。即使在乌克兰遭受重大损失的同时，弗拉基米尔·普京也没有放弃破坏欧洲稳定的努力。巴尔干地区是欧洲的软肋，是一个备受青睐的舞台：煽动成本低廉，是一个分散西方对乌克兰注意力的地方。
莫斯科长期以来一直利用塞尔维亚作为破坏科索沃稳定的杠杆。2017年，一列俄罗斯制造的火车开往科索沃北部，这是一次带有“科索沃是塞尔维亚”口号的滚动挑衅。俄罗斯在科索沃附近运营着一个所谓的人道主义中心，该中心被怀疑充当俄罗斯情报站。塞尔维亚与俄罗斯密切的情报联系使莫斯科能够接触到准备挑衅的当地民族主义力量。 2023年，科索沃北部警察遭到武装袭击，普里什蒂纳将此归咎于塞尔维亚支持的武装分子，这加剧了人们对与俄罗斯结盟的行为体利用紧张局势的担忧；今年早些时候，俄罗斯外交部长警告称，“欧洲中心正在酝酿一场重大爆炸性局势”。紧张局势一再爆发。 2023年5月，塞尔维亚抗议者与科索沃警察发生冲突，造成90多名北约维和人员受伤，促使塞尔维亚提高军事戒备级别。那年 9 月，在巴尼斯卡发生的一次袭击中，全副武装的塞族枪手杀死了一名科索沃警察，并将自己关在一座修道院里，这表明当地的冲突可以多么迅速地演变为地区危机。危险还没有过去。塞尔维亚强人亚历山大·武契奇承认在10月25日的塞尔维亚议会选举中落败，但贝尔格莱德的外交政策方向尚不确定，人们担心其对科索沃的看法不会改变。

【原文 English Original】
As the Pentagon finalizes its review of U.S. force posture in Europe, one relatively small commitment deserves protection from the budget axe: the roughly 600 American troops serving in NATO’s Kosovo Force. They barely register in a debate about brigades and billion-dollar line items, but they keep a hard-won peace in the Balkans, and pulling them out would save almost nothing while handing Moscow a cheap strategic win. KFOR was deployed in June 1999 under NATO command, after the alliance bombed Yugoslavia to stop the violence perpetrated by Slobodan Milosevic’s Serbian forces against ethnic Albanians. Kosovo declared independence in 2008, but Serbia, backed by Russia and China, still refuses to recognize it. The Europe posture review is a legitimate exercise. After years of urging European allies to shoulder more of their own conventional defense, the Trump administration is right to ask hard questions about where American forces add unique value and where Europe can step up given suitable time to develop their capabilities and capacities. But KFOR is a mission in which the American role is not easily replaced, because it is as much political as military, and where a wrong call risks instability on Europe’s southeastern flank. Start with the threat. Even while absorbing heavy losses in Ukraine, Vladimir Putin has not given up on destabilizing Europe. The Balkans, Europe’s soft underbelly, are a favored arena: cheap to stir, a place to distract Western attention from Ukraine. Moscow has long used Serbia as a lever against Kosovo’s stability. In 2017, a Russian-made train was sent toward northern Kosovo, a rolling provocation that bore the slogan “Kosovo is Serbia.” Russia runs a so-called humanitarian center near Kosovo that is suspected of serving as a Russian intelligence station. Close Serbian-Russian intelligence ties give Moscow access to local nationalist forces prepared for provocations. In 2023, an armed attack on Kosovo police in the north, which Pristina blamed on Serbian-backed militants, heightened fears that Russian-aligned actors were exploiting the tension; earlier that year, Russia’s Minister of Foreign Affairs warned that “a major explosive situation is brewing in the heart of Europe.” Tensions have repeatedly flared. In May 2023, clashes between Serb protesters and Kosovo police injured more than 90 NATO peacekeepers and prompted Serbia to raise its military alert level. That September, an attack in Banjska, where heavily armed Serb gunmen killed a Kosovo police officer and barricaded themselves in a monastery, showed how quickly a local flare-up can become a regional crisis. The danger has not passed. Serbian strongman Aleksandar Vucic conceded defeat in Serbia’s Oct. 25 parliamentary election, but Belgrade’s foreign-policy direction is uncertain and there are concerns that its views on Kosovo will not change. In October, Russia’s ambassador to the UN warned that the situation in Kosovo “remains persistently tense and is literally teetering on the brink.” Still, Kosovo and Serbia have remained at peace since 1999, in large part because of KFOR. In the words of a bipartisan group of U.S lawmakers, the force functions as “a political deterrent to those seeking to stoke ethnic violence.” An American drawdown from KFOR may embolden nationalist agendas in Kosovo and Serbia as well as separatist ambitions in Republika Srpska, the Serb-dominated region in nearby Bosnia. The American presence in KFOR is valued precisely because it is American. U.S. troops have anchored KFOR since its creation, and Washington currently leads Regional Command East, a position of real operational weight, not symbolism. The U.S. has traditionally provided the 600 or so American troops—often Army National Guardsmen—an economy-of-force mission with minimal cost or effect on the U.S. Army’s ability to execute missions elsewhere around the globe. The mission accounts for less than 1 percent of the total U.S. troops in Europe. KFOR’s value becomes plain when contrasted with Operation Althea in neighboring Bosnia. EUFOR, an EU-led force with roughly 1,500 troops, has struggled to respond decisively to repeated provocations by Republika Srpska leader Milorad Dodik, who’s backed by Moscow and Belgrade. EU ambassadors rejected Bosnian appeals to help enforce an arrest warrant against him in 2025, citing political risk. Dodik has openly mocked EUFOR’s patrols. Lacking an American anchor and a unified chain of command willing to act, EUFOR has too often had to manage crises rather than deterring them. KFOR, by contrast, has demonstrated it can surge forces when tested, providing genuine deterrence. After the 2023 Banjska incident, NATO increased its peacekeeping presence in Kosovo. Serbia drew down its border deployment, ending the crisis. The Pentagon is right to ask what the value of an American military presence is worth. For KFOR, the answer is plain: a few hundred U.S. troops are successfully maintaining a quarter-century-long peace that Russia would love to see unravel. Lawmakers from both parties already understand that. The Pentagon should, too, and keep KFOR intact. Mark Montgomery, a retired U.S. Navy rear admiral, serves as a senior director at the Foundation for Defense of Democracies’ (FDD), where Ivana Stradner is a research fellow. ]]>

title: Topco Scientific Establishes Dresden Hub, Makes SEMICON Europa Debut
zh_title: Topco Scientific 建立德累斯顿中心，SEMICON Europa 首次亮相
summary: 在《欧洲芯片法案》和半导体本土化制造趋势的推动下，欧洲对材料、设备和技术服务的需求日益受到关注。半导体产业综合服务商拓普科科技股份有限公司（TAIEX：5434）宣布，其德国子公司拓普科德国有限公司（TOPCO GERMANY）将首次参加11月10日至13日在德国慕尼黑展览中心举行的SEMICON Europa 2026，与台湾、日本的供应商合作伙伴一起展示其跨界合作。
content:
在《欧洲芯片法案》和半导体本土化制造趋势的推动下，欧洲对材料、设备和技术服务的需求日益受到关注。半导体产业综合服务商拓普科科技股份有限公司（TAIEX：5434）宣布，其德国子公司拓普科德国有限公司（TOPCO GERMANY）将首次参加11月10日至13日在德国慕尼黑展览中心举行的SEMICON Europa 2026，与台湾、日本供应商合作伙伴展示其跨境资源一体化和本地化服务能力。拓普科德国于2026年8月正式成立，将亮相台湾馆，展示涵盖工艺材料、特种化学品、扩散工艺清洗设备、关键零部件的一站式解决方案。这些解决方案旨在支持欧洲代工厂和汽车电子制造商的晶圆厂建设和生产需求。作为欧洲最大的半导体集群之一，德累斯顿是博世、英飞凌、恩智浦和格罗方德等主要半导体公司的所在地。随着世界领先的铸造厂在德国落户，TOPCO SCIENTIFIC 正在加速向欧洲市场的扩张。
该公司利用德累斯顿当地团队提供及时的材料供应和技术支持，将来自台湾、日本和其他市场的领先材料、设备和耗材供应商与欧洲客户联系起来。这种集成服务模式可帮助客户在半导体工厂不断扩张的情况下减轻供应链中断风险，并降低资质和入厂成本。对于关键的前端工艺材料，拓普科将在展会上展示日本供应商SHIN-ETSU POLYMER的12英寸晶圆载具解决方案，满足欧洲12英寸代工厂和集成器件制造商（IDM）严格的清洁度和自动化要求。其前开式统一盒 (FOUP) 具有抗静电保护和一体式结构，有助于缩短清洁和干燥周期，同时有效减少颗粒的产生。该公司还将展示符合 SEMI 标准的前开式运输箱 (FOSB)，并具有坚固的密封结构，可在长途国际运输过程中保护晶圆。为了满足先进半导体工艺的微缩要求，拓普科引进日本先进的前驱体材料，为高端薄膜沉积工艺提供全面的解决方案，包括化学气相沉积（CVD）和物理气相沉积（PVD）。
这些材料具有超高纯度和出色的热稳定性，有助于提高器件性能和产量，支持可靠的先进半导体制造。对于蚀刻和薄膜沉积工艺，TOPCO SCIENTIFIC 将展示使用 TAIWAN E&M SYSTEMS 的定制精密加工能力制造的关键组件。这些组件由石英、硅、陶瓷和碳化硅 (SiC) 制成，与主要半导体设备平台兼容。结合专门的抗等离子和耐磨涂层技术，它们有助于延长设备耗材的使用寿命，使客户能够提高产量，同时支持更可持续的制造。

【原文 English Original】
Driven by the European Chips Act and the trend toward localized semiconductor manufacturing, demand for materials, equipment, and technical services in Europe has attracted growing attention. TOPCO SCIENTIFIC Co., Ltd. (TAIEX: 5434), an integrated services provider for the semiconductor industry, announced that its German subsidiary, TOPCO SCIENTIFIC Germany GmbH (TOPCO GERMANY), will participate for the first time in SEMICON Europa 2026, to be held at Messe München in Germany from November 10 to 13. Together with supplier partners from Taiwan and Japan, the company will showcase its cross-border resource integration and localized service capabilities. Officially established in August 2026, TOPCO GERMANY will exhibit at the Taiwan Pavilion, presenting one-stop solutions covering process materials, specialty chemicals, diffusion process cleaning equipment, and critical components. These solutions are designed to support the fab construction and production needs of European foundries and automotive electronics manufacturers. As one of Europe’s largest semiconductor clusters, Dresden is home to major semiconductor companies, including Bosch, Infineon, NXP, and GlobalFoundries. With the world’s leading foundry establishing a presence in Germany, TOPCO SCIENTIFIC is accelerating its expansion into the European market. Leveraging its local team in Dresden to provide timely materials supply and technical support, the company connects leading materials, equipment, and consumables suppliers from Taiwan, Japan, and other markets with European customers. This integrated service model helps customers mitigate supply chain disruption risks and reduce qualification and onboarding costs amid the ongoing expansion of semiconductor fabs. For critical front-end process materials, TOPCO SCIENTIFIC will showcase 12-inch wafer carrier solutions from Japanese supplier SHIN-ETSU POLYMER at the exhibition, addressing the stringent cleanliness and automation requirements of European 12-inch foundries and integrated device manufacturers (IDMs). Its Front Opening Unified Pod (FOUP), featuring antistatic protection and an integrated, one-piece construction, helps shorten cleaning and drying cycles while effectively minimizing particle generation. The company will also showcase Front Opening Shipping Box (FOSB) that comply with SEMI standards and feature robust sealing structures to protect wafers during long-distance international transportation. To address the scaling requirements of advanced semiconductor processes, TOPCO SCIENTIFIC introduces advanced precursor materials from Japan, offering comprehensive solutions for high-end thin-film deposition processes, including chemical vapor deposition (CVD) and physical vapor deposition (PVD). Featuring ultra-high purity and excellent thermal stability, these materials help enhance device performance and yield, supporting reliable advanced semiconductor manufacturing. For etching and thin-film deposition processes, TOPCO SCIENTIFIC will showcase critical components manufactured using customized precision machining capabilities from TAIWAN E&M SYSTEMS . These components, made from quartz, silicon, ceramics, and silicon carbide (SiC), are compatible with major semiconductor equipment platforms. Combined with specialized plasma-resistant and wear-resistant coating technologies, they help extend the service life of equipment consumables, enabling customers to improve yield while supporting more sustainable manufacturing. For semiconductor facility engineering and equipment maintenance, TOPCO SCIENTIFIC also offers solutions for the maintenance and servicing of critical equipment and precision components. In the diffusion process segment, the company introduces quartz cleaning equipment from Japanese supplier FIRST EXA to improve the cleanliness of quartz components. Using automated acid cleaning and nitrogen purging technologies, the equipment effectively removes residues from high-temperature deposition processes, reduces particle contamination, and extends the service life of quartz consumables, helping safeguard wafer yield. Charles Lee, President of TOPCO SCIENTIFIC, said, “The regionalization and localization of global semiconductor supply chains have become an irreversible trend. TOPCO SCIENTIFIC established its German subsidiary in August 2026, positioning Dresden as its European operational and technical service hub. This move not only strengthens our presence in Europe but also establishes an important strategic hub for global supply chain integration. Building on more than 35 years of experience in the semiconductor industry, we connect suppliers from Taiwan and Japan with local European customers, providing timely technical support and integrated services. Going forward, we will further strengthen strategic cooperation with leading European suppliers to build an international supply chain platform connecting Asia and Europe and serving customers worldwide, thereby enhancing global supply chain resilience.” The post Topco Scientific Establishes Dresden Hub, Makes SEMICON Europa Debut appeared first on Semiconductor Digest .

title: U.S. Transfers Unmanned Surface Vessels to Philippine Marine Corps
zh_title: 美国向菲律宾海军陆战队转让无人水面舰艇
summary: 一艘 MARTAC Devil Ray T38 无人水面舰艇。 MARTAC 照片 菲律宾海军陆战队上周在苏比克湾接收了两艘美国制造的无人水面舰艇，这是华盛顿加强马尼拉在南中国海和吕宋海峡的不对称能力的努力的一部分。 11月4日，两艘海上战术系统T38魔鬼鱼无人水面艇被转移到苏比克湾的菲律宾海军陆战队。 PMC 部表示：“今天标志着我们继续努力加强菲律宾海军陆战队能力的又一个有意义的步骤，特别是在群岛海岸防御领域。”
content:
一艘 MARTAC Devil Ray T38 无人水面舰艇。 MARTAC 照片 菲律宾海军陆战队上周在苏比克湾接收了两艘美国制造的无人水面舰艇，这是华盛顿加强马尼拉在南中国海和吕宋海峡的不对称能力的努力的一部分。 11月4日，两艘海上战术系统T38魔鬼鱼无人水面艇被转移到苏比克湾的菲律宾海军陆战队。菲律宾海军陆战队副司令准将说：“今天标志着我们在不断努力加强菲律宾海军陆战队能力方面又迈出了有意义的一步，特别是在群岛海岸防御领域。”根据美国海军学院新闻提供的文字记录，巴亚尼·库拉明将军出席了仪式。据美国海军学院新闻六月报道，菲律宾海军陆战队被定为继菲律宾海军之后下一支接收无人机的部队。马尼拉海军陆战队处于南海争端的最前线，驻守着被大批中国正规军和准军事部队包围的前哨基地。一位熟悉此事的美国国防官员也强调了菲律宾陆军通过该计划接收无人机的可能性。据美国海军学院新闻了解，该部队正在寻求扩大其群岛海岸防御计划中监测和控制受威胁目标的能力。近年来，菲律宾海军陆战队装备了布拉莫斯岸防巡航导弹，并被部署到从苏禄海到吕宋海峡的战略海上交通线上。
横须贺亚太研究委员会东南亚区域项目主任查理·布朗告诉美国海军学院新闻，无人机转移使海军陆战队能够“在广阔且竞争日益激烈的海域”保持意识。布朗说：“这是建立可信的群岛防御能力的一个重要因素：不一定要与对手的平台相匹配，而是利用技术、信息共享和分布式能力使菲律宾的海上途径更加透明，其领土防御更具弹性。”在马尼拉和北京之间因南海争议领土问题出现一系列紧张局势之后，五角大楼正在做出更广泛的努力，以增强菲律宾的领海意识。 2023年以来，中国和菲律宾军队多次就对方声称拥有主权的多个浅滩和岛礁发生冲突。马尼拉为对抗中国军队而进行的新生现代化努力得到了美国和日本越来越多的支持。总部位于佛罗里达州的海上无人机制造商 Maritime Tactical Systems, Inc. 很早就被任命为菲律宾海军提供第一批无人水面航行器。目前，海军第一支无人水面航行器的核心由一艘 T38 Devil Ray 和四艘 MANTIS T12 组成。海军陆战队无人水面艇被转移到 MARTAC 的新苏比克湾设施。
根据该公司发布的消息，该无人机卓越中心旨在培训菲律宾无人机操作员并为“魔鬼鱼”储备零部件。MARTAC 发布的消息称：“该中心还将为当地创造就业机会和建立合作伙伴关系，以增强菲律宾在未来几年部署大型 USV 舰队的能力。”今年夏天，总部位于密西西比州的自主 USV 公司 Ocean Aero, Inc. 向菲律宾海军交付了四架 Triton 无人机。美国-菲律宾倡议目前的重点是提供海域意识能力，以解决东南亚群岛周围的重大差距

【原文 English Original】
A MARTAC Devil Ray T38 unmanned surface vessel. MARTAC photo The Philippine Marine Corps received two American-made unmanned surface vessels last week at Subic Bay as part of Washington’s efforts to bolster Manila’s asymmetric capabilities in the South China Sea and Luzon Strait. On Nov. 4, two Maritime Tactical Systems T38 Devil Ray USVs were transferred to the Philippine Marine Corps at Subic Bay. “Today marks another meaningful step in our continuing effort to strengthen the capabilities of the Philippine Marine Corps, particularly in the field of archipelagic coastal defense,” said PMC Deputy Commandant Brig. Gen. Bayani Curaming at the ceremony, according to a transcript provided to USNI News. The Philippine Marine Corps was slated as the next force to receive drones after the Philippine Navy, USNI News reported in June . Manila’s Marines are at the forefront of South China Sea disputes, manning outposts surrounded by swarms of Chinese regular and paramilitary forces. An American defense official familiar with the matter also highlighted the possibility of the Philippine Army receiving drones through the program. The force is looking to expand its capabilities to monitor and hold targets under threat in its Archipelagic Coastal Defense plan, USNI News understands. In recent years, Philippine Marines have been equipped with BrahMos coastal defense cruise missiles and were relocated to strategic sealines of communication from the Sulu Sea to the Luzon Strait. Charlie Brown, the Director of the Yokosuka Council on Asia Pacific Studies’ Southeast Asia Regional Program, told USNI News that the drone transfer enables the Marines in maintaining awareness “across a large and increasingly contested maritime domain.” “This is an important element of building a credible archipelagic defense capability: not necessarily matching an adversary platform for platform, but using technology, information-sharing and distributed capabilities to make the Philippines’ maritime approaches more transparent and its territorial defense more resilient,” said Brown. These drones are under a broader effort from the Pentagon to enhance Philippine maritime domain awareness following a renewed series of tensions over disputed territories in the South China Sea between Manila and Beijing. Since 2023, Chinese and Philippine forces have repeatedly clashed across several shoals and reefs claimed by the other. Manila’s nascent modernization efforts to contend with Chinese forces has seen increased American and Japanese backing . Florida-based sea drone manufacturer Maritime Tactical Systems, Inc. was tapped early on to provide the Philippine Navy’s first USVs. Currently, the core of the sea service’s USV Unit One is composed of one T38 Devil Ray and four MANTIS T12s. The Marine Corps USVs were transferred at MARTAC’s new Subic Bay facility. According to a company release, the drone center of excellence is designed to train Philippine drone operators and stock parts for the Devil Rays. “The CoE will also enable creation of local jobs and partnerships to build Philippines capabilities for deploying a large USV fleet over the next several years,” reads the MARTAC release. Over the summer, Mississippi-based Autonomous USV firm Ocean Aero, Inc. delivered four Triton drones to the Philippine Navy. The U.S.-Philippine initiative is currently focused on delivering maritime domain awareness capabilities to address significant gaps around the Southeast Asian archipelago of more than 7,600 islands. However, the program plans to integrate one-way attack drones and other lethal capabilities by 2027.

title: UPDATED: USS South Dakota Command Triad Relieved After October Grounding, Congressman Says
zh_title: 更新：国会议员称，十月搁浅后，南达科他州三合会指挥部被解职
summary: 2026 年 6 月 30 日，在康涅狄格州格罗顿的新伦敦海军潜艇基地，弗吉尼亚级核动力快速攻击潜艇南达科他号 (SSN-790) 指挥变更仪式上，鸣放 11 响礼炮，迎接第 2 潜艇大队指挥官梅尔文·史密斯少将的到来。丹尼尔·古德温接替了中校的职务。伯恩斯·C·W·布朗 (Burnes C.W. Brown) 担任南达科他州指挥官。美国海军照片 美国海军照片 南达科他号航空母舰 (SSN-790) 的指挥三合会上个月因搁浅事件而被拆除，根据一名国会议员的声明。潜艇的指挥官、执行官a
content:
2026 年 6 月 30 日，在康涅狄格州格罗顿的新伦敦海军潜艇基地，弗吉尼亚级核动力快速攻击潜艇南达科他号 (SSN-790) 指挥变更仪式上，鸣放 11 响礼炮，迎接第 2 潜艇大队指挥官梅尔文·史密斯少将的到来。丹尼尔·古德温接替了中校的职务。伯恩斯·C·W·布朗 (Burnes C.W. Brown) 担任南达科他州指挥官。美国海军照片 美国海军照片 南达科他号航空母舰 (SSN-790) 的指挥三合会上个月因搁浅事件而被拆除，根据一名国会议员的声明。根据众议院海上力量和投送部队小组委员会高级成员乔·考特尼（康涅狄格州民主党人）众议员和众议院军事委员会高级成员亚当·史密斯（华盛顿州民主党人）周四发布的一封信，该潜艇的指挥官、执行官和艇长于 10 月 14 日被解除指挥权，据称此次解除是由于搁浅事件。指挥官。据康涅狄格州新伦敦《每日报》报道，丹·古德温被解除南达科他州指挥官职务。根据五角大楼发布的消息，古德温于 2026 年 6 月接任南达科他州指挥官。一位知情人士告诉美国海军学院新闻，在潜艇舵软接地后，三合会被移除。信中称，议员们从一名记者要求就解雇事件发表评论的请求中得知，他们松了口气。
近一个月后，众议院军事委员会尚未收到任何有关解雇或潜在事件的通知。 2026 年 6 月 30 日在康涅狄格州格罗顿新伦敦海军潜艇基地的快速攻击潜艇码头上举行南达科他号 (SSN-790) 号航空母舰指挥变更仪式后，南达科他号 (SSN-790) 舰长丹尼尔·古德温被送上岸。信中写道：“海军部未能向国会通报这些事件是不可接受的。”致代理海军部长曹洪和海军作战部长达里尔·考德尔上将。海军通常会向国会通报海上事件、事故和指挥三合会的解散。 “海军缺乏透明度留下了许多悬而未决的问题，不仅涉及发生了什么，还涉及导致三合会解散的事件对南达科他州的结构健康、船员的福祉的影响，以及该事件是否暴露了必须解决的标准程序培训方面的任何系统性问题。由于海军未能沟通，本应成为信息共享标准的演习反而引发了人们对海军对透明度的承诺以及对与国会建立富有成效的工作关系的承诺的质疑。”这封信。一名国防官员向美国海军学院新闻证实了这一消息。
海军发言人承认了美国海军学院新闻的提问，但没有立即发表评论。 目前尚不清楚南达科他州是否受损。南达科他号于 2019 年服役，是海军最先进的潜艇之一，也是新型潜艇技术的试验台。美国海军学院新闻 2016 年报道称：“这艘船采用了使船舶更安静的涂层、更安静的喷水推进器以及安装在船体两侧的附加声纳，以提高船员探测敌方船只和潜艇的能力。”美国攻击潜艇上一次重大搁浅是在 2021 年。在南海执行任务时，美国海军康涅狄格号 (SSN-21) 与一艘水下潜艇相撞。

【原文 English Original】
11-gun salutes are fired for the arrival of Rear Adm. Melvin Smith, Commander, Submarine Group 2, during the Virginia-class nuclear-powered fast attack submarine USS South Dakota (SSN-790) Change of Command Ceremony at Naval Submarine Base New London in Groton, Connecticut, June 30, 2026. Cmdr. Daniel Goodwin relieved Cmdr. Burnes C.W. Brown as Commanding Officer of South Dakota. US Navy photo USS South Dakota (SSN-790) command triad was removed last month following a grounding incident, according to a statement from a member of Congress. The submarine’s commanding officer, executive officer and chief of the boat were relieved from command on Oct. 14, with the relief allegedly attributed to a grounding incident, according to a letter released Thursday by Reps. Joe Courtney (D-Conn.), Ranking Member of the House Seapower and Projection Forces Subcommittee, and Adam Smith (D-Wash.), Ranking Member of the House Armed Services Committee. Cmdr. Dan Goodwin was relieved as commander of South Dakota , according to a story in the Day newspaper based in New London, Conn. Goodwin assumed command of South Dakota in June of 2026, according to a Pentagon release . A source familiar told USNI News the triad removal followed a soft grounding of the submarine’s rudder. Lawmakers learned of the relief from a reporter’s request for comment on the dismissal, according to the letter. Nearly one month later, no notifications of the firings or the underlying incident had been made to the House Armed Services Committee. Cmdr. Daniel Goodwin, commanding officer of USS South Dakota (SSN-790) is piped ashore following the USS South Dakota (SSN-790) change of command ceremony that was held June 30, 2026, onboard the fast attack submarine pierside at Naval Submarine Base New London in Groton, Conn. US Navy photo “The Department of the Navy’s failure to communicate these incidents to Congress is unacceptable,” reads the letter, which is addressed to Acting Secretary of the Navy Hung Cao and Chief of Naval Operations Adm. Daryl Caudle. The Navy typically informs Congress of at-sea incidents, accidents and dismissals of command triads. “The Navy’s lack of transparency leave many outstanding questions about not only what occurred, but the impact of the events leading the triad’s dismissal on the structural health of South Dakota , the well-being of the crew, and whether the incident laid bare any systemic issues with training to standard procedures that must be addressed. As a result of the Navy’s failure to communicate, what should have been a standard exercise in information sharing has instead raised questions about the Navy’s commitment to transparency and its commitment to a productive working relationship with Congress,” reads the letter. A defense official confirmed the removals to USNI News. A Navy spokesperson acknowledged a question from USNI News but did not immediately provide a comment. It’s unclear whether South Dakota was damaged. Commissioned in 2019, South Dakota is one of the Navy’s most advanced submarines and serves as the test bed for new submarine technology. “The boat received coatings that keep the ship quieter, a quieter water jet propulsor and additional sonars mounted on the sides of the hull to increase the crew’s ability to detect enemy ships and submarines,” USNI News reported in 2016 . The last major grounding of a U.S. attack submarine was in 2021. While operating in the South China Sea, USS Connecticut (SSN-21) collided with an underwater sea mount, resulting in extensive damage to the boat. The submarine is still undergoing repairs.

title: Russia’s Push for AI Sovereignty Faces Setbacks
zh_title: 俄罗斯推动人工智能主权面临挫折
summary: 内容摘要：10 月份乌克兰无人机袭击俄罗斯，损坏了 Yandex、VK、Sberbank 和俄罗斯联邦税务局运营的数据中心，扰乱了数字服务，并引发了将基础设施从莫斯科地区搬迁到远东的讨论。随着人们越来越担心俄罗斯系统落后于美国和中国模式，莫斯科正在着手正式确定其人工智能（AI）政策。新的人工智能立法于 9 月生效。俄罗斯官员将国内人工智能视为国家主权问题，但计算基础设施和滑雪设备短缺
content:
内容摘要：10 月份乌克兰无人机袭击俄罗斯，损坏了 Yandex、VK、Sberbank 和俄罗斯联邦税务局运营的数据中心，扰乱了数字服务，并引发了将基础设施从莫斯科地区搬迁到远东的讨论。随着人们越来越担心俄罗斯系统落后于美国和中国模式，莫斯科正在着手正式确定其人工智能（AI）政策。新的人工智能立法于 9 月生效。俄罗斯官员将国内人工智能视为国家主权问题，但计算基础设施和技术人员的短缺，以及外国人工智能模型的日益使用，威胁着莫斯科发展有竞争力的国内行业的努力。 10 月 8 日，乌克兰无人机袭击了俄罗斯最大科技公司 Yandex 旗下的大型数据中心之一，导致该公司在全国各地的服务大规模中断。罢工使该公司的云服务进入紧急模式，客户不得不将数据转移到其他云系统（Habr，10 月 12 日）。 Yandex 数字生态系统内的其他服务需要数周时间才能恢复（T-J，10 月 26 日）。
VK Company Limited 是另一家控制着领先的俄语社交媒体网站 VKontakte 和 Odnoklassniki、国家消息系统 Max 以及俄罗斯领先的电子邮件服务 Mail.ru 的大型科技公司，最近其数据中心也遭受了损害，俄罗斯最大的金融机构 Sberbank 也是如此（CNews，10 月 18 日）。这些攻击只是克里姆林宫在继续推动完全数字主权时面临的众多困难之一。这些 10 月份的攻击符合乌克兰无人机针对俄罗斯数据中心的更广泛模式，包括那些属于联邦组织的数据中心，例如下诺夫哥罗德的国家税务局（Nastoyashee Vremya，10 月 23 日）。 Ozon 是一家电子商务公司，被认为是俄罗斯的亚马逊，自 8 月以来一直面临着针对其仓库的无人机袭击（Omskinform，10 月 28 日）。这些攻击对俄罗斯发展安全和主权科技行业的努力产生了严重后果。俄罗斯科技行业正在呼吁加强安全性，一些人正在讨论将数据中心迁往远东的可能性，因为目前 75% 的商业数据中心位于莫斯科州（Techora，10 月 27 日）。技术媒体讨论的其他选择包括将数据中心移至哈萨克斯坦。 Yandex 尚未面临西方的全面制裁，使其有可能将基础设施转移到国外（Habr，10 月 12 日）。
对俄罗斯科技行业的物理攻击正值克里姆林宫越来越担心该国人工智能（AI）的未来。俄罗斯杜马成立了一个委员会来解决人工智能问题，由执政的统一俄罗斯党副秘书长、俄罗斯“外国代理人”法的发起人之一亚历山大·西迪亚金（Aleksandr Sidyakin）领导，该法名义上旨在减少外国在该国的影响力，并压制独立媒体、非政府组织和非系统性政治反对派（Meduza， 9 月 24 日）。俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京表示，俄罗斯的主权将取决于该国开发自己的国内人工智能的能力（RBC，4 月 10 日）。人工智能在俄罗斯对乌克兰战争中的快速发展彻底改变了战场，减少了

【原文 English Original】
Executive Summary: Ukrainian drone strikes on Russia in October damaged data centers operated by Yandex, VK, Sberbank, and Russia’s Federal Tax Service, disrupting digital services and prompting discussion of relocating infrastructure from the Moscow region to the Far East. Moscow is moving to formalize its artificial intelligence (AI) policy as concerns grow that Russian systems are falling behind U.S. and Chinese models. New AI legislation entered into force in September. Russian officials view domestic AI as a matter of national sovereignty, but shortages of computing infrastructure and skilled personnel, alongside growing use of foreign AI models, threaten Moscow’s efforts to develop a competitive domestic sector. Ukrainian drone strikes on October 8 struck one of the large data centers belonging to Yandex, Russia’s largest tech company, leading to massive interruptions in the company’s services around the country. The strikes pushed the company’s cloud services into emergency mode, and clients had to move their data to other cloud systems ( Habr , October 12). Other services within the Yandex digital ecosystem required weeks to recover ( T-J , October 26). VK Company Limited—another major tech company which controls the leading Russian-language social media sites VKontakte and Odnoklassniki, the national messaging system Max, and Mail.ru, Russia’s leading e-mail service—also recently faced damage to its data centers, as did Sberbank, Russia’s largest financial institution ( CNews , October 18). These attacks underscore just one of the many difficulties facing the Kremlin as it continues to push for complete digital sovereignty. These October attacks fit into a broader pattern of Ukrainian drone strikes against Russian data centers, including those belonging to federal organizations, such as the National Tax Service in Nizhnyi Novgorod ( Nastoyashee Vremya , October 23). Ozon, an e-commerce company that is considered Russia’s answer to Amazon, has faced continued drone attacks targeting their warehouses since August ( Omskinform , October 28).  The attacks have had serious consequences for Russia’s attempts to develop a secure and sovereign tech sector. The Russian technology industry is calling for additional security, and some are discussing potentially relocating data centers to the Far East, as 75 percent of commercial data centers are currently located in Moscow oblast ( Techora , October 27). Other options discussed in the technology press include moving data centers to Kazakhstan. Yandex has not faced comprehensive Western sanctions, enabling it to potentially move infrastructure abroad ( Habr , October 12). The physical attacks on Russia’s technology sector come as the Kremlin becomes more concerned about the future of artificial intelligence (AI) in the country. The Russian Duma formed a committee to address AI issues, headed by Aleksandr Sidyakin, deputy secretary general of the ruling United Russia party and one of the initiators of Russia’s “foreign agents” law, which nominally aimed to reduce foreign influence in the country and suppressed independent media, non-governmental organizations, and non-systemic political opposition ( Meduza , September 24). Russian President Vladimir Putin has said that Russia’s sovereignty will depend on the country’s ability to develop its own domestic AI ( RBC , April 10). The rapid development of AI use in Russia’s war against Ukraine has completely altered the battlefield, reducing the applicability of lessons from previous wars, according to Russian Deputy Defense Minister General Yunus-Bek Evkurov in an August interview ( RBC , August 10). The first legislation specifying Kremlin policies for the development of domestic models entered into effect in September, though some provisions will not take effect until March 2027. “Sovereign” AI models must use only domestic technologies under the law, while “national” models can use foreign components and open-source solutions ( RBC , August 31). “Sovereign” models, according to Sidyakin, must “conform to Russian spiritual and moral values” ( RIA Novosti , October 27). Moscow is concerned that Russian AI is falling behind models from the United States and the People’s Republic of China (PRC). Sberbank President German Gref estimated that Russian AI was a half-year behind Beijing’s systems and expressed fears that this lag will continue ( RBC , September 24). This announcement followed news that PRC models were the second and third most popular models among Russian clients using domestic cloud platforms, with the use of PRC AI growing elevenfold year-on-year ( Kommersant , August 13). Surveys published in the summer found that respondents from 79 percent of 100 major Russian companies reported too few AI specialists and 91 percent lacked sufficient server infrastructure ( ITZine , July 29).  These concerns about AI development are compounded by evidence of brain drain. Arkadii Volozh, the original founder of Yandex, immigrated to the Netherlands in 2024 after criticizing Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine, taking 1,000 engineers with him, along with plans to develop a company specializing in infrastructure for AI systems. His assets were then sold to Russian investors for $5.4 billion ( IncRussia , July 16). The Kremlin is subsidizing the development of domestic AI by offering tax breaks to small and medium enterprises that adopt domestic solutions, but the country will need 89,000 AI specialists by 2030, according to estimates presented at a tech conference by former Russian Deputy Prime Minister Dmitrii Gorgenko ( Vedomosti , September 21; Ekspert , October 24). The new AI legislation is part of a broader shift toward Russian digital sovereignty. This push includes a “sovereign” internet and national network defense system (see EDM , May 20). Russia faces serious challenges, including developing national AI systems that can compete with U.S. and PRC versions while protecting its technology infrastructure from Ukrainian strikes. Further attacks leading to extended online interruptions would likely undermine support for the war effort and disrupt Russia’s digital economy. A major relocation of technology infrastructure to the Far East would likely require heavy state support and the development of an ecosystem to support the data centers, both serious undertakings for an economy that is facing stagnation (see EDM , November 2).  The post Russia’s Push for AI Sovereignty Faces Setbacks appeared first on Jamestown .

content:
巴黎——一家英国公司藏在法国郊区会议中心的一个黑暗角落里，掌握着美国最新战舰的下一个设计方案。上周，2026 年欧洲海军陆战队巴布科克国际展台上的展示台上展示了​​ 31 型“箭头”号的模型。这是白宫设计的美国海军外国护卫舰竞赛的六个竞争者之一，目的是在美国掀起新一轮造船和投资浪潮。随着特朗普政府不断追求外国军舰设计和造船，在两年一度的会议上，几家欧洲防务公司急于讨论如果美国来敲门，他们可以在潜在的国际竞争中提出的选择。美国海军目前正在建造两艘护卫舰设计。一年前前海军部长约翰·费兰取消了该计划后，芬坎蒂尼马里内特海军陆战队仍在威斯康星州造船厂建造前两艘星座级护卫舰。与此同时，HII 的英格尔斯造船公司签订了一份长期合同，用于启动基于美国海岸警卫队国家安全巡逻舰的 FF(X) 护卫舰。据美国海军学院新闻了解，虽然美国海军几十年来一直未能成功推出护卫舰项目，但美国海军正在努力在未来几年内将外国设计用于新型舰艇。哈德逊研究所海军分析师布莱恩·克拉克表示，新护卫舰的工作要求已基本完成。
现在，海军优先考虑的是能够护航其他船只的护卫舰，而不是执行反潜战，这是现已取消的星座级计划的主要任务。克拉克表示，海军需要一个能够实施封锁并防御中层威胁的平台，就像美国中央司令部目前面临的中等威胁。 “一艘护卫舰可以防御我们所看到的来自伊朗的那种规模的威胁，”克拉克在欧洲海军之前告诉美国海军学院新闻。 “并不是真正的[反潜战]——更多的是执行这种海上控制、海上安全类型的任务。”为此，来自全球各地的六种设计已成为国际竞赛的潜在候选者，该竞赛将遵循唐纳德·特朗普总统在八月份的造船备忘录中所呼吁的设计。白宫文件呼吁海军推行所谓的“芬兰模式”，即在外国投资美国造船基础设施之前，可以在外国造船厂开始建造最多前两艘船体。白宫正在利用芬兰模式，在芬兰、德克萨斯州和路易斯安那州的造船厂建造两个独立的设计，以启动北极安全巡逻艇计划。白宫管理和预算办公室主任拉斯·沃特一直直言不讳地主张对小型水面作战舰艇和辅助舰艇使用相同的模型。
但国会抵制了这一努力，在众议院和参议院版本的《2027 财年国防授权法案》中都加入了草案，该法案将阻止海军购买外国建造的军舰。国会对购买海外辅助舰艇持更开放的态度。尽管遭到国会的抵制，八月的一份备忘录还是勾勒出了这场竞赛的蓝图——由国防部长皮特·赫格斯和代理海军部长曹洪制定。该计划将于周四向白宫提交。竞争者 Type 31 Babcock 图片 自 2023 年以来，Babcock 一直与美国领先者保持合作关系

【原文 English Original】
PARIS — Tucked in a dark corner of a convention center in the French suburbs, a British company could hold the next design for America’s newest warship. A model of the Type-31 Arrowhead sailed on a display table at the Babcock International booth at Euronaval 2026 last week. It was one of a half a dozen contenders for the U.S. Navy’s foreign frigate competition designed by the White House to jumpstart a new wave of shipbuilding and investment in the U.S. With the Trump administration’s ongoing pursuit of foreign warship design and shipbuilding, several European defense companies at the biennial conference were eager to discuss the options they could propose in a potential international competition should the U.S. come knocking at their doors. The U.S. Navy currently has two frigate designs under construction in the U.S. Fincantieri Marinette Marine is still building the first two Constellation-class frigates at its Wisconsin yard after former Navy Secretary John Phelan canceled the program one year ago . Meanwhile, HII’s Ingalls Shipbuilding has a long lead-time contract to start the FF(X) frigate that is based on the U.S. Coast Guard’s National Security Cutter. While a successful frigate program has eluded the U.S. Navy for decades, the service is working toward using a foreign design for a new class of ships in the next few years, USNI News understands. The working requirements for a new frigate are mostly done, according to Hudson Institute naval analyst Bryan Clark. Now the Navy is prioritizing frigates that can escort other ships instead of performing anti-submarine warfare, which was the main mission of the now-cancelled Constellation-class program. The service wants a platform that can enforce a blockade and protect against medium tiered threats like what the military is currently facing in U.S. Central Command, according to Clark. “A frigate could defend against the kind of scale of threat that we’re seeing from the Iranians,” Clark told USNI News ahead of Euronaval. “Not really [anti-submarine warfare] – more about doing this kind of sea control, maritime security type mission.” To that end, six designs from around the globe have emerged as potential candidates in an international competition that would adhere to the one President Donald Trump called for in an August shipbuilding memo. The White House document called on the Navy to pursue the so-called “Finland model,” in which construction could begin in a foreign shipyard for up to the first two hulls before a foreign investment in U.S. shipbuilding infrastructure. The White House is using the Finland model to jumpstart the Arctic Security Cutter program by building two separate designs in shipyards in Finland, Texas and Louisiana. White House Office of Management and Budget Director Russ Vought has been vocal about using the same model for small surface combatants and auxiliaries. But Congress has resisted the effort by including draft language in both the House and Senate versions of the Fiscal Year 2027 National Defense Authorization Act that would prevent the Navy from buying foreign-built warships. Congress is more open to buying auxiliaries overseas. Despite congressional resistance, an August memo outlined a blueprint for that competition – crafted by Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth and Acting Navy Secretary Hung Cao. The plan was due to the White House on Thursday. The Contenders Type 31 Babcock image Since 2023, Babcock has maintained a partnership with lead American shipbuilder HII as part of the AUKUS security pact. The British company also works with HII on the unmanned surface vessel Romulus, which the U.K.’s Royal Navy is purchasing. Sir Nick Hine, the chief executive of Babcock’s marine division, said he thinks the Type 31 frigate could fill the U.S. Navy’s need for a small surface combatant. That platform should be able to “perform anti‑submarine warfare, surface warfare and convoy escort duties,” according to the White House memo. The Type 31 frigate could function as a command vessel in a fleet that includes a mix of manned and unmanned ships, according to Hine. Babcock has already worked with Lockheed Martin, meaning the platform could integrate the AEGIS Combat System and the AN/SPY-7 radar. The design also features a Mark 41 launcher with 32 Vertical Launching System cells, but Hine says it could potentially take additional cells. “Navies are short of two things always, even yours, short of money and people,” Hine, making the case for the Type 31, told USNI News on the sidelines of Euronaval last week. “You need a cheaper frigate because the cost of some of these platforms is insane, and you need a platform that’s got less people in it because you don’t have enough people. The Type 31 was designed to be more adaptable, more affordable, more available, and it was designed to have less people in it,” he added. “It was designed for a crew of a complement of 100, not to exceed 100. It’s 6,000 tons, 140 meters in length, and therefore it was designed for North Atlantic operations, so it’s designed to operate in high sea states for long periods of time.” To field the platform in the U.S. fleet faster, the hull could be built abroad to the point where it’s ready to sail away while the combat system is integrated back in the U.S., Hine said. Another option is out of Spain’s Navantia, which is working on an export version of its Bonifaz-class F-110 anti-submarine warfare frigate. Navantia, which is partnered with Lockheed Martin for the F-110, plans to submit a bid should the U.S. Navy issue a request for proposals, Navantia commercial director Juan de la Cueva told USNI News during a wine and tapas-fueled reception on the convention center floor. F-110 frigate. Navantia image “All Navantia ships have a U.S. legacy because we came from a very long-standing relationship with the United States,” de la Cueva said. “We learned from Bath Iron Works, Gibbs & Cox how to build ships. So these ships pass … [Naval Sea Systems Command]” standards. De la Cueva noted the long relationship Navantia has maintained with major U.S. yards like General Dynamics Bath Iron Works and HII. The company has already provided the U.S. Navy with some information and is waiting to hear about the next steps in the competition. A U.S. variant could feature Lockheed Martin’s Aegis Combat System and the SPY-7 air and defense radar, de la Cueva said. In addition to the Brits and the Spanish, the Italians also have an option for the U.S. should it kick off an international competition. Italy’s Fincantieri, which has its own American subsidiary at Marinette Marine in Wisconsin, could propose the FREMM EVO. That platform is an updated version of the FREMM multi-mission frigate that the U.S. used as the parent design for the Constellation class. “I would call us untapped potential,” Fincantieri Marinette Marine chief executive officer George Moutafis told USNI News in September. The yard is still finishing the Royal Saudi Navy’s multi-mission surface combatant while building the first two Constellation-class frigates and preparing to build the Marine Corps’ Landing Ship Medium. “It’s an evolution of the original version, which is meant to say all the benefits are still there,” Moutafis said of the FREMM EVO. “The hard lines that work well for an [anti-submarine warfare] mission all is there, and they’ve been working on the areas that you would think would be the attractive ones – you know making it more lethal, making it ready to host energy-wise future growth for future missions, bringing in capabilities that have to do again with the ASW mission – and at the same time identifying the ways that it can integrate well with deploying, recovering and managing unmanned elements of across all domains.” The Wisconsin yard currently has about 2,200 employees and would need to hire about 500 over time should it receive a contract to build more frigates. Other possible designs could come out of Japan, South Korea and Turkey, USNI News previously reported . Following a discussion between Trump and Turkish leadership on the sidelines of July’s NATO summit, the Istanbul-class guided-missile frigate built by several Turkish shipyards entered the mix, two sources previously told USNI News. Fincantieri image Perhaps the nation most closely associated with the ongoing conversation about foreign shipbuilding is South Korea, which has pledged to invest $150 billion in the U.S. shipbuilding industry as part of a trade deal in the works with the Trump administration. The Chungnam-class guided-missile frigate, which several South Korean companies build, is one option under consideration, USNI News has learned. Meanwhile, the export version of Japan’s Mitsubishi Heavy Industries’ FFM Mogami-class guided-missile frigate is also on the table. While the Trump administration has repeatedly made its preference for an international competition known, the Navy has experienced setbacks when pursuing foreign designs. When altering the FREMM parent design for the Constellation-class program, Gibbs & Cox made so many changes to meet NAVSEA’s requirements that the commonality between the FREMM and the FFG(X) went from 85 percent to under 15 percent, USNI News reported in 2024 . “The thing that will prevent Constellation 2.0 is stop changing the requirement. If you set the requirement and leave it alone, and just let industry build it, whoever that is, that will stop Constellation 2.0,” Babcock’s Hine told USNI News. “Don’t even change the color of the curtains. Just build it,” he added. “It’s this sort of constant fiddling, and I know from being in the [U.K. Royal] Navy for most of my life, that we can’t help ourselves.”

content:
以下是上周西太平洋主要舰船活动和演习的摘要。 2026 年 11 月 9 日，新加坡，一名隶属于第 137 电子攻击中队 (VAQ) 的美国水手在尼米兹级航空母舰西奥多·罗斯福号 (CVN-71) 机库湾对 E/A-18G 咆哮者进行维护。美国海军照片 西奥多·罗斯福号航母打击群于周日从新加坡出发。该打击群包括西奥多·罗斯福号航空母舰（CVN-71）及其第11舰载机联队（CVW）、长津号巡洋舰（CG-65）以及保罗·汉密尔顿号驱逐舰（DDG-60）和迪凯特号（DDG-73）。西奥多·罗斯福、长津和迪凯特向西航行进入马六甲海峡，而保罗·汉密尔顿则向东航行进入南中国海。西奥多·罗斯福号、长津号和迪凯特号目前正在印度洋前往美国中央司令部。日本横须贺附近 印度海军 Shivalik 级隐形多用途护卫舰 INS Sahyadri (F 49)、日本海上自卫队日向级直升机驱逐舰 JS Ise (DDH 182)、最上级护卫舰 JS Mogami (FFM 1)、澳大利亚皇家海军安扎克级护卫舰 HMAS Stuart (FFH 153) 和美国海军 San 2026 年 11 月 7 日，安东尼奥级两栖运输船坞运输舰安克雷奇号 (LPD-23) 和约翰·穆萨号 (LPD-26) 在 2026 年马拉巴尔演习期间在西太平洋编队航行。美国海军照片 2026 年马拉巴尔四方演习于周四在日本横须贺附近海域结束。
参与的资产包括日本海上自卫队直升机驱逐舰 JS Ise (DDH-182)、护卫舰 JS Mogami (FFM-1)、日本海上自卫队潜艇和 P-1 海上巡逻机 (MPA)、印度海军护卫舰 INS Sahyadri (F49)、澳大利亚皇家海军护卫舰 HMAS Stuart (FFH153) 和澳大利亚皇家空军 P-8A Poseidon MPA、美国海军 P-8A 海神 MPA 和两栖运输船坞 USS Anchorage (LPD-23) 和 USS John P. Murtha (LPD-26)。安克雷奇号和约翰·P·穆萨号与两栖攻击舰马金岛号 (LHD-8) 以及已登船的第 13 海军陆战队远征部队组成了马金岛两栖待命大队。据当地船舶观察员称，这三艘船均于周六从横须贺舰队活动司令部（CFAY）出发。 2026 年 11 月 8 日，在日本横须贺，美国海军陆战队海军陆战队海军陆战队中型倾转旋翼机中队 (VMM) 364（加强型）的飞行员从圣安东尼奥级两栖运输船坞舰安克雷奇 (LPD-23) 的飞行甲板上驾驶一架 MV-22B 鱼鹰。美国海军照片安克雷奇于周五返回横须贺，目前停泊据当地船舶观察员称，那里近海。据当地船舶观察员称，澳大利亚皇家海军斯图尔特号护卫舰在参加 2026 年马拉巴尔演习后于周四返回横须贺。据当地船舶观察员称，印度海军护卫舰 INS Sahyadri 于周四返回横须贺，并于周五离开。
据当地船舶观测员称，潜艇补给船弗兰克·凯布尔号 (AS-40) 于周三驶入横须贺指挥官舰队活动基地。在西太平洋，隶属于海军陆战队中型倾转旋翼机中队 (VMM) 364 的美国海军陆战队 CH-53 种马准备从圣安东尼奥级两栖运输船坞舰约翰·P·穆萨号 (LPD-26) 的飞行甲板起飞， 2026 年 11 月 9 日。美国海军照片 两栖攻击舰马金岛号和两栖运输船坞约翰·P·穆萨号正在美国第七舰队作战区域航行。在菲律宾海 台湾民族党秘书长吴钊燮于 2026 年 11 月 12 日发布的图片

State media Korea Central News Agency photo North Korea leader Kim Jong Un inspected the construction site of a new naval base on Wednesday in Thongchon County, Kangwon Province, located on North Korea’s east coast, state media Korean Central News Agency reported. In Maizuru, Japan Royal Navy offshore patrol vessel HMS Spey (P234) departed JMSDF Maizuru Naval Base on Nov. 10, 2026. zh_title: 日本承诺在菲律宾最新的国防计划中提供无人机和海防雷达
summary: BRP Jose Rizal 与两艘日本海上自卫队舰艇进行演习。菲律宾海军照片 日本将在东京最新的防御计划中向菲律宾军方转让无人机和海岸防御雷达系统，以增强马尼拉的军队。日本驻菲律宾大使北川胜郎和菲律宾外交部长特蕾莎·拉扎罗周一签署了一项协议，涵盖通过官方安全援助计划提供价值高达 2700 万美元的防务转移。此次援助标志着首次通过
content:
BRP Jose Rizal 与两艘日本海上自卫队舰艇进行演习。菲律宾海军照片 日本将在东京最新的防御计划中向菲律宾军方转让无人机和海岸防御雷达系统，以增强马尼拉的军队。日本驻菲律宾大使北川胜郎和菲律宾外交部长特蕾莎·拉扎罗周一签署了一项协议，涵盖通过官方安全援助计划提供价值高达 2700 万美元的防务转移。据日本外务省周一发布的新闻稿称，此次援助标志着首次通过专用海岸雷达系统向菲律宾转移国防设备。该雷达将由菲律宾海军操作，菲律宾海军是日本类似监视系统的先前接收者。上个月在马尼拉举行的日本自卫队成立 72 周年招待会上，日本公司展示了各种打算出售或转让给菲律宾军方的海岸监视系统。这些雷达包括能够跟踪 24 海里外船只的短程系统，以及能够感知 140 海里外海上目标的功能更强大的多用途雷达。除了海域意识援助外，菲律宾空军还将接收型号和数量不详的无人机。 2025年夏天，东京通过OSA向马来西亚转让了14架Aerobo Wing AS-VT02A无人机，价值高达270万美元。
此次移交是马尼拉和东京之间的首次无人移交。此前，日本将TC-90涡轮螺旋桨飞机移交给菲律宾海军航空联队用于海上巡逻。日本大使馆的新闻稿称：“该项目对于进一步促进日本和菲律宾之间的安全合作、加强日本重要海上通道的安全以及维护和加强地区和平与稳定具有重要意义。”近年来，由于对南海和吕宋海峡的共同担忧，东京与马尼拉寻求更密切的防务关系。自 2010 年代以来一些最重要的进展包括承诺为菲律宾海岸警卫队提供 17 艘巡逻舰，以及日本自卫队作战部队抵达东南亚群岛进行演习。今年，日本军队与美国、菲律宾和加拿大军队一起演习，保卫吕宋岛北部的海滩。东京首次全面实战演习以在击沉演习中发射反舰导弹而达到高潮。新的国防装备转让指南也为前日本自卫队装备出售或转让给菲律宾军方开辟了新的机会。目前正在讨论将即将退役的阿巴库巴级护卫舰转移给菲律宾海军。

【原文 English Original】
BRP Jose Rizal conducts exercises with two Japan Maritime Self-Defense ships. Philippine Navy photo Japan will transfer unmanned aerial vehicles and a coastal defense radar system to the Philippine military in Tokyo’s latest defense package to bolster Manila’s forces. Japanese Ambassador to the Philippines Katsuro Kitagawa and Philippine Secretary of Foreign Affairs Theresa Lazaro signed an agreement on Monday covering the defense transfer worth up to $27 million via the Official Security Assistance program. The assistance marks the first transfer of defense equipment to the Philippines via a dedicated coastal radar system, as classified by a Japanese Ministry of Foreign Affairs news release published on Monday. This radar will be operated by the Philippine Navy, which has been the previous recipient of similar surveillance systems from Japan. At the 72nd Japan Self-Defense Force anniversary reception in Manila last month, Japanese firms showcased a variety of coastal watch systems intended for sale or transfer to the Philippine military. These ranged from short-range systems capable of tracking vessels out to 24 nautical miles to more capable multirole radars that can sense maritime targets 140 nautical miles away. Alongside the maritime domain awareness assistance, the Philippine Air Force will receive an unspecified variant and quantity of UAVs. In the summer of 2025, Tokyo transferred 14 Aerobo Wing AS-VT02A UAVs worth up to $2.7 million to Malaysia through OSA. The latest transfer is the first instance of unmanned transfers between Manila and Tokyo. Previously, Japan handed over TC-90 turboprops to the Philippine Naval Air Wing for maritime patrols. “This project is of great importance in further promoting security cooperation between Japan and the Philippines, enhancing security of important sea lanes for Japan, and contributing to maintaining and strengthening regional peace and stability,” reads the Japanese Embassy release. In recent years, Tokyo has pursued closer defense relations with Manila amid mutual concerns over the South China Sea and Luzon Strait. Some of the most significant developments since the 2010s include the commitment of 17 patrol ships for the Philippine Coast Guard and the arrival of Japan Self-Defense Force combat troops for drills across the Southeast Asian archipelago. This year, Japanese troops drilled alongside American, Philippine and Canadian forces to defend a beach in Northern Luzon. Tokyo’s full-scale combat exercise debut culminated with the launch of anti-ship missiles at a sinking exercise. New defense equipment transfer guidelines are also opening up new opportunities for ex-JSDF equipment to be sold or transferred to the Philippine military. Discussions are ongoing to transfer soon-to-be retired Abakumba-class destroyer escorts to the Philippine Navy.

summary: 发言人办公室关于七国集团外长巴黎会议的联合声明 媒体报道 2026年11月13日，加拿大、法国、德国、意大利、日本、英国、美国等七国集团外长和欧盟高级代表发表以下声明。文本开头：2026 年 11 月 9 日至 10 日在巴黎举行的七国集团外长会议后的联合声明 我们，代表加拿大、法国、德国、意大利、日本、英国和美利坚合众国的七国集团外长，以及
content:
发言人办公室关于七国集团外长巴黎会议的联合声明 媒体报道 2026年11月13日，加拿大、法国、德国、意大利、日本、英国、美国等七国集团外长和欧盟高级代表发表以下声明。正文：2026 年 11 月 9 日至 10 日巴黎七国集团外长会议后的联合声明 我们，代表加拿大、法国、德国、意大利、日本、英国和美利坚合众国的七国集团外长，以及欧盟高级代表，于 2026 年 11 月 9 日至 10 日在巴黎举行的 2026 年七国集团主席国法国会议上举行会议。 乌克兰 我们重申对乌克兰及其勇敢人民的坚定支持他们捍卫自己的领土完整、主权、自由和独立。我们完全声援乌克兰人民，他们每天都遭受俄罗斯袭击，影响住宅楼、民用基础设施和文化遗产，以及针对乌克兰和其他伙伴的恶意混合活动。我们谴责黑海地区针对民用航运的袭击行动，这对全球粮食安全产生了重大影响，并加强了我们对保障粮食供应链的承诺。我们重申支持美国领导的通过直接和认真的谈判促进和平的持续努力。
我们重申了确保全面、全面和互惠停火的重要性。相互停止对所有能源基础设施和黑海的攻击，以保护平民，减少对能源（包括供暖、水和卫生设施以及粮食供应）的干扰，并支持全球市场的更大稳定，这是实现公正和持久和平的重要第一步。我们重申，有关欧洲未来安全的谈判必须包括欧洲人。正如我们在埃维昂七国集团峰会上所承诺的那样，我们评估了向乌克兰提供防空能力、系统和拦截器、远程能力和许可证方面取得的进展，这些能力将使其能够增加军事生产并行使其固有的自卫权。我们仍然致力于继续并加强朝这个方向的努力。我们承认需要以协调一致的方式解决乌克兰 2027 年及以后紧迫的融资需求，以支持乌克兰。我们谴责朝鲜和伊朗向俄罗斯提供军事援助，以及中国提供武器、军事训练和军民两用部件，这使得战争得以继续。我们明确表示打算继续对这些国家采取行动。基于我们领导人在埃维昂达成的共识，我们讨论了对俄罗斯战时经济日益增加的压力，包括通过制裁。
我们重申两国领导人承诺在针对俄罗斯的制裁问题上密切协调。我们重申决心重点关注悬挂假旗的船只或无国籍船只，以及保险公司、石油贸易商和中介机构等结构性推动者，以进一步扰乱和威慑用于规避制裁的影子舰队。我们重申支持乌克兰能源安全和恢复力，决定加大资金和物资支持力度，帮助乌克兰度过冬季。我们欢迎为使切尔诺贝利新安全隔离设施的修复保持在国际议程上的高度重视而做出的努力

【原文 English Original】
Office of the Spokesman Joint Statement on the G7 Foreign Ministers Meeting in Paris Media Note November 13, 2026 The following statement was released by the G7 Foreign Ministers of Canada, France, Germany, Italy, Japan, the United Kingdom, the United States of America and the High Representative of the European Union. Begin Text: Joint declaration following the G7 Foreign Ministers Meeting in Paris on 9 and 10 November 2026 We, the G7 Foreign Ministers representing Canada, France, Germany, Italy, Japan, the United Kingdom and the United States of America, along with the High Representative of the European Union, met under the 2026 French G7 Presidency in Paris, on 9 and 10 November 2026. Ukraine We reaffirmed our unwavering support to Ukraine and its courageous people as they defend their territorial integrity, sovereignty, freedom, and independence. We stand in full solidarity with the Ukrainian population suffering from daily Russian attacks affecting residential buildings, civilian infrastructure, and cultural heritage, as well as malicious hybrid activities against Ukraine and other partners. We condemned the campaign of strikes carried out against civilian shipping in the Black Sea area, which have significant consequences on global food security, and strengthened our commitment to safeguarding food supply chains. We reiterated our support to ongoing U.S.-led efforts to facilitate peace through direct and serious negotiations. We reaffirmed the importance of securing a full, comprehensive, and reciprocal ceasefire. A reciprocal halt to attacks on all energy infrastructure and in the Black Sea to protect civilians, reduce disruption to energy, including heating, water and sanitation, and food supply and support greater stability in global markets is an important first step towards just and lasting peace. We reiterated that negotiations on the future security of Europe must include the Europeans. As we pledged during the G7 Summit in Évian, we took stock of progress on supplying Ukraine with air defense capabilities, systems and interceptors, long-range capabilities and licenses that will allow it to increase its military production and to exercise its inherent right of self-defense. We remain committed to continuing and strengthening our efforts in this direction. We acknowledged the need to address Ukraine’s pressing financing needs for 2027 and beyond in a coordinated way to support Ukraine. We condemned the provision of military assistance to Russia by North Korea and Iran, and the provision of weapons, military training and dual-use components by China, which enables the continuation of the war. We made clear our intention to continue to take action against these countries. Building on the consensus among our leaders in Évian, we discussed increasing pressure on Russia’s war economy, including through sanctions. We reaffirmed the commitment of our leaders to closely coordinate on sanctions against Russia. We reiterated our determination to focus on ships flying false flags or stateless ships, as well as structural enablers, such as insurers, oil traders, and intermediaries, to further disrupt and deter shadow fleet vessels used to circumvent sanctions. We reaffirmed our support to Ukraine’s energy security and resilience, and decided to step up our financial and material support to help the country get through the winter. We welcomed efforts to keep the repair of the Chornobyl New Safe Confinement high on the international agenda, as demonstrated by the donors’ conference organized in Paris on 9 November by France, EBRD, and Ukraine. We also welcomed the ongoing projects coordinated through the Tallinn Mechanism under Italy’s Chairpersonship to support Ukraine’s civilian cyber resilience. Middle East On Iran, we commended the work of the regional mediators and reiterated our support for all diplomatic efforts aimed at reaching a lasting settlement that addresses international concerns over Iran’s nuclear program and contributes to regional security. We reiterated that Iran must never be allowed to develop or acquire a nuclear weapon. We urged Iran to stop its support for nonstate armed groups in the region. Absent a diplomatic solution, we committed to continuing our coordination to economically and politically constrain the Iranian regime’s ability to sow instability in the region and around the world. We strongly condemned Iran’s attacks against its neighbors and the disruption of international trade, energy security, and the global economy caused by the obstruction of transit passage through the Strait of Hormuz. We reaffirmed the importance of protecting civilians and civilian objects, and called on Iran to respect its international human rights and humanitarian law obligations. We called on Iran to cease its persistent attacks against civilian vessels in the Strait of Hormuz. We reaffirmed our commitment to the right of safe and free passage and our opposition to any tolls, fees, illegal costs, discriminations or any limitation imposed on maritime transit through the Strait. We underscored the importance of the defensive activities undertaken by U.S. Central Command in the Strait of Hormuz to demine the waterway and escort civilian vessels. We recognized that the multinational, independent, and defensive initiative led by France and the UK can play an important role in facilitating the resumption of maritime traffic through the Strait of Hormuz also by supporting the verification of the removal of all mines. We reaffirmed our commitment to fully implement the obligations under all relevant UN Security Council resolutions sanctions and related restrictive measures reinstated in September 2025 through the snapback mechanism under UN Security Council resolution 2231, and called on all UN Member States to do the same. We urged Iran to return to compliance with its international obligations, and in particular to resume full cooperation with the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) in order to restore transparency regarding the nature of its nuclear program. We also expressed grave concern over Iranian involvement in violent plots against many of our citizens and territories. We recognized the United Kingdom’s attribution of Iran’s involvement in the incident at RAF Fairford on 27 September. Iran should be in no doubt that we are united and remain committed to safeguarding our sovereignty. On Yemen, we condemned in the strongest terms the unacceptable continued strikes carried out by the Houthis in Yemen and against the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, including those on civilians and civilian infrastructure. We called on the Houthis to immediately cease all military actions and threats and refrain from any further escalation to enable a return to an inclusive political process. We expressed our solidarity with the Government of Yemen and the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, and reaffirmed their right to defend their security, sovereignty and territorial integrity in accordance with international law. We urged all actors, including Iran, to end their arming of and support for the Houthis, in violation of several United Nations Security Council resolutions. We expressed deep concern at the worsening humanitarian impact of the conflict and called for the protection of civilians and safe, unimpeded humanitarian access with the urgent opening of a humanitarian corridor in Taiz. We reiterated our call for the immediate and unconditional release of all humanitarian personnel, including the 70 UN staff who remain unjustly detained by the Houthis. We reaffirmed the importance of maritime safety and security in the Red Sea and the Bab al-Mandab Strait. We shared the importance of continuing support to the Government of Yemen, including through capacity-building. We recognized the positive contribution of the EU maritime defensive operations EUNAVFOR ASPIDES and EUNAVFOR ATALANTA to restore maritime security and protect maritime shipping and the lives of seafarers in the Strait of Bab al-Mandab, the Red Sea and the Gulf of Aden. On Lebanon, we stressed the need for all parties to fully respect the ceasefire and expressed support for implementation of the Trilateral Framework and of UN Security Council Resolution 1701. We reiterated that the disarmament of all non-state armed groups, foremost among them Hezbollah, remains essential to ensuring that all weapons are brought under the authority and control of the Lebanese state. We called on Lebanon and Israel to make progress implementing the pilot zones to allow for full and verifiable Hezbollah disarmament and Israeli redeployment as the Lebanese Armed Forces (LAF) deploy. We reiterated our support for the Lebanese authorities’ efforts to achieve the disarmament of all non-state armed groups and for Lebanese sovereignty and territorial integrity. As the mandate of the United Nations Interim Force in Lebanon (UNIFIL) is set to expire at the end of the year, we underscored the need for a robust, credible, and long-lasting security architecture in Lebanon in support of the LAF, in line with UN Security Council resolution 1701 and enabling further implementation of the Trilateral Framework. In calling for a strengthened LAF, we welcomed the establishment of the EU CSDP mission EU Support Mission in Lebanon (EUSM Lebanon). We called upon Lebanese actors to move forward in the adoption and implementation of financial reforms in view of agreeing on an IMF program. On Gaza, we remained committed to the swift implementation of UN Security Council Resolution 2803 and to accelerate humanitarian, recovery and reconstruction efforts aimed at fostering long-term stability. We unequivocally condemned the attacks committed by Hamas on the 7th of October, reiterating that Hamas can have no role in Gaza’s future and must decommission its weaponry. Israel must progressively withdraw from the Gaza Strip, under the conditions outlined in UN Security Council Resolution 2803. We stressed the urgent need for the safe, rapid, sustained, and unimpeded delivery of humanitarian assistance throughout Gaza and the opening of additional crossings, as well as the rehabilitation of humanitarian infrastructure and the protection of civilians. It is vital that all parties continue to engage constructively on the next steps outlined in the Comprehensive Plan, in pursuit of a political horizon for peaceful and prosperous coexistence, for the Israeli and Palestinian people, that advances Middle East peace and stability. We called for ending terrorist attacks and other actions which increase tensions and the risk of escalation in the West Bank. On Syria, we reaffirmed our strong support for a peaceful and inclusive political transition towards a united, sovereign and stable Syria, ensuring respect for human rights and fundamental freedoms for all Syrians. We stressed the importance of fully implementing the arrangements reached on the peaceful integration of Northeast Syria and reiterated our commitment to fighting terrorism. We expressed concern over the situation in Southern Syria, calling for the protection of civilians and respect for Syria’s sovereignty and territorial integrity. We also reaffirmed the importance of supporting Syria’s economic recovery and reconstruction to achieve lasting stability and to enhance regional connectivity. Indo-Pacific We emphasised the importance of a free and open Indo-Pacific region which is prosperous and secure, and that protects shared principles including sovereignty, territorial integrity, the rule of law, and the peaceful settlement of disputes. We reiterated our commitment to upholding freedom of navigation and overflight in the region and called on States to abide by their obligations under international law, as reflected in the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS). We expressed our serious concerns over the situation in the East China Sea and the South China Sea. We reaffirmed our strong opposition to any unilateral attempts to change the status quo, particularly by force or coercion or any actions that raise tensions and risk escalation. We reiterated that the award rendered by the Arbitral Tribunal on 12 July 2016 is a significant milestone, which is final and legally binding upon the parties to the proceedings. We stressed the importance of maintaining peace and stability across the Taiwan Strait. In the context of China’s increasingly assertive activities in the waters east of Taiwan, which threaten regional stability, freedom of navigation and the safety of international shipping, we reaffirmed our opposition to any unilateral attempts to change the status quo, particularly by force or coercion, or the threat thereof. We encouraged the peaceful resolution of cross-Strait issues through constructive dialogue. We also expressed our support for Taiwan’s meaningful participation in international organizations. We strongly condemned North Korea’s unlawful nuclear weapons and ballistic missile programs and reaffirmed our commitment to the complete denuclearization of North Korea, in accordance with all relevant United Nations Security Council resolutions. We underlined that increased cooperation between Russia and North Korea has serious consequences for European and Indo-Pacific security. We urged North Korea to immediately cease all assistance and to withdraw its troops. We reaffirmed our concern regarding cryptocurrency thefts and cybercrimes committed by North Korea and expressed the need to respond to its unlawful overseas labor program. We urged North Korea to immediately resolve the issue of abductions. We remain deeply concerned by the deterioration of the human rights and humanitarian situation across Myanmar. We reiterated the need for the immediate de-escalation of violence, the unimpeded passage of humanitarian assistance, and a genuine and inclusive democratic process that reflects the will of the people of Myanmar. Sudan We were alarmed by the devastating consequences of the war on the Sudanese people and the growing risk of famine in parts of Darfur and Kordofan. Continued fighting, restrictions on humanitarian access and attacks, including by drones, affecting healthcare facilities, displacement camps and the infrastructure civilians rely on for food are putting lives at risk, which is being compounded by the impact of El Niño. A year after the atrocities in El Fasher, we unequivocally condemned all violations and abuses against civilians, including conflict-related sexual violence against women and girls. We called on all external actors to cease supplying or facilitating armed, logistical, and financial support to the belligerents and to use their influence to encourage the warring parties to protect civilians and civilian infrastructure, lift restrictions on humanitarian access and support de-escalation, and avoid any action that could contribute to the conflict. We underscored that, beyond an immediate cease-fire, a peaceful and durable resolution of the conflict is essential to securing unity and long-term stability in Sudan. In line with the principles stated at the Sudan Ministerial Conference in Berlin in April this year, we reaffirmed that a credible Sudanese civilian-led, inclusive, and transparent political dialogue process that addresses historical grievances and respects Sudan’s sovereignty and territorial integrity is critical to securing a lasting peace. We demanded the Rapid Support Forces and the Sudanese Armed Forces comply with international humanitarian law, engage in negotiations including with the Quad with a view to reaching a permanent ceasefire, and guarantee rapid and unimpeded humanitarian access. We reiterated our full support to the work of the Quintet aiming to facilitate such a dialogue, in a process that should run in parallel to and in close alignment with efforts to secure a ceasefire. We call on the wider international community to support these efforts. Horn of Africa We noted with great concern the worsening security situation in the Horn of Africa, specifically between Ethiopia and Eritrea, which bears the risk of regional escalation amid rising cross-border tensions. We underlined the serious consequences further escalation could have for regional stability, already dire humanitarian crises, security and international trade, including in the Red Sea. We called on all parties to exercise maximum restraint, pursue diplomatic solutions, and ensure safe and unhindered humanitarian access and the protection of civilians, especially women and children. We reaffirmed the importance of respecting the sovereignty, political independence and territorial integrity of all countries in the region. In particular, we supported efforts by the United Nations and the African Union to reduce tensions and to facilitate dialogue between the parties. Haiti We supported and welcomed the renewal of the Gang Suppression Force (GSF) mandate through March 2027, which aims to assist Haitian forces in restoring security and stability in Haiti. We also welcomed the renewal of the UN sanctions regime, which promotes accountability for individuals and entities who threaten peace, security, and stability in Haiti. We called for international support to strengthen the Haitian National Police and Haitian Armed Forces, uphold the rule of law, and combat impunity. We also called on all security actors operating in Haiti to prioritize the protection of Haitian civilians in all security operations. We stressed the importance of organizing democratic elections in Haiti and noted the postponement of the first round of elections to July 2027. Noting progress made by the government and the Provisional Electoral Council in their work to advance Haiti’s path to elected governance, we underlined the need to safeguard the credibility and integrity of the electoral process and underscored the responsibility of Haitian authorities to ensure their full and impartial implementation of the electoral decree. We called for concrete results that strengthen public confidence in the electoral process and contribute to a credible return to democratic governance. We noted with concerns regarding the participation of sanctioned individuals in the political process, which undermines accountability and public trust. The people of Haiti have a right to determine their future through credible democratic processes and leaders who serve the public interest with integrity. We remain deeply concerned by the ongoing humanitarian crisis, widespread violence, and reports of human rights violations in Haiti. We urged the international community to intensify financial contributions to the UN Trust Fund, recognizing that the success of the UN-mandated hybrid mission depends on sustained multilateral support to resource its operations. We urged critical international support for humanitarian assistance for Haiti, in order to address the multiple crises facing the people of Haiti. We also underscored the importance of laying the groundwork for Haiti’s economic recovery with the support of international financial institutions and other multilateral partners. We welcomed the World Bank’s Compact with the Haitian authorities as a common framework to assess Haitian-led reform efforts and strengthen accountability for results. We committed to working with diverse Haitian and international partners to promote greater coordination and complementarity of efforts. Cuba We expressed our concerns about the profound economic crisis and humanitarian needs facing the Cuban people, including shortages of food, fuel and medicines. We stressed the importance of improving humanitarian aid delivery mechanisms into and throughout Cuba in order to improve the welfare of the Cuban people. We called on the Cuban authorities to pursue and implement significant and meaningful political and economic reforms to advance prosperity, respect for human rights, and the legitimate aspirations of the Cuban people, and to take concrete steps towards multi-party democratic governance, press freedom, and freedom of expression and association. We also called on the Cuban authorities to release all individuals who have been arbitrarily detained. We encouraged constructive and inclusive dialogue in order to find a way out of the crisis. Venezuela We acknowledged the will of the people of Venezuela to turn the page on the country’s prolonged political and economic crisis. In this regard, we reaffirmed our full support for the ongoing reconciliation talks that bring together the interim government and the delegation representing the National Assembly elected in 2015 and which have already yielded measurable progress. We called on all parties to continue to engage in good faith on the path leading from the restoration of institutions and the rule of law to the holding of free and fair elections. We emphasised the particular importance of providing guarantees to all parties and civil society organizations to enable their participation in the democratic process. We called for the release of all political prisoners. We acknowledged that Venezuela’s economic recovery is inextricably linked to the political reconciliation process and encouraged investments and commercial deals that help build a more stable and prosperous future for the Venezuelan people. We also offered emergency humanitarian response and civil protection activities following the devastating twin earthquakes on June 24, 2026. UN reform and efficiency of humanitarian assistance Committed to making the UN more efficient and effective, accountable and impactful, we welcomed ongoing efforts under the UN80, as well as humanitarian reform initiatives, including the Humanitarian Reset. These latter initiatives aim to strengthen the humanitarian system through better coordination, mandate delineation, and consolidation of common services and critical enablers, while remaining fully open to all impartial humanitarian actors and in full compliance with international law and the UN Charter. We reiterated the importance of maintaining sustained momentum in driving forward reform at this critical juncture for the UN. We commended the work of the G7 working group on the efficiency of the humanitarian supply chain (LOG+7), which is one of the most strategic drivers to increase the impact of assistance in a context of a significant decrease in financing and worsening of crises. These efforts towards a more integrated supply chain, including the reinforcement of the existing humanitarian hubs and pooling of resources, will help reach a greater proportion of the population in need without budgetary changes, and thereby contributing to address growing humanitarian needs including food insecurity and malnutrition in all its forms. This work will continue within the framework of the Humanitarian Leadership Group on Supply Chain led by the European Union and through the UN80 integrated supply chain initiative. Food security and nutrition We stressed our commitment to food security and nutrition to address the consequences of conflicts and instability, and to strengthen food systems resilience. We called for continuing action to address the disruptions to food trade in the Black Sea in the context of the war in Ukraine, the closure of the Strait of Hormuz and the El Niño phenomenon. Together, in 2026, we mobilized 2.5 billion USD of international funding to address the crisis in the Middle East, adding to our long-term commitment to more resilient food systems and fertilizer markets. Forced displacement of people We noted the serious impact of conflict, violence, and instability on affected countries and regions, as well as on broader regional and international security affecting the security of civilian populations. This constitutes a driver of forced displacement and irregular migration, and exposes victims of human trafficking to acute forms of abuse and exploitation. Malicious hybrid activities We condemned persistent malicious hybrid activities by states and non-state actors aimed at undermining the security and stability of the G7 Members and partner countries, through coordinated and deliberate campaigns, including acts of sabotage against critical infrastructure, malicious cyber activities, foreign information manipulation and interference, and the instrumentalization of migration. Such actions risk unintended effects, escalation, and miscalculation. We reaffirmed our determination to act resolutely and in a coordinated manner to address hybrid campaigns, using all available tools to prevent, deter, and respond to these actions, irrespective of their origin, scale and intensity. We stressed the need to reinforce our common efforts and accelerate work on all relevant work strands, in order to strengthen resilience, enhance preparedness, and protect critical infrastructure. Transnational Organized Crime We expressed concern about the increasingly sophisticated methods, violence, and reach of transnational organized criminal groups worldwide, in particular those involved in drug trafficking, human trafficking, and migrant smuggling, and underscored the importance of international cooperation to strengthen maritime security, combat illicit trafficking networks, and dismantle these groups. We also recognized that online scams are a form of rapidly growing transnational organized crime that poses a threat to regional and international peace and security, and stressed the need to strengthen collaboration, including with the private sector, as appropriate, and to disrupt online scam networks, which may be linked to other forms of transnational organized crime. Maritime and port security We reaffirmed the absolute necessity of ensuring maritime safety and security, and of safeguarding freedom of navigation worldwide, in accordance with international law as reflected in the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS), in order to prevent any lasting disruption to global supply chains, particularly with regard to energy, fertilizers and food products, because this can seriously affect vulnerable economies and populations. We recalled the global pledge initiated by the EU of 12 October 2026 on maintaining the integrity of the international law of the sea “No Fees, No Tolls”. We also underlined the need to strengthen the resilience and protection of critical undersea infrastructure, particularly submarine energy infrastructure and telecommunications cables, and their landing stations, including through enhanced international cooperation, information-sharing, redundancy and rapid repair capabilities. We encouraged practical cooperation with industry to improve access to repair vessels, equipment and spare parts, and to facilitate timely authorizations and port access for repairs, consistent with applicable international law and national requirements. In order to strengthen operational cooperation across our key maritime ports or relevant authorities, we, together with Brazil and the Republic of Korea, launched the G7+ Ports Network to Combat Drug Trafficking. This network will help strengthen operational cooperation, the exchange of information and the sharing of best practices to protect our ports from drug trafficking, in coordination and coherence with existing initiatives such as the European Ports Alliance, the European Coalition Against Drugs and the Maritime Safety Committee, and with the support of international organizations, in particular the United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime. We welcomed the work of the members of the G7++ “Friends of the Gulf of Guinea” group to create opportunities for deeper engagement with the Yaoundé Architecture for strengthening partnerships in the fields of training, capacity-building and joint operations, as well as our judicial cooperation to facilitate the prosecution of traffickers apprehended at sea.
