We welcomed the work carried out by the members of the G7 and Nordic Baltic 8++ Shadow Fleet Task Force and reiterated our commitment to enhance G7 coordination with partners to further disrupt and deter the global shadow fleet engaged in illegal, unsafe or environmentally perilous activities. Resilience of critical satellite infrastructure We also recognized the need to strengthen the resilience of critical satellite infrastructure, including satellites, ground stations and control centres, and their supporting terrestrial connections and power supplies. We encouraged stronger protection against physical and cyber threats and harmful interference, as well as redundancy and contingency arrangements to maintain essential services. Taking into account the interdependence of undersea, satellite and terrestrial networks, we encouraged cooperation among competent authorities and operators on risk assessment, timely and secure incident information-sharing, and preparedness exercises. Such cooperation should support rapid service restoration, including through complementary connectivity options for essential communications, while safeguarding sensitive information. Frontier models We recognized the opportunities offered by frontier models to advance science and strengthen our economies, while also noting the need to ensure the secure and trustworthy development of these advanced systems and models through adequate safeguards and human-centric adoption, taking into account that they can pose risks, including for society and economic security. We acknowledged that frontier models can be misused by state and non-state malicious actors, including for malicious cyber activities and criminal activities, or to acquire and enhance chemical, biological, radiological, nuclear or explosive capabilities. We recognized the importance of strengthening the security and resilience of frontier models to advance innovation, economic prosperity, and national security. The developments and issues are complex. That is why it is key that governments, international organizations businesses and academia engage in discussions on model adoption. We will pursue our discussion to advance a secure innovation ecosystem for trusted frontier model deployment including through efforts started with the Hiroshima AI Process. Economic security and critical minerals We reaffirmed our shared concerns regarding the use of non-market policies and practices and economic coercion, especially on critical minerals and their related dual-use items. We will work towards strengthening our competitiveness and addressing the root causes of our common challenges. We affirmed the importance of the G7 Coordination Platform on Economic Coercion to build a common response to economic coercion and further promote cooperation with partners beyond the G7. We further recognized the importance of maintaining and strengthening of our midstream and downstream industries’ competitiveness, including in relation to critical minerals, by protecting critical technologies and commit to working within the G7 and with partners to coordinate on policy measures for technology control. Recognizing the strategic role of critical minerals value chains for the economic prosperity and security of our countries, and in light of the high market concentration in certain economies in the critical minerals sector, we reiterated the urgency of reducing strategic dependencies and vulnerabilities by diversifying and securing trusted supply chains to build up our collective resilience. In that regard, we recognized the importance of the measures announced at the Evian Summit to ensure critical minerals supply chains resilience and security. We commended the expansion of the G7 Critical Minerals Resilience and Production Alliance which builds on the G7 Critical Minerals Production Alliance launched under Canada’s G7 Presidency in 2025. This expanded Alliance and other platforms provide a venue for cooperation within the G7 and with partner countries in order to facilitate discussion, support data-driven decision-making and foster coordination among members to strengthen diversification and resilience of critical minerals value chains. End Text.

title: Destroyer returns from 11-month-deployment
zh_title: 驱逐舰结束 11 个月的部署返回
summary: 夏威夷珍珠港——导弹驱逐舰迈克尔·墨菲号在经过 346 天的部署（其中包括在南中国海的行动、12 次有争议地穿越霍尔木兹海峡、43 次海上补给以及 10 个月后撤换其指挥官）之后于周四返航，受到了草裙舞者和海峡上空延伸的彩虹的欢迎。尽管这艘航空母舰于 10 月 8 日返回圣地亚哥基地，但其大部分部署时间都隶属于亚伯拉罕·林肯号航母打击群。但它可能打破的任何部署长度记录都是短暂的。斯普鲁亚
content:
夏威夷珍珠港——导弹驱逐舰迈克尔·墨菲号在经过 346 天的部署（其中包括在南中国海的行动、12 次有争议地穿越霍尔木兹海峡、43 次海上补给以及 10 个月后撤换其指挥官）之后于周四返航，受到了草裙舞者和海峡上空延伸的彩虹的欢迎。尽管这艘航空母舰于 10 月 8 日返回圣地亚哥基地，但其大部分部署时间都隶属于亚伯拉罕·林肯号航母打击群。但它可能打破的任何部署长度记录都是短暂的。另一艘阿利伯克级驱逐舰斯普鲁恩斯号在经过 12 个月的部署后于今天返回家园，驻日本的约翰·芬恩号船员被告知预计将进行 13 至 14 个月的部署。正如《防务一号》10 月 22 日报道的那样，海军官员告诉家属，在可预见的未来，部署时间预计为 10 到 10 个月，这与近几十年来典型的 7 个月部署形成鲜明对比。海军最高军士长、海军军士长约翰·佩里曼 (John Perryman) 一周后证实了这一点，并表示至少在未来几年内，10 至 11 个月将成为常态。迈克尔·墨菲号中校表示，“迈克尔·墨菲”号于 2025 年 12 月 1 日离开夏威夷，穿过南中国海和马六甲海峡，然后到达北阿拉伯海，并在那里度过了大部分部署时间。大卫·尼古拉斯一个月前接任这艘驱逐舰的指挥。
尼古拉斯说，“迈克尔·墨菲”号在“史诗狂怒”行动期间发动了“战斧”导弹袭击，并参与了霍尔木兹海峡的封锁。“我非常自豪能够成为这个团队的一员，”他说。 “这是我有幸共事过的最有韧性的团队。”尼古拉斯此前指挥过另一艘导弹驱逐舰奥斯卡·奥斯汀号。据海军新闻稿称，当他于 9 月 10 日将掌权交给继任者时，他将成为罗德岛州水面作战学校的教官。但一名海军官员向《防务一号》证实，当“迈克尔·墨菲”号的前任上司中校改变了他的计划。凯特琳·坎宁安 (Caitlin Cunningham) 在执掌约 11 个月后，因“失去信心”而于 9 月 27 日被解职。在周四的返校节上，三等士官杰西·布莱森第一个下船，成为“初吻”抽奖的获胜者。他和妻子阿里安娜·里奥斯站在一起，开玩笑说这次部署涉及“大量的水”。 “加入海军，看看世界——但世界 70% 都是水，”他笑着说。但是，他补充说，工作人员很棒。 “我认为你可以把这艘船上的任何人放在任何其他船上，他们都会脱颖而出，”布莱森说。 ]]>

【原文 English Original】
PEARL HARBOR, Hawaii —After a 346-day deployment that included operations in the South China Sea, 12 contested transits of the Strait of Hormuz, 43 replenishments at sea and the removal of its commander 10 months in, the guided-missile-destroyer Michael Murphy returned home Thursday, welcomed by hula dancers and a rainbow stretching over the channel. The ship was attached to the Abraham Lincoln carrier strike group for much of its deployment, though the aircraft carrier returned to its home in San Diego on Oct. 8. But any deployment-length records it may have broken were short lived. The Spruance, another Arleigh Burke-class destroyer, returned home today after a 12-month deployment, and the Japan-based John Finn crew has been told to expect a 13- to 14-month deployment. As Defense One reported on Oct. 22, Navy officials have told families to expect 10- to 10-month deployments for the foreseeable future—a stark contrast from the typical 7-month deployments of recent decades. The Navy’s top enlisted sailor, Master Chief Petty Officer of the Navy John Perryman, confirmed that a week later, saying 10-11 months will be the norm for at least a few years. The Micheal Murphy left Hawaii on Dec. 1, 2025, and sailed through the South China Sea and Strait of Malacca before reaching the North Arabian Sea, where it spent the bulk of the deployment, said Cmdr. David Nicolas, who took command of the destroyer a month ago. The Michael Murphy launched Tomahawk missile strikes during Operation Epic Fury and took part in the blockade of the Strait of Hormuz, Nicolas said. “I’m incredibly proud to be part of this team,” he said. “This is the most resilient crew that I’ve had the pleasure to serve with.” Nicolas previously commanded the Oscar Austin, another guided-missile destroyer. When he handed over the helm to his successor on Sept. 10, he was slated to become an instructor at Surface Warfare Schools in Rhode Island, according to a Navy press release . But a Navy official confirmed to Defense One that his plans were changed when the Michael Murphy’s previous boss, Cmdr. Caitlin Cunningham, was relieved on Sept. 27 due to a “loss of confidence” after roughly 11 months in charge.    At Thursday’s homecoming, Petty Officer 3rd Class Jesse Bryson was first off the ship, as the winner of the “first kiss” raffle. Standing with his wife, Arianna Rios, he joked that the deployment involved “a lot of water.” “Join the Navy, see the world—but the world is 70-percent water,” he said with a laugh. But, he added, the crew was great. “I think you could put anyone from this ship on any other ship and they’d stand out,” Bryson said. ]]>

title: Spies and silicon chips: Alice Huang’s tangled corporate web
zh_title: 间谍和硅芯片：Alice Huang 错综复杂的企业网络
summary: 总部位于新加坡的科技集团 Megaspeed 经营着价值数十亿美元的世界上最先进的人工智能芯片，但法新社访问时，其办公室已是空壳，其员工似乎早在间谍指控传到他们家门口之前就消失了。数据中心公司 MegaSpeed International 的新加坡办事处。照片：Taryn/法新社 Megaspeed 前董事 Alice Huang 本周被指控为中国间谍，被指控在为北京挖掘公司机密时与 Nvidia 联合创始人 Jensen Huang 有染。爱丽丝·黄 (Alice Huang) 的生活细节模糊不清，几乎令人印象深刻
content:
总部位于新加坡的科技集团 Megaspeed 经营着价值数十亿美元的世界上最先进的人工智能芯片，但法新社访问时，其办公室已是空壳，其员工似乎早在间谍指控传到他们家门口之前就消失了。数据中心公司 MegaSpeed International 的新加坡办事处。照片：Taryn/法新社 Megaspeed 前董事 Alice Huang 本周被指控为中国间谍，被指控在为北京挖掘公司机密时与 Nvidia 联合创始人 Jensen Huang 有染。关于爱丽丝·黄 (Alice Huang) 的生活细节很模糊，几乎不可能确定她住在哪里、在哪里工作、或者出生时间。但她的影响力无疑是广泛传播的，从不起眼的新加坡办公室，到东南亚庞大的数据中心，再到硅谷闪闪发光的董事会会议室。她与云计算公司 Megaspeed 的关系是丑闻的核心。 Megaspeed 标榜自己是一家处于人工智能革命核心的公司，使用 Nvidia 的先进硅芯片为大型数据中心内的高性能计算提供动力。但它也因一个更隐秘的目的而受到调查。据称，Megaspeed 打着为其东南亚数据中心购买计算机硬件的幌子，通过向中国运送 Nvidia 芯片来帮助北京规避贸易限制。北京方面否认了间谍活动的指控，Megaspeed 表示正在调查其是否遵守了敏感芯片的出口管制。
在位于新加坡商业区中心的 Megaspeed 办公室，锁着的玻璃门后面看不到任何工作人员。邻居告诉法新社，过去几个月他们没有看到任何人进出。同样，在距离新加坡仅一桥之隔的马来西亚柔佛州新开发社区的一家购物中心里，子公司 Speedmatrix 的办公室里也没有员工。 2025 年 5 月 22 日，数据中心公司 Megaspeed 的中国高管 Alice Huang（右）出席 Nvidia 首席执行官兼联合创始人黄仁勋（左）在台北一家餐厅举办的晚宴。照片：法新社照片 / CTI via AFPTV。新加坡警方于 2025 年 2 月对 Megaspeed 和其他几家涉嫌规避或违反出口管制的公司展开调查。作为新加坡调查的一部分，爱丽丝·黄接受了采访。新加坡内政部表示，尽管没有受到任何指控，但她于 2026 年 2 月被禁止进入新加坡，原因是提供不准确信息以“淡化她在 Megaspeed 中的作用”。爆炸性增长 公司记录显示黄直接参与了 Megaspeed 的诞生。记录显示，与她有联系的一家公司于 2023 年初收购了中国视频游戏开发商第七大道国际的新加坡子公司。几乎立刻，7Road 的名称就被抛弃并改为 Megaspeed International。黄在 2023 年 3 月至 2023 年 11 月期间担任 Megaspeed 董事不到一年。
她的到来恰逢命运的巨大变化，Megaspeed 从一家名不见经传的视频游戏制造商转变为亚洲最大的 Nvidia 芯片买家之一。根据 2024 年提交的公司账目，在 12 个月内，Megaspeed 的收入从 0 美元跃升至近 3 亿美元。Megaspeed 自称为“云托管服务提供商”，其资产价值从 3200 万美元飙升至近 30 亿美元。期间。 Nvidia 的 H200 芯片。照片：英伟达。只是哦

【原文 English Original】
Singapore-based tech group Megaspeed dealt in billions of dollars’ worth of the world’s most advanced AI chips, but its office was an empty shell when AFP visited, its staff seemingly vanished long before claims of espionage landed at their door. The Singapore office of the data centre company MegaSpeed International. Photo: Taryn/AFP Megaspeed’s former director Alice Huang was this week outed as an alleged Chinese spy, accused of having an affair with Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang while digging up company secrets for Beijing. Details about Alice Huang’s life are vague, making it almost impossible to pin down where she lives, where she works, or when she was born. But her influence undoubtedly spreads far and wide, from the nondescript Singapore office, to hulking data centres in Southeast Asia, to the gleaming boardrooms of Silicon Valley. Her connection to cloud computing firm Megaspeed sits at the centre of the scandal. Megaspeed touts itself as a company at the heart of the AI revolution, using Nvidia’s advanced silicon chips to power high-performance computing inside vast data centres. But it is also under investigation for serving a murkier purpose. Under the guise of buying computer hardware for its Southeast Asia data hubs, Megaspeed has allegedly helped Beijing skirt trade restrictions by sending Nvidia chips into China. Beijing has denied allegations of spying, and Megaspeed said it was investigating if it had complied with export controls on the sensitive chips. At Megaspeed’s office in the heart of the Singapore business district, no staff could be seen behind its locked glass doors. Neighbours told AFP they had not seen anyone come or go for the past few months. Likewise in a mall at a newly developed neighbourhood in Johor, the Malaysian region a bridge away from Singapore, no employees were around in subsidiary Speedmatrix’s office. Alice Huang (R), a Chinese executive linked to the data centre company called Megaspeed, attending a dinner hosted by Nvidia’s chief executive and co-founder Jensen Huang (L in black back facing camera) at a restaurant in Taipei on May 22, 2025. Photo: AFP photo/ CTI via AFPTV. Singapore police opened an investigation in February 2025 into Megaspeed and several other companies suspected of circumventing or violating export controls. Alice Huang was interviewed as part of Singapore’s probe. Although no charges were laid, she was barred from the city-state in February 2026 for providing inaccurate information to “downplay her role in Megaspeed”, Singapore’s home ministry said. Explosive growth Corporate records show Huang’s direct involvement in the birth of Megaspeed. A company linked to her acquired the Singapore arm of Chinese video game developer 7Road International in early 2023, the records showed. Almost immediately, the 7Road name was ditched and changed to Megaspeed International. Huang was listed as a Megaspeed director for less than a year, taking the role between March and November 2023. Her arrival coincided with a drastic change in fortunes, as Megaspeed pivoted from a little-known video game maker to one of Asia’s biggest buyers of Nvidia chips. Within 12 months, Megaspeed’s revenue jumped from $0 to almost US$300 million, according to company accounts filed in 2024. Megaspeed — which described itself as a “cloud hosting services provider” — saw the value of its assets skyrocket from $32 million to almost $3 billion over the same period. Nvidia’s H200 chips. Photo: Nvidia. Just one of Nvidia’s advanced AI computer chips can cost tens of thousands of dollars. Over two years, Megaspeed reportedly traded in upwards of $4 billion worth of Nvidia chips. A financial trail weaving through Singapore, Malaysia and the Cayman Islands suggests Megaspeed’s business may have been boosted by a connection to Chinese tech giant Alibaba. Megaspeed has a Malaysian subsidiary that struck a deal in 2024 pledging assets to Apex Enterprise Solutions in Singapore as security in case of contractual breaches. Apex is linked through a parent company to Alibaba Group Holding Ltd, a firm registered in the Cayman Islands, Singapore corporate data shows. By that time, Huang was no longer registered as a director at Megaspeed. But Singapore authorities said she remained one of Megaspeed’s “key controllers”. Megaspeed’s ultimate holding company is a Singapore firm called Swiftdata. Singapore businessman Tan Yong Pong — who has previously run printing and graphic design companies — is a director of both Megaspeed and Swiftdata. No one answered when AFP visited Tan’s registered address in eastern Singapore, although dogs could be heard barking behind the door. “They are friendly. I occasionally bump into the lady at the lift landing when she’s walking her dog,” an elderly neighbour told AFP. “But we have not seen them for months.” Awkward questions In June 2025, US investigators turned up at Megaspeed to carry out a “post-shipment verification”, with Huang present, according to Singapore’s home ministry, adding that it was the first time it found out about Washington’s probe. The American flag is raised on the newly-installed flagpole on the South Lawn of the White House on June 18, 2025. Photo: White House, via Flickr. That same day, Huang was interviewed by Singapore police who impounded her passport. By then, she and Nvidia boss Jensen Huang had already been spotted together in public. In one of their early outings together, they were seen mingling at an afterparty following the Computex trade show in Taiwan at the beginning of 2024. Trump was briefed on the intelligence findings about their relationship well before it exploded into a public scandal, but said Sunday he did not regret not acting on it. “No, I don’t think so. I think — you know, he’s an honorable guy,” Trump said. But the scandal has sparked national security fears. China and the United States are fighting for supremacy in artificial intelligence, and Nvidia’s market-leading products have become a major point of contention. Nvidia controls an estimated 90 percent of the market for the chips used to train and run AI models, and the US imposed rules in 2022 to restrict their sales to China. In the past years, Jensen Huang has emerged as the leading tech boss urging  Trump to lift those curbs. In any case, the restrictions appear to have been widely circumvented. Singapore. File photo: Tom Grundy/HKFP. A Chinese university tied to the nation’s defence establishment was able to buy advanced Nvidia chips, according to procurement notices from October and September. Singapore’s probe into Megaspeed is ongoing. Separately, Malaysia said Friday it is investigating the company’s subsidiary Speedmatrix to determine if chips imported into the country had been exported to other jurisdictions. Megaspeed itself said it has retained a US lawfirm to examine its compliance. “Megaspeed takes its compliance obligations under US export control laws extremely seriously,” it said. Tangled webs Alice Huang sits in the middle of a corporate web, connected to myriad shell companies, investment houses and major Chinese technology firms. Corporate records filed in Hong Kong list her as a director of Nanjing Lingxing Technology, which operates the popular T3 ride hailing platform in China. Other notable investors in Nanjing Lingxing Technology include Alibaba and Tencent, as well as state-backed carmakers like China FAW and Dongfeng Motor Group. A corporate CV published by a Chinese investment firm details Huang’s rapid ascent through the ranks of Asian investment banking. She served in a senior role at HSBC sometime around 2012, the resume claims, before moving on to stints at CITIC Securities and Shanghai Hexi Investment. The HSBC headquarters in Central, Hong Kong. File photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. Singapore business filings described her as a Chinese citizen with a Hong Kong passport. She was born in China’s landlocked Hunan province, which she left to study media in Hong Kong, HK01 media reported. A CCTV reporter wrote on Weibo that she worked with Huang at the Chinese broadcaster, but later deleted the post.

title: Trump, Xi, Putin to hold historic meeting in China: White House
zh_title: 特朗普、习近平、普京将在中国举行历史性会晤：白宫
summary: 白宫周五表示，唐纳德·特朗普、弗拉基米尔·普京和习近平将于下周在深圳举行的峰会上举行美国、俄罗斯和中国领导人之间的首次三方会晤。 2026 年 7 月 6 日星期一，美国总统唐纳德·特朗普在椭圆形办公室举行的特朗普账户启动活动中敲响了纽约证券交易所和纳斯达克的开盘钟。照片：Joyce N. Boghosian，来自 Flickr。特朗普希望在周四的三边会谈中讨论削减核武库的问题，并且还将提及他在伊朗的战争，但预计他不会讨论俄罗斯
content:
白宫周五表示，唐纳德·特朗普、弗拉基米尔·普京和习近平将于下周在深圳举行的峰会上举行美国、俄罗斯和中国领导人之间的首次三方会晤。 2026 年 7 月 6 日星期一，美国总统唐纳德·特朗普在椭圆形办公室举行的特朗普账户启动活动中敲响了纽约证券交易所和纳斯达克的开盘钟。照片：Joyce N. Boghosian，来自 Flickr。美国官员表示，特朗普希望在周四的三边会谈中讨论削减核武库的问题，并且还将提及他在伊朗的战争，但预计他不会讨论俄罗斯在乌克兰的战争。白宫发言人奥利维亚·威尔士告诉记者，三位领导人将在中国南方城市亚太经合组织峰会期间会面。 “总统已明确表示，除其他议题外，他将讨论世界范围内核武器的削减。特朗普总统认为，这种扩散非常危险，”威尔士说。美国官员表示，主导特朗普第二个总统任期的主要冲突之一将成为焦点，但另一个则不会。一位不愿透露姓名的美国高级官员在电话中对记者表示：“我认为总统确实打算在与习近平和普京的三边会议上讨论伊朗问题。” 2026 年 5 月 20 日，中国国家主席习近平在北京人民大会堂。照片：克里姆林宫。
这位官员补充说，华盛顿与基辅和莫斯科有“完全不同的轨道”谈判，旨在结束乌克兰战争。他指的是美国特使最近几天与普京和乌克兰总统泽连斯基进行的会谈。“中国实际上并不是该轨道的一部分，因此在那里讨论乌克兰问题似乎并不合适，”该官员补充道。官员们表示，特斯拉和 Space X 的老板埃隆·马斯克将陪同特朗普访华，但不会参与与习近平和普京的会面。特朗普周四还将与中国国家主席举行双边工作午餐和会晤，这是自美国总统去年重新掌权以来的第四次会面。但特朗普没有计划与普京进行单独的一对一会谈。官员们表示，除其他话题外，英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋因与一名所谓的中国间谍有染而辞职的问题预计不会出现在特朗普与习近平的会晤中。 2026 年 5 月 20 日，中国国家主席习近平（左）在北京人民大会堂欢迎俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京。照片：克里姆林宫。另一位美国高级官员表示：“英伟达的情况实际上不会对此次访问产生任何影响。”美国也不打算讨论敏感芯片技术的出口管制，而这正是英伟达丑闻的核心。 “我们不就美国的出口管制进行谈判。
第二位官员表示：“这些都是我们在政府中制定的国家安全问题……我们不希望它出现在我们在那里与中国人的任何对话中。”特朗普将于周一离开华盛顿，周二抵达菲律宾参加东南亚国家联盟（ASEAN）峰会，然后前往深圳。

【原文 English Original】
Donald Trump, Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping will hold the first ever three-way meeting between the leaders of the United States, Russia and China at a summit in Shenzhen next week, the White House said Friday. US President Donald Trump rings the opening bell for the New York Stock Exchange and the Nasdaq during an event to launch Trump Accounts, Monday, July 6, 2026, in the Oval Office. Photo: Joyce N. Boghosian, via Flickr. Trump wants to talk about reducing nuclear arsenals at the trilateral talks on Thursday and is also set to bring up his war in Iran — but he is not expected to discuss Russia’s war in Ukraine, US officials said. The three leaders will meet on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in the southern Chinese city, White House spokeswoman Olivia Wales told reporters. “The president has made it clear that, among other topics, he will discuss the reduction of nuclear weapons in the world. This proliferation, President Trump believes, is very dangerous,” Wales said. One of the major conflicts dominating Trump’s second term as president will feature, but the other will not, the US officials said. “I think the president does intend to talk about Iran in the trilateral meeting with Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin,” a senior US official, speaking on condition of anonymity, told reporters on a call. Chinese President Xi Jinping at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing on May 20, 2026. Photo: The Kremlin. Washington has a “whole other track” of negotiations with Kyiv and Moscow aimed at ending the war in Ukraine, the official added, referring to talks that US envoys have had in recent days with Putin and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky. “China is not really a part of that track, so it doesn’t seem appropriate to have the Ukraine discussion there,” the official added. Tesla and Space X boss Elon Musk will accompany Trump on his trip to China but won’t be involved in the meeting with Xi and Putin, the officials said. Trump will also hold a bilateral working lunch and meeting with the Chinese president on Thursday — their fourth meeting since the US president’s return to power last year. But Trump is not scheduled to have a separate one-on-one with Putin. Among other topics, Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang’s resignation over an affair with an alleged Chinese spy is not expected to come up in Trump’s meetings with Xi, the officials said. Chinese President Xi Jinping (left) welcomes Russian President Vladimir Putin at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing on May 20, 2026. Photo: The Kremlin. “The situation with Nvidia should not really have any bearing on the trip,” a second US senior official said. The United States also did not plan to discuss export controls on sensitive chip technology, which were at the heart of the Nvidia scandal. “We do not negotiate American export controls. These are national security matters that we develop in the administration… and we don’t expect it to figure at all in any of our conversations with the Chinese while we’re there,” the second official said. Trump will leave Washington on Monday and arrive in the Philippines on Tuesday for a summit of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) summit before heading to Shenzhen.

title: Joshua Wong’s prison letters reveal inner shift as Hong Kong activist faces another decade behind bars
zh_title: 黄之锋的监狱信件揭示了香港活动人士面临又一个十年牢狱之灾的内心转变
summary: 在今年早些时候的一封监狱信中，黄之锋表达了他对涉外勾结案即将被判刑的担忧。 “无论是2032年还是2037年，我的精神状态都不好，”他用中文写道，权衡着自己何时才能重获自由。黄之锋于2019年6月17日从荔枝角接待中心获释。资料照片。 “痛苦不可避免地源于此：如果是 2037 年怎么办？嗯，（人们）当下很容易产生同情，但很难保持一致，而且只会变得更加困难。”这位30岁的民主活动人士已经花掉了几乎
content:
在今年早些时候的一封监狱信中，黄之锋表达了他对涉外勾结案即将被判刑的担忧。 “无论是2032年还是2037年，我的精神状态都不好，”他用中文写道，权衡着自己何时才能重获自由。黄之锋于2019年6月17日从荔枝角接待中心获释。资料照片。 “痛苦不可避免地源于此：如果是 2037 年怎么办？嗯，（人们）当下很容易产生同情，但很难保持一致，而且只会变得更加困难。”这位30岁的民主活动人士已经因多项罪行入狱近六年，原定于一月份获释，直到当局去年指控他与外国势力勾结，这是北京实施的国家安全法针对他的第二起案件。 11月5日，就在他即将获释前两个月，法院以共谋罪判处他10年以上有期徒刑。目前，他预计将服役到 2036 年底，届时他将年满 40 岁。当新的刑期宣布时，黄站在被告席内，微微摇头并做了笔记，但显得很平静。谭威廉法官裁定，根据北京实施的国家安全法，黄的罪行属于“性质严重”的罪行之一，该法可判处最低 10 年监禁、最高无期徒刑。 2026 年 2 月，黄之锋写给朋友、前学生活动同学路易斯·李 (Louis Lee) 的一封监狱信。
这张照片拍摄于 2026 年 9 月 30 日。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。法官因黄认罪而将起始刑期 13 年减刑三年。在黄之锋被判刑前，两位密友向《香港自由报》分享了狱中信件，这位香港民主运动的前典型代表有时会反思面临额外十年监禁的压力。他对朋友们以及整个社会的记忆中消失感到焦虑。 “我不知道随着时间的流逝，我还会失去多少，”黄在一封信中写道。 “责任其实就是反应能力。但谁来反应呢？我不禁深思和怀疑。”黄曾是一位首先致力于香港政治未来的民主活动人士，现在开始以一位富有魅力、雄辩的学生领袖的身份参加竞选活动，他敢于对抗当局，甚至是北京。 Netflix 的一部关于他的纪录片的标题很简洁：《约书亚：青少年与超级大国》。 2026 年 11 月 5 日，黄之锋被判刑后，前学民思潮活动人士李路易斯 (Louis Lee) 和陈蒂芙尼 (Tiffany Chin) 在高等法院。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。然而，入狱多年后，黄已经改变了。据他的朋友说，这位一心关注香港民主运动的少年，尽管被监狱高墙隔开，却变得更有能力关心周围的人。 “对我来说，我们并不是唯一支持他的人。
“事实上，他一直在以自己的方式支持外界的人。”与黄先生一起竞选的前学生活动家蒂芬妮·陈(Tiffany Chin)说。两人曾经是恋人，现在是朋友。而且，随着他曾经支持的政治事业现在被彻底粉碎，黄先生开始向内反思自己。他在另一封信中写道：“我们从小就对社会抱有如此高的抱负，我们应该以同样的标准来要求自己。只有拒绝平庸的生活，我们才配得上我们所设想的世界。”黄之锋被拍照

【原文 English Original】
In a prison letter earlier this year, Joshua Wong expressed dread over the looming sentence in his foreign collusion case. “Fretting about whether it’s 2032 or 2037, my mental state is hardly all right,” he wrote in Chinese, weighing when he might regain his freedom. Joshua Wong released from Lai Chi Kok Reception Centre on June 17, 2019. File photo. “The agony inevitably stems from this: What if it’s 2037? Well, it’s easy [for people] to sympathise in the moment, but it’s difficult to be consistent, and it will only get harder.” The 30-year-old pro-democracy activist has already spent almost six years behind bars over various offences and was set for release in January, until authorities charged him last year with conspiring to collude with foreign forces – the second case against him under the Beijing-imposed national security law. On November 5, just two months before he was due to be released, a court sentenced him to 10 more years in prison for the collusion offence. He is now expected to serve until late 2036, when he turns 40. Standing inside the dock as his new sentence was announced, Wong shook his head slightly and made notes, but appeared calm. Judge William Tam ruled that Wong’s offence was one of a “grave nature” under the Beijing-imposed national security law, which carries a minimum penalty of 10 years in jail and up to life imprisonment. A prison letter Joshua Wong wrote to friend and former fellow student activist Louis Lee in February 2026. This photo is taken on September 30, 2026. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. The judge knocked off three years from a 13-year starting sentence for Wong’s guilty plea. In prison correspondence shared with HKFP by two close friends ahead of Wong’s sentencing, the former poster child of Hong Kong’s democracy movement had at times reflected on the weight of facing an additional decade behind bars. He expressed anxiety over fading from the memory of his friends – and from society at large. “I have no idea how much more I will lose in the passing of time,” Wong wrote in one letter. “Responsibility is, in fact, response-ability. But who will respond? I can’t help but ponder and doubt.” Once a pro-democracy activist dedicated first and foremost to Hong Kong’s political future, Wong began campaigning as a charismatic, eloquent student leader who dared to stand up to the authorities – even to Beijing. A Netflix documentary about him is succinctly titled Joshua: Teenager vs. Superpower . Former Scholarism activists Louis Lee and Tiffany Chin at the High Court after Joshua Wong’s sentencing on November 5, 2026. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. Yet, after years behind bars, Wong has changed. The teenager who focused single-mindedly on Hong Kong’s democracy movement has become more capable of caring for those around him despite being separated by prison walls, according to his friends. “For me, it doesn’t feel like we’re the only ones supporting him. In fact, he has been supporting people on the outside in his own way,” said Tiffany Chin, a former student activist who campaigned alongside Wong. The pair were once romantically involved and are now friends. And, with the political causes he once championed now firmly crushed, Wong has turned inward to reflect on himself. In another letter, he wrote: “We had held such high aspirations for society from a young age, we should hold ourselves to the same standard. Only by refusing a life of mediocrity can we be worthy of the world we envisioned.” Joshua Wong is photographed inside the Lai Chi Kwok Reception Centre on March 4, 2021. File Photo. From ‘robot’ to caring friend On a bright summer day in June 2025, while serving a sentence for subversion at Stanley Prison, Wong was arrested behind bars and brought to court the same day on a fresh charge of conspiracy to collude with foreign forces. The prosecution came without warning. That day, Chin and Louis Lee, another longtime friend of Wong’s, rushed to the court after hearing the news, but failed to see him in person. Authorities accused him of conspiring with Nathan Law in 2020 to collude with foreign elements, citing Wong’s sharing of Law’s social media posts calling for international sanctions against Hong Kong as evidence. The unexpected new charge was devastating to Wong. That month, he confessed he had had a lot of pressure – something he rarely did in the past, Chin said. Nathan Law and Joshua Wong are photographed outside the Lai Chi Kwok Reception Centre on June 17, 2019. File Photo. “After so many prison terms and all the ups and downs over the last decade… he seldom openly showed vulnerability,” she said. “So when he felt the need to say so bluntly that he was not OK, I truly believed he wasn’t.” Having begun campaigning at the age of 14, Wong has been in and out of prison throughout his years of activism. He now has a total of eight criminal convictions, including three separate offences linked to unlawful assembly and two national security offences. Born in 1996 to a Christian family – one year before Hong Kong was handed over to China from British rule – Wong rose to prominence in 2011 when he co-founded student protest group Scholarism amid a public outcry against a proposed patriotic education curriculum. The following year, Scholarism activists occupied the forecourt outside government headquarters in Admiralty and staged a hunger strike to protest what they described as a “brainwashing” curriculum. In a widely reported encounter, the teenager Wong twice rejected shaking hands with then city leader Leung Chun-ying, who visited the protest site alongside education officials. Joshua Wong campaigns on September 28, 2019. He was running for a seat during the 2019 District Council Elections, but was eventually barred from entering the race. File photo. A brief chronology of Joshua Wong’s political activism + Dates Events May 2011 Wong cofounded student group Scholarism  June 2011 –  August 2012 Wong protested against gov’t-proposed Moral and National Education school curriculum through meeting with officials and demonstration August 30, 2012  Scholarism occupied gov’t headquarters, launched hunger strike to oppose the proposed curriculum; Hundreds of thousands joined September 8, 2012 Then-Chief Executive Leung Chun-ying shelved the curriculum April 2014 Scholarism and Hong Kong Federation of Students (HKFS) jointly proposed a political reform package as civic groups introduced proposals of universal suffrage of CE election August 31, 2014 The Standing Committee of the National People’s Congress issued decision on the selecting method of CE candidates in election reform, which is seen a method to screen out opposition candidates September 26, 2014 Members of Scholarism and HKFS broke into “Civic Square” in gov’t headquarters, leading to hundreds of thousands of citizens arriving to support the students; Wong was arrested by police September 28, 2014 Organiser of “Occupy Central with Love and Peace” announced the start of the campaign November 26, 2014 Wong was arrested amid police clearance at the Mong Kok occupation site April 2016 Wong, Nathan Law and some pro-democracy activists founded political party of Demosisto to advocate for democratic self-determination November 2016 Wong travelled to the US for lobbying, meeting US politicians Nancy Pelosi and Marco Rubio Mid-2017 Wong and Law jailed around 70 days over the “Reclaiming Civic Square” protest May 2019 Wong jailed for two months following conviction of contempt of court linked to 2014 social movement June 2019 Wong Joined the 2019 protests and unrest soon after being released from prison  August – September 2019 Wong met political counsellors of the US Consulate General in Hong Kong; travelled to Germany and the US to meet foreign politicians.  October 2019 Wong announced to run for the 2019 District Council Elections  June 30, 2020 Wong announced to resign from the secretary-general of Demosisto; Demosisto announced to disband November 2020 Wong remanded in custody after pleading guilty to Unlawful assembly linked to 2019 protest case; sentenced to four months in 2021 February 28, 2021 Charged with conspiracy to commit subversion along with other 46 democrats over participation in pro-democracy primaries May 2021 Sentenced to 10 months over unlawful assembly for attending 2020 Tiananmen vigil November 2024 Sentenced to four years, eight months over the pro-democracy primaries case June 6, 2025 Charged with conspiracy to collude with foreign forces November 5, 2026 Sentenced to 10 years over foreign collusion Hundreds of thousands of people rallied behind Wong and his fellow student activists, forcing the government to back down and shelve the proposal. But the teenage campaigner was also viewed as somewhat distant and domineering among the inner circle of Scholarism. Lee, who mainly handled protest logistics at that time, described his relationship with Wong as “almost like that of a boss and subordinate.” “I was working at the secretariat at the time, and he would constantly ask for progress updates. Sometimes he’d call to check in, and other times he’d tag us on Facebook,” Lee recalled. “He didn’t care much about how you were doing. He just wanted to get things done.” Louis Lee, a longtime friend of Joshua Wong, is photographed in his room on September 30, 2026. The two engaged in activism together as members of Scholarism between 2011 and 2016. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. Chin, who joined Scholarism around 2013, similarly described Wong as a deeply rational figure who seldom expressed his emotions. “Ten years ago, everyone described him as someone without many feelings,” she said. “Like a robot.” Wong might even come across as “rude,” she added, noting that he rarely said thanks to others during that period. A large part of Wong’s youth coincided with a period of escalating social movements in Hong Kong. Just two years after the anti-patriotic education protests, the city saw the 79-day Umbrella Movement in 2014. Wong, then aged 17, took centre stage in mobilising public support for student protesters, who demanded democratic reform and universal suffrage. In a demonstration that sparked the Umbrella Movement, Wong and other student leaders led protesters into the forecourt of the government headquarters in an action dubbed “Reclaiming Civic Square,” seeking to escalate their campaign. That eventually resulted in Wong’s first criminal conviction. In 2016, Wong and fellow student leaders Alex Chow and Nathan Law were found guilty of unlawful assembly. Though initially spared prison, Wong later served around 69 days behind bars – his first jail term – following a government appeal in 2017. His penalty was ultimately quashed by the Court of Final Appeal in 2018.  Also in 2016, Scholarism disbanded. Wong and several former members, as well as young activists like Law, went on to establish Demosisto, a political party advocating for “democratic self-determination” in the city. Wong served as general secretary. Louis Lee, photographed on November 12, 2026. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. Lee and Chin did not join the new party and they grew estranged from Wong during that period. That year, Law was elected to the Legislative Council, making him the youngest lawmaker in Hong Kong history at the age of 23. He won over 50,000 votes, giving Demosisto a strong popular mandate. The prospect of youth democracy activism appeared bright at the time, but Law was eventually disqualified from his seat in 2017 following an oath-taking controversy. Reconnections It was only after Wong’s detention in late 2020 that Lee and Chin reconnected with him, beginning with an exchange of letters. In 2019, citywide protests and unrest triggered by a controversial extradition bill engulfed the city. Wong and Demosisto were heavily involved in the protests, with the activist frequently lobbying foreign governments to impose sanctions on Hong Kong officials and halt the export of crowd control equipment to the city’s police force. Then, in June 2020, Beijing imposed the national security law, in effect crushing political dissent in the city. Demosisto disbanded on the eve of the law’s enactment, while Nathan Law left Hong Kong in self-exile. In November that year, Wong was remanded in custody after pleading guilty to an unlawful assembly charge linked to the 2019 unrest, marking the beginning of his prison stint that continues to this day. Hong Kong’s West Kowloon district, November 12, 2026. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. For Chin, the catalyst for reconnecting with Wong was realising how much their relationship meant to her following his incarceration. “We were like family to each other. And I felt it was time to resolve our past grievances and carry on our relationship,” she said, pausing briefly to find the words. “Not a romantic one, but one with the kind of care you find in a family.” Their correspondence, Chin said, focused mostly on daily life – the routine details of what was happening on both sides of the prison walls. Some of those Chin received stretched across multiple pages, covered in Wong’s slightly angular handwriting. At times, she would dictate an entry via voice-to-text, edit it on her computer, and assemble photos she had taken into letters running up to a dozen pages. A major change in Wong, Chin noticed, was how often he reflected on his past interactions with people, rather than his public advocacy. “He has changed quite a bit after nearly six years in prison. Like I said, he would reflect on things he didn’t handle well in the past,” she said of Wong’s growth while in prison. “Age is certainly a factor. But, like he said, he has had plenty of time to contemplate now.” “One of the big differences is that he has cherished his connections and bonds with friends even more,” she added. From left: Joshua Wong, Agnes Chow, and Nathan Law, photographed on March 10, 2018. File Photo. Meanwhile, Lee’s exchanges with Wong centred on their wide-ranging shared interests, touching on everything from Taiwanese politics and Japanese idols to popular anime series and Cantopop. “You see in our letters we may go on from anime to worldly affairs, come back to Hong Kong, before heading off to other parts of the world. It may not be easy [for others] to follow,” he said. While in prison, Wong was charged with conspiring to subvert state power under the national security law, in a landmark case known as the “Hong Kong 47” – a reference to the number of defendants. The defendants were prosecuted over an unofficial primary in 2020 aimed at fielding viable candidates, in a bid to secure an unprecedented legislative majority for the pro-democracy camp. Once achieved, the camp had planned to veto government budgets and force the chief executive to resign. Wong was among those who pleaded guilty before the trial opened. In 2024, he was sentenced to four years and eight months in jail. Lee and Chin both described Wong as being “prepared” for the subversion term. “He was able to predict a range within which the sentence would fall. And eventually his prediction was just two months off,” Chin said. “You weren’t overly worried about him. Because at that time you had the feeling that he was capable of handling this, both physically and mentally,” she added. Wong even started imagining what he would do after his release in January 2027, Lee said, before the new charge dimmed his hope. ‘Await your return’ A Correctional Services vehicle believed to be carrying Joshua Wong appears at the High Court on November 5, 2026, for the activist’s sentencing over a collusion conviction. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. In September, Wong pleaded guilty to the collusion offence. His lawyer argued for a sentence of less than 10 years, submitting that his role in the conspiracy was limited and that the activist demonstrated genuine remorse. Wong has had a “lengthy opportunity to reflect on… the path he took,” his lawyer told the court. “He has not wasted his time in prison.” That day, Chin and Lee sat in the front row of the public gallery inside the courtroom. In subsequent letters, Wong thanked them for caring deeply about him. A sense of gratitude runs through the pages of his letters, Chin said. “These few years, he cherished those still beside him, and those who had supported him in any way,” she said. Tiffany Chin uploaded this photo of herself and Joshua Wong after Wong was sentenced to 10 years in jail for foreign collusion. Photo: Supplied. Wong has used his time in prison to read extensively. He has also put on muscle – he has long been known for his slender build – and taken up the guitar. He has also grown attentive to others’ interests and become expressive. Knowing that Chin likes the Beatles and the history of the Second World War, he would include newspaper clippings on those subjects in his letters to her. At times, he has lamented the dwindling attention he receives over the years. “He once mentioned that, for him, not receiving letters meant not feeling cared for,” Chin said. “Some people might have written at first, but gradually stopped… He certainly never feels people have a responsibility or obligation to write to him, but the reality is that fewer have.” Louis Lee, photographed on November 12, 2026. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. The uncertainty of a potentially heavy sentence has weighed on Wong and his close friends. “Honestly speaking, not only does he worry about a long jail term, those of us on the outside also worry that one day we may no longer be able to help as we enter new stages of life,” Lee said, noting that many mutual friends had either left the city or drifted away. It was a “great pain” to face the years ahead, Chin said, adding that she had once shared this feeling with Wong in a letter. “But I am learning to live with this pain, because I feel like it has bonded us, that we are carrying this feeling together,” she said. A photo of Tiffany Chin and Joshua Wong at a ramen shop in Shibuya, Tokyo, in 2016. Chin uploaded this photo to Instagram on November 5, 2026 after Wong was sentenced to 10 years in prison for foreign collusion. Photo: Supplied. Lee said he would wait for Wong’s release for as long as it takes. “Ten years is a really long time, but 10 years can also pass in the blink of an eye,” he said, before quipping: “I always say one of my regrets is that I’ve never had a drink with him… We weren’t even adults back then, and he was obviously the good-boy type.” Former Scholarism members had hoped to gather in 2031, the 20th anniversary of the group, but that would now have to be postponed. The night following Wong’s sentencing, Chin recounted a 2016 trip with him to Japan on social media. At a ramen shop, the pair posed for a photo. “I didn’t know that I would have to wait 20 years for that casual photo to be taken again,” she wrote. Wong reassured her in a letter that they would one day return to that ramen shop in Shibuya, Tokyo. Joshua Wong’s signature on one of his prison letters, photographed on September 30, 2026. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. Quoting the lyrics from a Cantopop song, Chin wrote: “Under the drizzle, I still await your return.”

title: Taiwan Indigenous farmer revives climate-resilient millet
zh_title: 台湾本土农民复兴气候适应型小米
summary: 台湾东南部的原住民农民巴努·伊斯马哈桑 (Banu Ismahasan) 走过一片金色的高秆田，用手收割一种能够抵抗极端天气的古老作物的谷粒。 2026 年 10 月 21 日，台湾农民巴努·伊斯马哈桑 (Banu Ismahasan) 在台东将刚收获的油小米摊开在阳光下晒干。照片：I-Hwa Cheng/AFP 台湾原住民农民曾种植油小米，以防主粮枯死，但 60 多年前，随着水稻变得更加容易获得，油小米基本上从田间消失了。在过去的十年里，伊斯玛哈桑和他年迈的父母一直致力于复兴几乎被遗忘的地方。
content:
台湾东南部的原住民农民巴努·伊斯马哈桑 (Banu Ismahasan) 走过一片金色的高秆田，用手收割一种能够抵抗极端天气的古老作物的谷粒。 2026 年 10 月 21 日，台湾农民巴努·伊斯马哈桑 (Banu Ismahasan) 在台东将刚收获的油小米摊开在阳光下晒干。照片：I-Hwa Cheng/AFP 台湾原住民农民曾种植油小米，以防主粮枯死，但 60 多年前，随着水稻变得更加容易获得，油小米基本上从田间消失了。在过去的十年里，伊斯马哈桑和他年迈的父母一直在台东县布克拉武村的布农社区努力恢复几乎被遗忘的农作物。 “我们只是希望带回许多传统的布农族作物，并再次在这片土地上种植它们，”48岁的伊斯马哈桑在晴朗的蓝天下的油小米田里告诉法新社。油小米，即布农语中的“莳萝”，是台湾特有的植物，可以在山上野生生长。伊斯玛哈桑首先在网上了解到这种植物，然后开始自己的研究，梳理历史文献并与部落长老交谈，其中包括一位记得上次吃这种植物是在半个世纪前的妇女。他发现，布农族农民过去常常在种植主要作物谷子的同时种植油小米，作为收成歉收或发生灾害时的“后备”。经过多年亲自种植油小米，伊斯玛哈桑开始明白为什么他的祖先依赖这种作物。
一粒油小米种子可以长出 15 至 20 个圆锥花序或分枝种子簇，并且茎可以自行再生，而谷子通常每粒种子长出一个圆锥花序，必须在切割后重新播种。事实证明，当极端天气或疾病爆发破坏了他 2.2 公顷（5.4 英亩）的农场时，它比谷子更坚强。伊斯马哈桑说，几年前一场持续了 200 多天的干旱期间，油小米“保持鲜绿色”，而其他作物却枯萎了。台风、洪水，甚至锈病爆发也没有影响到它。台湾中央研究院退休教授、植物遗传学专家邢月娥15年前在一个国际论坛上第一次听说了油小米。幸不知道的是，1890 年代采集的台湾油粟标本就存放在英国皇家植物园 (Kew)。兴带领一个研究小组在台湾东南部的山区找到了油小米，并开始研究这种鲜为人知的谷物。她发现种子的保护性蜡涂层使其无需灌溉、化肥或杀虫剂即可生长，即使在质量较差的土地上也是如此。 2026 年 10 月 21 日，台湾农民 Linkav Ismahasan 在台东的一块田里收割油小米。照片：I-Hwa Cheng / 法新社 油小米富含油、蛋白质和矿物质，可用于人类和动物消费，也可用作燃料。 “它在利用阳光和水方面自然非常有效，”辛说。
“至于土壤条件，即使是在地面布满大石头的山区，它也能生长得很好。” “非常珍贵”伊斯马哈桑从一粒油小米开始了他的种植。现在，这个家庭每年在他们种植其他传统布农谷类作物的土地上每年收获两次油小米。油小米个头小，无味，可以用来做粥、馒头、面包，甚至爆米花。但该家族一直在努力说服其他农民种植这种植物，因为它在商业上尚不可行。油粟不仅是劳动密集型产业，而且意义重大

【原文 English Original】
Indigenous farmer Banu Ismahasan walks through a golden field of tall stalks in southeastern Taiwan , harvesting by hand the grain heads of an ancient crop resistant to extreme weather. Taiwan farmer Banu Ismahasan spreads freshly harvested oil millet out to dry in the sun in Taitung on October 21, 2026. Photo: I-Hwa Cheng / AFP Once grown by Indigenous farmers in Taiwan in case their staple crops died, oil millet largely disappeared from fields more than 60 years ago as rice became more available. Over the past decade, Ismahasan and his elderly parents have worked to revive the nearly forgotten crop in the Bunun community in Buklavu, a village surrounded by lush green mountains in Taitung county. “We just hope to bring back many traditional Bunun crops and grow them on this land again,” Ismahasan, 48, told AFP in his oil millet field under a clear blue sky. Oil millet, or “dill” in the Bunun language, is endemic to Taiwan and can be found growing wild in the mountains. Ismahasan first read about the plant online and then embarked on his own research, combing through historical documents and speaking to tribal elders, including a woman who recalled last eating it half a century ago. He discovered that Bunun farmers used to grow oil millet alongside their staple crop foxtail millet as a “back-up” when harvests failed or disasters hit. After years of growing oil millet himself, Ismahasan came to understand why his ancestors relied on the crop. A single oil millet seed can grow 15 to 20 panicles, or branching seed clusters, and the stems regenerate on their own, while foxtail millet typically grows one panicle per seed and must be sown again after being cut. It has also proven hardier than foxtail millet when extreme weather or disease outbreaks have ravaged his 2.2-hectare (5.4-acre) farm. During a drought several years ago that lasted more than 200 days, the oil millet “stayed bright green” while other crops withered, Ismahasan said. Typhoons, floods and even a rust disease outbreak have not affected it either. Hsing Yue-ie, a retired professor from Taiwan’s Academia Sinica and an expert in plant genetics, first heard of oil millet 15 years ago at an international forum. Unbeknownst to Hsing, specimens of Taiwan oil millet collected in the 1890s were sitting in Britain’s Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew. Hsing led a research team to find oil millet in the mountains of southeastern Taiwan and began studying the little-known cereal. She found that the seed’s protective wax coating enabled it to grow without irrigation, fertilisers or pesticides, even on poor-quality land. Taiwan farmer Linkav Ismahasan harvests oil millet in a field in Taitung on October 21, 2026. Photo: I-Hwa Cheng / AFP Rich in oil, protein and minerals, it can be used for human and animal consumption, as well as for fuel. “It’s naturally very efficient at using sunlight and water,” said Hsing. “As for soil conditions, even in mountainous areas where the ground is full of large rocks, it can still grow very well.” ‘Very precious’ Ismahasan started his crop with one panicle of oil millet. The family now harvests oil millet twice a year on a section of their property where they grow other traditional Bunun cereal crops. Tiny and tasteless, oil millet can be used in porridge, steamed buns, bread and even popcorn. But the family has struggled to convince other farmers to grow it because it is not yet commercially viable. Oil millet is not only labour intensive but also significantly more expensive for consumers than rice, by far Taiwan’s most popular staple. While the current market for oil millet is limited, Taiwan’s National Crop Germplasm Center sees value in preserving its seeds for the future, when climate change might force more farmers to consider growing the crop. Oil millet seeds are “very precious” because of their genetic diversity and ability to adapt to the environment, Lin Yen-yu, an assistant researcher at the centre, told AFP. Seeds are kept in aluminium foil packets and stored at -18C under low-moisture conditions where they can last for decades, Lin said. “In the future, when cultivation methods or climate change undergo certain shifts, their value may start to be recognised and discovered,” he said. “It preserves many possibilities.” Ismahasan said his priority for now was to get more people in his community growing and eating oil millet, bringing “it back into our everyday lives, just as it was for our elders”. “If we don’t even eat it ourselves anymore, how can we expect to turn it into a viable business?” he said.

title: ‘Davidson Window’ Admiral Hopes He Was Wrong On China’s Ability To Take Taiwan By 2027
zh_title: “戴维森之窗”海军上将希望他对中国 2027 年占领台湾能力的判断是错误的
summary: 五年前，这位在国会作证的人提出了所谓的“戴维森窗口”，即中国有能力在 2027 年之前对台湾发动可信的入侵，现在这个日期即将到来，他为他的想法提供了一些见解。当时在太平洋地区指挥美军的海军上将菲利普·戴维森 (Philip Davidson) 在周五发布的播客中表示，自他 2021 年退役以来发生的一些事态发展可能会改变他的预测。然而，美国印太司令部（现太平洋司令部或PACOM）前司令告诉我们为什么要关心这个问题
content:
五年前，这位在国会作证的人提出了所谓的“戴维森窗口”，即中国有能力在 2027 年之前对台湾发动可信的入侵，现在这个日期即将到来，他为他的想法提供了一些见解。当时在太平洋地区指挥美军的海军上将菲利普·戴维森 (Philip Davidson) 在周五发布的播客中表示，自他 2021 年退役以来发生的一些事态发展可能会改变他的预测。然而，美国印太司令部（现太平洋司令部或PACOM）前司令告诉《我们为什么要关心印太？》他仍然认为有理由担心。他特别敦促美国在入侵台湾之前向台湾提供军事援助，以更好地威慑中国采取行动。中国军队练习海滩登陆。 (解放军) 戴维森发表上述声明之际，中国一直在稳步增加在台湾周边的军事演习，中国认为台湾是一个分裂的省份，有朝一日将重新置于其控制之下。在了解戴维森对 SeaLight 基金会创始人兼执行董事雷·鲍威尔 (Ray Powell) 和 BowerGroupAsia 高级顾问吉姆·卡鲁索 (Jim Carouso) 所说的话之前，让我们回顾一下戴维森于 2021 年 3 月 9 日对参议院军事委员会所说的话。
戴维森在谈到中国​​时表示：“我担心他们正在加速实现取代美国的野心，以及我们在基于规则的国际秩序中发挥领导作用的野心，他们长期以来一直表示希望在 2050 年之前实现这一目标，我担心他们会进一步接近这一目标。”菲利普·戴维森，当时担任海军上将和美国印度太平洋司令部司令。 （美国海军）两年后，对所谓“戴维森之窗”的评估得到了中央情报局（CIA）的支持。时任中央情报局局长比尔·伯恩斯 (Bill Burns) 表示：“习主席已指示中国军事领导层解放军 (PLA) 在 2027 年之前做好入侵台湾的准备。”从那以后发生了什么变化？ “从本质上讲，我希望自己是错的，”戴维森在谈到他的国会证词时说道。 “如果我错了，那就意味着我们向印太司令部建议的事情、美国政府和其他国家政府在过去七年里采取的事情是有效的。而且没有发生战争。” “我主张，从军事意义上来说，五套能力——我认为很重要的投资指南，”戴维森解释道，他现在是国防承包商 AV 的董事会成员。
“美国需要重新考虑其在印太地区的兵力态势和设计——我们在哪里、我们如何部署、我们轮换什么、这些部队的能力是什么。我们还需要更多样化、更大规模的联合部队火力，这意味着进攻性火力不仅来自海上，还来自陆地和空中。”这位海军上将补充道：“你现在肯定会看到这种情况正在发生，包括部署和导弹部署、海军陆战队、陆军在菲律宾和第一岛链沿线的部署。” “这很有帮助。”第 1 多域特遣部队远程火力营第 3 野战炮兵团第 5 营查理炮台的中程能力 (MRC) 发射器抵达菲律宾吕宋岛北部战区，这是该能力首次部署到战区的一部分

【原文 English Original】
The man whose congressional testimony five years ago led to what’s known as the “Davidson Window” for China being capable of launching a credible invasion of Taiwan by 2027 is offering some insights into what he is thinking now that the date is drawing near. Philip Davidson – the admiral who led U.S. forces in the Pacific at the time – said on a podcast released Friday that several developments have taken place since he retired in 2021 that could change his projection. However, the former commander of U.S. Indo-Pacific Command (now Pacific Command or PACOM) told the Why Should We Care About the Indo-Pacific? podcast he still sees reasons for concern. In particular, he urged the U.S. to deliver military aid to Taiwan before an invasion to better deter China from acting. Chinese forces practice a beach landing. (PLA) Davidson’s statements were delivered as China has been steadily increasing military exercises around Taiwan , which it considers a breakaway province that it will someday bring back under its control. Before getting into what Davidson told podcasters Ray Powell, founder and executive director of the SeaLight Foundation , and Jim Carouso, a senior advisor at BowerGroupAsia , let’s recall what Davidson told the Senate Armed Services Committee on March 9, 2021. “I worry that they are accelerating their ambitions to supplant the United States, and our leadership role in the rules-based international order, which they have long said that they want to do that by 2050, I am worried about them moving that target closer,” Davidson said of China. “Taiwan is clearly one of their ambitions before then, and I think the threat is manifest during this decade, in fact, in the next six years.” Philip Davidson when he was a Navy admiral and commander of U.S. Indo-Pacific Command. (USN) The assessment of the so-called “Davidson Window” was backed two years later by the Central Intelligence Agency (CIA). “President Xi has instructed the PLA [People’s Liberation Army], the Chinese military leadership, to be ready by 2027 to invade Taiwan,” then-CIA Director Bill Burns stated . What’s Changed Since Then? “At the heart of it, I’m hoping to be wrong,” said Davidson about his congressional testimony. “If I’m wrong, that means the things we recommended from Indo-Pacific Command, the things that the United States government and other governments have undertaken over the last seven years, have been effective. And there hasn’t been war.” “I advocated for, just in the military sense, five capability sets – investment guidelines that I thought were important to do,” explained Davidson, now on the board of directors at defense contractor AV . “The United States needed to rethink its force posture and design in the region, in the Indo-Pacific – where we are, how we deployed, what we rotated through, what the capabilities of those sets were. We also needed more diverse and a larger set of joint force fires, meaning offensive fires, not just from the sea, but from land and air domain.” “You’re certainly seeing that play out right now, with deployments and missile deployments, with Marine formations , Army formations in the Philippines and along the First Island Chain,” the admiral added. “That has been a help.” Mid-Range Capability (MRC) Launcher from Charlie Battery, 5th Battalion, 3rd Field Artillery Regiment, Long Range Fires Battalion, 1st Multi-Domain Task Force arrives as part of the capability’s first deployment into theater on Northern Luzon, Philippines, April 8, 2024. The MRC deployment aims to enhance Philippine maritime defense capabilities, while bolstering interoperability and readiness within the U.S.-Philippine Alliance. (U.S. Army) U.S. Army In addition, Davidson noted that the U.S. “needed to improve our exercises, our experimentation, and our innovation in the region. We have deepened the relationship with Japan and Australia in the Keen series of exercises over the last five years, and in a way that was kind of unheard of in my day, which I think is a profound improvement.” The Keen Sword training exercise occurred last month and saw about “45,000 Japan Self-Defense Force, 11,000 U.S. service members and forces from Australia, Canada, France, Germany, the Netherlands, New Zealand and the Philippines…participating alongside observers from the Republic of Korea and the United Kingdom,” according to the U.S. Navy. A Japan Maritime Self-Defense Force Landing Craft Air Cushion (LCAC) hovercraft assigned to Amphibious Warfare Squadron One, Amphibious and Mine Warfare Group, coasts into the harbor at Marine Corps Air Station Iwakuni, Japan, Oct. 28, 2026, during Keen Sword. (U.S. Marine Corps photo by Lance Cpl. Donald Dugger) Lance Cpl. Donald Dugger Japan taking a more assertive security posture toward China has been a huge change from when he was in command, Davidson noted. “Japan absolutely has come forward, they reissued their national security strategy in December of [2022], and there were a number of alliance announcements made in January of [2023],” he explained.  The Japanese doubled their investment in defense from 1% to 2% of its GDP, Davidson highlighted. Japan also “established space [and] cyber forces, instilled the cybersecurity principles and laws that would be necessary to deepen our relationship in a classified way. And this is almost unknown to anybody in America. Completely redistributed and reset their ground formations and air formations in the Southwest Island chain, between Okinawa and along the Ryukyu chain.” “Most importantly, they identified China as the strategic threat in the region,” Davidson proffered. “And in the alliance announcement in January of [2023] with us, said that our interests have converged in this regard.” A Japan Air Self-Defense Force F-15 fighter performs during the Komatsu Air Festival on September 26, 2026 in Komatsu, Japan. (Photo by Zhang Hui/VCG via Getty Images) VCG Taiwan too has made some needed improvements in its approach to defending itself since he retired, Davidson explained. “You have to be encouraged by Taiwan’s actions taken since then,” he stated. “They expanded the conscription timeline from just a few months to a year of service. They have done an enormous amount of work in their national emergency preparedness realm.” Davidson also credited Adm. Lee Hsi-min, chief of the Taiwanese Armed Forces general staff from 2017 to 2019, for developing the Overall Defense Concept (ODC). Lee envisioned a mix of mines, uncrewed aerial systems (UAS), uncrewed surface vehicles (USVs), uncrewed underwater vehicles (UUVs), crewed coastal defense boats, land-based mobile short- and medium-range precision munitions, precision-guided multiple launch rocket systems, man portable air defense systems (MANPADS), anti-armor rocket systems and electronic warfare measures to counter the PLA’s overwhelming advantages in aviation and naval assets and long-range fires. Taiwan sits about 130 miles east of China. (Google Earth) “He said, ‘We really have to develop the kind of asymmetric capabilities that help round out our lack of capacity vis-a-vis its relationship with the People’s Republic of China, and make sure that we have a strategic and operational design that can kill in the littoral and along the landing beaches and things like that,’” Davidson pointed out. “They’ve been getting after autonomy. They’ve been getting after robotics and drones and sensing.” In 2025, Taiwan revealed a new drone boat, or uncrewed surface vessel (USV), the Endeavor Manta, said to be the first of its kind for the Republic of China Navy (ROCN). However, as we have frequently pointed out , Taiwan is still far behind where it needs to be in many of these areas, but especially uncrewed systems . In addition, Davidson said growing relations with the Philippines and Australia are also helping. Australia signed the Australia–United Kingdom–United States security partnership (AUKUS) in September 2021, months after Davidson retired. AUKUS calls for the United States and Britain to share nuclear-submarine technology with Australia. A rendering of the future SSN-AUKUS design. (U.K. Ministry of Defense) “So over the span of the last six years since March 9 of 2021, you’ve seen a lot of change that I think has reinforced the deterrence of the West here, and I think that’s important to note,” Davidson stated. What Still Needs To Change Despite seeing the U.S. and its allies better prepared to defend against a Chinese invasion of Taiwan, Davidson said he is concerned that the U.S. is not moving fast enough to provide promised military aid. “I would like to see the $14 billion in committed [Foreign Military Sales] to Taiwan move over there in the next few months or a year,” Davidson stated. Approval of the package, which is a major point of controversy with China, has been stalled, Taiwan’s Defense Minister Wellington Koo said in September . The minister’s remarks “come as concerns mount that President Donald Trump could halt arms sales to Taiwan. China has pressed Washington to halt the arms sales, most prominently during a May summit in Beijing between Trump and China’s President Xi Jinping,” The Associated Press noted . “The United States paused the $14 billion arms deal after that meeting.” The package “largely consists of [Patriot] PAC-3 and NASAMS [ National Advanced Surface-to-Air Missile System ] air defense missiles,” Reuters reported . However, another huge factor beyond tensions with China is the U.S. supply of these air defense munitions, which has been drastically affected by the current and recent Middle East conflicts . Donations to Ukraine have also eaten into U.S. stocks. The lack of sufficient magazine depth is an issue that TWZ has raised frequently for years, and especially in regard to America’s air and missile defenses , in particular. Commitments for deliveries to 20 other nations and an overall insatiable global demand for interceptors due to numerous destabilizing events has put further strain on the supply of American interceptors. All this is also straining the ability of industry to provide enough capacity. For instance, current PAC-3 MSE production “is around the baseline rate of 650 interceptors per year, with half the deliveries going to the United States and the rest to allies and partners,” according to a report from the Center for Strategic and International Studies (CSIS). The Pentagon is trying to boost production. Under a contract with the Pentagon inked in January , Lockheed Martin is committed to raising annual Patriot output to 2,000 interceptors. A Patriot PAC-3 interceptor (Lockheed Martin) In addition to wanting to see the arms package pushed forward, Davidson warned about China’s information warfare capabilities. “The one thing that has really jumped out at me that was a problem, certainly, when I was the Indo-Pacific commander, but it’s worse now, is the information environment,” Davidson posited. “China is working to undermine the democratic processes in Taiwan. They’re working to undermine any U.S. citizens’ confidence in business leadership and political leadership and military leadership. They’re exploiting accidents or difficulties that someone might be having to flood social networks, and it’s happening not just from China, but from Russia and Iran and independent actors elsewhere. “ “It’s really dangerous,” the former commander emphasized. “There’s been some estimations that some of the activity from bots and from propaganda players is accounting for up to 70% of the commentary in social media threads here and there, and that’s a much more difficult place to be.” Davidson said the U.S. needs to step up its own information warfare capabilities. “I think we should be putting as much effort into [the information domain] as we’ve been putting into drones and autonomy and things like that in this day and age,” Davidson stated. Chinese hovercraft land on a beach during training. (PLAN) Davidson did not address some other glaring issues in regard to China’s potential seizure of Taiwan. The biggest being will the U.S. actually respond militarily if a major Chinese exercise suddenly became an actual invasion operation? Would there even be enough time and what about China’s anti-access capabilities that could keep much of America’s combat power at bay during the early stages of such a conflict? Would there even be support for such an intervention operation domestically, especially considering it could be very bloody and it would surely manifest itself here at home? Then, as we mentioned in the piece, there are many areas where Taiwan seems to be moving far too slowly while China’s military force continues to balloon on nearly all fronts. Regardless, it’s nice to hear from the man who inadvertently gave birth to the “Davidson Window” now that this ominous window of vulnerability he predicted a half decade is cracking open. Contact the author: howard@twz.com The post ‘Davidson Window’ Admiral Hopes He Was Wrong On China’s Ability To Take Taiwan By 2027 appeared first on TWZ .

title: Hong Kong NGO urges legislation to restrict children’s social media use after survey finds widespread screen addiction
zh_title: 调查发现屏幕成瘾现象普遍存在后，香港非政府组织敦促立法限制儿童使用社交媒体
summary: 最近的一项调查发现低收入家庭的青少年普遍存在屏幕成瘾现象，香港一家社会服务慈善机构呼吁立法限制儿童使用社交媒体。 SoCO holds a press conference on November 8, 2026 on electronic device use among children from low-income families.照片：提供。为弱势社区服务的非政府组织社区组织协会 (SoCO) 周日表示，29.9% 的低收入家庭儿童对电子设备“上瘾”。 Meanwhile, 61.4 per cent reported “tired eyes” after usi
content:
最近的一项调查发现低收入家庭的青少年普遍存在屏幕成瘾现象，香港一家社会服务慈善机构呼吁立法限制儿童使用社交媒体。 SoCO 于 2026 年 11 月 8 日召开新闻发布会，讨论低收入家庭儿童的电子设备使用情况。照片：提供。为弱势社区服务的非政府组织社区组织协会 (SoCO) 周日表示，29.9% 的低收入家庭儿童对电子设备“上瘾”。与此同时，SoCO 在新闻发布会上表示，61.4% 的人表示在使用电子设备后“眼睛疲劳”，40% 的人表示“睡眠受到影响”，约 30% 的人表示“注意力不集中”。该调查从2月到7月采访了254名儿童，其中约67%是小学生，约25%是中学生。他们来自家庭月收入中位数为14,000港元的家庭。调查发现，电子设备已成为这些家庭的必需品，孩子们使用智能手机、平板电脑和电脑做作业、看电影、玩网络游戏以及通过社交媒体平台与同龄人联系。受访儿童平均每天使用电子设备的时间为6小时11分钟，其中娱乐使用时间占比最高，超过两个半小时。
52%的儿童每天在电子设备上娱乐的时间为两个小时或以上，而32.3%的儿童每天在电子设备上娱乐的时间为三个小时或以上。65%的儿童表示曾因使用电子设备娱乐而与父母发生争执。 Social media apps on a smartphone.照片：Tracy Le Blanc/Pexels。 SoCO 呼吁立法限制儿童使用社交媒体，建议政府考虑禁止 11 岁以下儿童使用社交媒体。调查显示，80%的儿童同意香港应通过立法规范儿童和青少年使用电子设备。与此同时，47.6%的人支持“规定儿童可以使用社交媒体的年龄”。该社会服务组织表示，由于低收入父母忙于工作和家务，他们中的许多人倾向于让孩子使用电子设备，这些设备提供免费的视频和游戏供娱乐。 7 月，政府在回应立法者时表示，没有计划立法限制青少年社交媒体。学校智能手机使用指引 该非政府组织还敦促教育局出台智能手机在学校使用指引，并加强数码素养教育，帮助儿童更负责任地使用电子设备。 “理想情况下，应该完全禁止使用手机，并且只在放学后归还。
否则，学校至少应该禁止在上课期间使用智能手机，提供安全的存储设施，允许学生在紧急情况下与家人联系，并在午休和放学后提供灵活的安排。” 2015/16 年，该数字低于 50%。

【原文 English Original】
A Hong Kong social services charity has called for legislation to restrict social media use among children after a recent survey found widespread screen addiction among youths from low-income families. SoCO holds a press conference on November 8, 2026 on electronic device use among children from low-income families. Photo: Supplied. The Society for Community Organization (SoCO), an NGO serving disadvantaged communities, said on Sunday that 29.9 per cent of children from low-income families reported being “addicted” to electronic devices. Meanwhile, 61.4 per cent reported “tired eyes” after using electronic devices, 40 per cent said their “sleep was affected,” and around 30 per cent reported “a lack of concentration,” SoCO said during a press conference. The survey interviewed 254 children from February to July, with around 67 per cent primary school students and around 25 per cent secondary school students. They came from families with a median monthly household income of HK$14,000. The survey found that electronic devices had become necessities in those families, as children used smartphones, tablets and computers for doing homework, watching films, playing online games and connecting with peers through social media platforms. The children interviewed spent an average of six hours and 11 minutes on electronic devices per day, with entertainment use accounting for the highest portion at over two and a half hours. Fifty-two per cent of children spent two hours or more per day on screens for entertainment, while 32.3 per cent spent three hours or more. Sixty-five per cent of children reported having argued with their parents over using electronic devices for entertainment. Social media apps on a smartphone. Photo: Tracy Le Blanc/Pexels. SoCO called for legislation to impose restrictions on children’s social media use, suggesting that the government consider banning social media use for those under 11 years old. According to its survey, 80 per cent of children agreed that Hong Kong should regulate children’s and youths’ use of electronic devices through legislation. Meanwhile, 47.6 per cent supported “regulating the age at which children can use social media.” The social services organisation said that as low-income parents were fully occupied by work and chores, many of them tended to allow their children to use electronic devices, which provide free videos and games for entertainment. In July, the government said in response to a lawmaker that it had no plans to legislate social media restrictions for adolescents. Guidelines for smartphone use in schools The NGO also urged the Education Bureau to introduce guidelines for smartphone use in schools and to enhance digital literacy education to help children use electronic devices more responsibly. “Ideally, mobile phones should be banned altogether and only returned after school. Otherwise, schools should at least prohibit smartphone use during class hours, provide secure storage facilities, allow students to contact their families in emergencies, and offer flexible arrangements during lunch breaks and after school,” SoCO said in a Chinese-language statement. Hong Kong’s children are spending increasingly more time on screens for entertainment. According to government reports on student health, over 60 per cent of children spent two hours or more on screens for entertainment per day in the 2024/25 school year, a significant rise from 2015/16, when the figure was below 50 per cent. The Department of Health recommends that primary school students spend less than two hours daily on screens for entertainment.

title: Four more mainland Chinese universities to admit Hong Kong students on DSE results from 2027
zh_title: 2027年起又有四所内地大学将凭DSE成绩录取香港学生
summary: 自2027年起，香港学生可凭DSE成绩申请入学的计划又增加了四所内地高等教育机构，使参与学校总数达到169所。 浙江财经大学。图片：浙江财经大学 中国教育部周一宣布，2027/28学年参与内地高等学校招收香港学生的院校将增至169所。机构遍布全国21个省份
content:
自2027年起，香港学生可凭DSE成绩申请入学的计划又增加了四所内地高等教育机构，使参与学校总数达到169所。 浙江财经大学。图片：浙江财经大学 中国教育部周一宣布，2027/28学年参与内地高等学校招收香港学生的院校将增至169所。机构遍布全国21个省市及内蒙古、广西壮族自治区。新加入的四所院校分别是浙江财经大学、丽水大学、广州新华大学和福耀科技大学。该计划接受香港中学文凭（DSE）考试成绩，并豁免香港学生参加中国的统一入学考试——这是一种专为香港、澳门和台湾学生设计的特殊大学入学考试，而不是众所周知的竞争激烈的国家考试（即高考）。教育局发言人表示，这些内地院校提供多元化课程，鼓励香港学生考虑接受高等教育。
发言人在一份声明中表示：“我们鼓励香港学生通过招生计划到内地升学，抓住机会了解国家最新的社会、经济和文化状况，为自己的未来发展做好规划。”档案照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。该计划还设有校长提名机制，允许中学校长提名最多八名学生。在此轨道下，申请人必须在公民身份和社会发展方面至少取得“达标”成绩，并且在三个核心科目（中文、英语和数学）中的总分至少达到八分，并且任何科目的分数不得低于二分。学生可以在12月1日至31日期间在线申请，并在明年1月10日前确认申请。 1月31日前缴纳港币460元申请费。由教育部港澳台办公室、大学生事务司和教育局联合主办的2027/28内地高等教育博览会将于12月5日至6日举行。香港一直鼓励本地学生到内地升学，同时增加大学招收非本地学生，其中不少来自内地。
自2026/27学年起，本市公立大学自资课程的非本地学生招生限额已提高至本地学生名额的50%。

【原文 English Original】
Four more mainland higher education institutions have been added to a scheme allowing Hong Kong students to seek admission based on their DSE results from 2027, bringing the total number of participating schools to 169. Zhejiang University of Finance & Economics. Photo: Zhejiang University of Finance & Economics China’s Ministry of Education announced on Monday that the number of institutions participating in the Scheme for Admission of Hong Kong Students to Mainland Higher Education Institutions will increase to 169 for the 2027/28 academic year. The institutions are located in 21 provinces or municipalities and the autonomous regions of Inner Mongolia and Guangxi Zhuang. The four newly participating institutions are Zhejiang University of Finance and Economics, Lishui University, Guangzhou Xinhua University and Fuyao University of Science and Technology. The scheme accepts the Hong Kong Diploma of Secondary Education (DSE) exam results and exempts Hong Kong students from taking China’s joint entrance examination – a special university entrance exam designed for students from Hong Kong, Macau and Taiwan as opposed to the notoriously competitive national exam, known as the Gaokao. A spokesperson for the Education Bureau (EDB) said these mainland institutions offered diverse programmes and encouraged Hong Kong students to consider them for higher education. “We encourage Hong Kong students to pursue further studies on the Chinese Mainland through the Admission Scheme and seize the opportunity to learn about the country’s latest social, economic and cultural landscape, and plan ahead for their future development,” the spokesperson said in a statement. Secondary school students in Hong Kong. File photo: Kyle Lam/ HKFP. The scheme also features a principal nomination mechanism allowing secondary school principals to nominate up to eight students. Under this track, applicants must achieve at least an “attained” grade in Citizenship and Social Development and a minimum total score of eight across the three core subjects – Chinese Language, English Language and Mathematics – with no score below two in any of those subjects. Students can apply online from December 1 to 31 and confirm their application before January 10 next year. They should pay an application fee of HK$460 by January 31. The Mainland Higher Education Expo 2027/28, jointly organised by the Office of Hong Kong, Macao and Taiwan Affairs and the Department of College Students Affairs of the Ministry of Education, and the EDB, will be held on December 5 and 6. Hong Kong has been encouraging local students to study in mainland China while increasing the intake of non-local students at its universities, many of whom come from the mainland. Starting from the 2026/27 academic year, the enrolment limit for non-local students in self-financing programmes at the city’s publicly funded universities has been raised to 50 per cent of local student places.

title: Taiwan lawmaker wanted by police in China closes gap in race for Taipei mayor
zh_title: 被中国警方通缉的台湾议员缩小台北市长竞选差距
summary: 一名被中国警方通缉的台湾议员正在竞选台北市市长，这场竞选在国民党的中心地带进行，这场竞选出人意料地势均力敌，国民党倾向于与北京建立更密切的关系。 2026 年 11 月 15 日，台湾总统赖清德（左）和民进党台北市市长候选人沉宝阳（又名普马沉）在台北竞选期间举起礼仪剑。照片：郑宇辰/法新社。夜市、寺庙和车队正在为 11 月 28 日选举进行竞选活动，选举将决定市长、地方法官和其他职位的竞选
content:
一名被中国警方通缉的台湾议员正在竞选台北市市长，这场竞选在国民党的中心地带进行，这场竞选出人意料地势均力敌，国民党倾向于与北京建立更密切的关系。 2026 年 11 月 15 日，台湾总统赖清德（左）和民进党台北市市长候选人沉宝阳（又名普马沉）在台北竞选期间举起礼仪剑。照片：郑宇辰/法新社。夜市、寺庙和车队正在为 11 月 28 日的选举进行竞选活动，该选举将决定全岛民主政体的市长、地方法官和其他职位的竞选。 2022 年，国民党赢得了台湾 22 个市县中的 14 个席位（包括台北），而赖清德领导的民进党则获得了 5 个席位。 44 岁的台北民进党候选人普马·沉 (Puma Shen) 正在寻求推翻长期以来被认为是安全的国民党职位，成为近 30 年来第一位民进党首都市长。沉在 2024 年成为立法委员，他几乎没有机会击败 47 岁的国民党现任议员蒋万安，后者被视为台湾历史最悠久的政党的后起之秀和未来的总统候选人。但最近的选民调查显示，沉正接近甚至略微领先蒋介石。
另请参阅：台湾指控香港居民雇佣 4 名人员监视批评中国的议员。沉在台湾立法院附近的办公室接受法新社采访时表示，“我始终相信自己能够获胜”。沉在台湾议会附近的办公室接受法新社采访时表示，他一直直言不讳地谈论中国的影响力和虚假信息。沉因涉嫌犯罪“分裂活动”正在接受中国警方的调查，并被禁止入境。沉说，他在选民中越来越受欢迎——他的竞选团队将其称为“洋流”，这是对他名字最后一个字符的戏剧——部分原因是他愿意回答他们的问题。 “我认为这就是民主的本质，”沉说，他利用演讲台和社交媒体直接与当地人接触。蒋的团队拒绝了法新社采访市长的请求。上海市市长龚正与台北市长蒋万安在2023上海台北城市论坛上握手。照片：台北市政府。前国民党顾问曾伟业表示，两位候选人的性格和政治风格截然不同。他说，蒋是一位“正派的政治家”，但“在表达自己的观点时非常保守”，而沉则更“直言不讳”，更适合社交媒体。北京关注的选民调查还显示，台湾最大城市、国民党另一个据点新北市的市长竞选可能会出现重大意外。
在2028年总统选举之前，失去台北和新北市对国民党来说将是一个打击，届时国民党将寻求阻止民进党获得第四个任期。赖政府中的一些人担心，国民党在这两个重要城市的失利可能会让与该党关系密切、关注选举的中国领导人感到尴尬。中国国家主席习近平今年四月会见了国民党主席郑丽媛，她是十年来第一位访问中国的国民党领导人，这被视为对她作为党主席的认可。国民党主席郑立文于 2026 年 4 月会见中国领导人习近平。照片：中国共产党。民进党在台北和新北市的胜利可能对北京来说“看起来非常令人担忧”，因为这将表明该党可以获得以前被视为国民党轻松获胜的席位。

【原文 English Original】
A Taiwanese lawmaker wanted by police in China is running for Taipei mayor in an unexpectedly close race in the heartland of the Kuomintang party, which favours closer ties with Beijing. Taiwan’s President Lai Ching-te (L) and Taipei mayoral candidate Shen Pao-yang, also known as Puma Shen, of the Democratic Progressive Party (DPP) raise a ceremonial sword during an election campaign in Taipei on November 15, 2026. Photo: Cheng Yu-chen/AFP. Campaigning in night markets, temples and motorcades is underway for the November 28 elections that will decide races for mayors, magistrates and other posts across the island democracy. The Kuomintang party (KMT) won 14 of Taiwan’s 22 cities and counties — including Taipei — in a huge victory in 2022, while President Lai Ching-te’s Democratic Progressive Party (DPP) secured five seats. Puma Shen, the 44-year-old DPP candidate in Taipei, is seeking to flip what has long been considered a safe KMT post and become the first DPP mayor of the capital in nearly 30 years. Shen, who became a lawmaker in 2024, had been given little chance of beating KMT incumbent Chiang Wan-an, 47, who is seen as a rising star and future presidential candidate for Taiwan’s oldest party. But recent voter surveys show Shen closing in on, or even slightly ahead, of Chiang. See also: Taiwan accuses Hong Kong residents of hiring 4 people to spy on lawmaker critical of China “I always believe I can win,” Shen told AFP in an interview at his office near Taiwan’s parliament, where he has been outspoken about Chinese influence and disinformation. Shen is under investigation by police in China for alleged criminal “separatist activities” and is barred from entering the country. Shen said his growing popularity among voters — which his campaign has dubbed an “Ocean Current”, in a play on the last character of his name — is partly due to his willingness to answer their questions. “I think that’s the essence of democracy,” said Shen, who has used soapboxes and social media to engage directly with locals. Chiang’s team declined AFP’s request for an interview with the mayor. Shanghai mayor Gong Zheng and Taipei mayor Chiang Wan-an shaking hands at the 2023 Shanghai–Taipei City Forum. Photo: Taipei City Government. Albert Tzeng, a former KMT adviser, said the two candidates have very different personalities and political styles. Chiang is a “decent politician” but “very conservative in articulating his view”, while Shen is more “outspoken” and better suited to social media, he said. Beijing watching Voter surveys also show a potential major upset in the mayoral race in New Taipei City, Taiwan’s largest city and another KMT stronghold. Losing Taipei and New Taipei City would be a blow for the KMT ahead of the 2028 presidential election when the party will seek to prevent the DPP from securing a fourth term. Some in Lai’s government worry that KMT losses in the two key cities could embarrass Chinese leaders who have close ties with the party and will be watching the election. Chinese President Xi Jinping met with Kuomintang chairwoman Cheng Li-wun in April, the first KMT leader to visit China in a decade, in what was seen as his endorsement of her as head of the party. KMT chair Cheng Li-wun meets Chinese leader Xi Jinping in April 2026. Photo: Communist Party of China. A DPP victory in Taipei and New Taipei City might “look very concerning” to Beijing because it would show the party can gain seats previously seen as easy wins for the KMT, said Lev Nachman, a political science professor at National Taiwan University. A poor performance by the KMT would also likely increase pressure on Cheng, whose strident pro-Beijing stance has angered many in her own party, to step down. Most KMT candidates have kept their distance from Cheng during their campaigns and after the elections there will be a “very ugly struggle”, Tzeng predicted. “There are many people who believe if Cheng Li-wun stays in power, the KMT will have zero chance in 2028.” Local issues Analysts cautioned that local elections should not be seen as a predictor of how people might vote in the presidential race, with history showing repeatedly that it can be the reverse. “The things they (voters) weigh in local elections differ from what they weigh in national-level elections,” Hsiao Yi-ching, director of the Election Study Center at National Chengchi University, told AFP. “Local elections should be relatively less affected by cross-strait tensions and geopolitical or international political factors.” Shen and Chiang have avoided talking about China during their campaigns, focusing instead on local issues such as urban renewal, transportation, childcare and artificial intelligence. Campaign posters for Chiang Wan-an and Puma Shen. Photo: Chiang Wan-an and Puma Shen, via Facebook.
