Lo Hui-fen, a 67-year-old retiree and supporter of Chiang, said he thought the mayor was “excellent” and had achieved a lot during his first term. “To me, he is like the son next door,” Lo said at a night market where Chiang was holding a campaign event. “He’s very approachable and willing to get things done.” Shen supporter Jamie Cheng, 35, said the DPP candidate made her feel like he was listening. “I can have a formal exchange with him,” Cheng, a digital designer, told AFP at a rally for the opening of Shen’s campaign office. “It feels like my voice is being heard.”

title: Hong Kong police activate facial recognition across AI-enabled CCTV network, as police chief says tools ‘won’t be abused’
zh_title: 香港警方通过人工智能闭路电视网络启动面部识别，警察局长表示工具“不会被滥用”
summary: 香港警务处宣布将于周一在其监控摄像系统中启动面部识别工具。该措施是一项耗资 40 亿港元的扩大人工智能闭路电视网络计划的一部分。 SmartView 摄像头馈送。资料图：香港警务处。警务处处长 Joe Chow 周日告诉 TVB，该技术将在其 SmartView 网络上推广。 “我们所有的调查工具都有制衡的要求，这样就不会被滥用……我们理解很多人可能会担心这一点，所以这是我们的常规做法，”周先生用粤语说道。
content:
香港警务处宣布将于周一在其监控摄像系统中启动面部识别工具。该措施是一项耗资 40 亿港元的扩大人工智能闭路电视网络计划的一部分。 SmartView 摄像头馈送。资料图：香港警务处。警务处处长 Joe Chow 周日告诉 TVB，该技术将在其 SmartView 网络上推广。据香港电台报道，周先生用粤语说：“我们所有的调查工具都有制衡的要求，这样就不会被滥用……我们知道很多人可能会担心这一点，所以这是我们的常规做法。”他补充说，这些工具主要用于处理失踪人员或刑事案件：“该系统不会随便使用——我相信这不是公众所期望的。”周说，他理解公众的担忧，但闭路电视系统已经被用来侦破抢劫案件。旺角的闭路电视摄像机。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。在周六的香港警察学院结业游行上，他表示，部署面部识别功能的目的是为了更好地保护守法居民，并起到威慑犯罪活动的作用。另请参阅：香港警方今年可能在闭路电视摄像机中添加面部识别功能，作为 40 亿港元扩张计划的一部分。当被记者问到口罩或伪装是否会阻碍该系统时，周表示，警方不会透露技术和操作细节。
不过，他补充说，隐蔽方法无法与警方的能力相抗衡。 SmartView系统扩展 自2024年推出以来，SmartView系统已安装在犯罪黑点和人口密集地区，警方声称该系统已帮助破获了1,659起谋杀、伤人和抢劫案件。该政府主导的计划涉及约 5,000 个警察摄像头和 6,000 个第三方源。去年施政报告中提出的第二阶段计划包括安装 20,000 个摄像头，到 2028 年在全市实现 60,000 个摄像头网络。上个月，安全部门负责人 Chris Tang 表示，警方正与私人购物中心讨论将摄像头纳入 SmartView 系统的最后阶段。他没有透露涉及的商场名称。 “我们看到，在一些没有闭路电视的地方，公众不愿意参观，因为那里很危险，人们担心成为犯罪的受害者，”他用粤语说。警方网站指出 SmartView 计划有四个目的，第一个是维护国家安全。它还列出了犯罪的预防、侦查和调查，维护公共秩序和安全，以及防止生命和财产伤害。

【原文 English Original】
The Hong Kong Police Force has announced that it will activate facial recognition tools across its surveillance camera system on Monday. The measure is part of a HK$4 billion plan to expand the AI-enabled CCTV network. SmartView camera feeds. File Photo: HKPF. Police Commissioner Joe Chow told TVB on Sunday that the technology would be rolled out across its SmartView network. “All of our investigation tools have the requirement of check and balance, so that they won’t be abused… We understand that many people may be concerned about this, so it’s our routine practice,” Chow said in Cantonese, according to RTHK. He added that the tools would mostly be used to deal with missing persons or criminal cases: “The system will not be used casually – I believe this is not what the public expects.” Chow said he understood public concerns, but the CCTV system had already been used to solve robbery cases. A CCTV camera in Mong Kok. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. At a Hong Kong Police College passing-out parade on Saturday, he said the deployment of facial recognition features was aimed at better protecting law-abiding residents and acting as a deterrent against criminal activity. See also: Hong Kong police may add facial recognition to CCTV cameras this year as part of HK$4 billion expansion plan When asked by reporters if face masks or disguises could thwart the system, Chow said the force would refrain from disclosing technical and operational details. However, he added that concealment methods would be no match against the capabilities of the police. SmartView system expansion Since its launch in 2024, the SmartView system has been installed across crime blackspots and dense population areas, with the police claiming that it has helped solve 1,659 cases including murder, wounding and robbery. The government-led programme involves around 5,000 police cameras and 6,000 third-party feeds. The second phase of the scheme, laid out in last year’s Policy Address, involves the installation of 20,000 more cameras to achieve a network of 60,000 across the city by 2028. Last month, security chief Chris Tang said the police force was in the final stages of discussion with private shopping centres to bring their cameras into the SmartView system. He did not name the malls involved. “[W]e see that in some places without CCTV, members of the public do not want to visit because they are dangerous and people fear becoming victims of crime,” he said in Cantonese. The police website states four purposes for the SmartView scheme, with the first being safeguarding national security. It also lists the prevention, detection and investigation of crimes, the preservation of public order and safety, and the prevention of injury to life and property.

summary: TWZ 获得了有关海狼级潜艇康涅狄格号在 2021 年在南中国海与水下海山相撞后正在进行维修的新细节。海军一直在考虑大约三年的时间表来建造替换的船首声纳导流罩。最终，仅用了不到一年的时间就建成了。康涅狄格州的总体维修计划已被推迟，我们是第一个报告该船预计要到明年夏天才能恢复使用的人。编者注：这篇报道发表后，Janicki Industries 达成了
content:
TWZ 获得了有关海狼级潜艇康涅狄格号在 2021 年在南中国海与水下海山相撞后正在进行维修的新细节。海军一直在考虑大约三年的时间表来建造替换的船首声纳导流罩。最终，仅用了不到一年的时间就建成了。康涅狄格州的总体维修计划已被推迟，我们是第一个报告该船预计要到明年夏天才能恢复使用的人。编者注：这篇报道发表后，Janicki Industries 联系我们，要求在进行额外审查时删除圆顶的图像。出于礼貌，我们同意了，如果完全获得批准，我们将重新发布它。 Janicki Industries 今天告诉我们，该公司在大约 10 个月内生产出了新型船首声纳导流罩，并于 2024 年交付给海军。据其网站称，Janicki 拥有为美国核潜艇项目生产“声纳罩和精密加工硬件”的历史。它还支持各种备受瞩目的航空航天项目，包括 B-21 袭击者轰炸机和 F-35 联合攻击战斗机。根据一份经过大量编辑的海军事故报告，康涅狄格号的船头在五年前的碰撞事件发生后，最初至少在某种程度上仍然保持着连接状态。然而，当潜艇一瘸一拐地驶向关岛时，整个船首结构随后断裂。
随后，这艘船驶往加利福尼亚州圣地亚哥，然后前往华盛顿州的普吉特海湾海军造船厂和中间维护设施 (PSNS-IMF)，此后一直待在那里。 2023 年，在普吉特湾海军造船厂和中间维护设施中看到的康涅狄格号航空母舰，其船首圆顶明显缺失。美国海军“普吉特海湾海军造船厂和国际货币基金组织（中间维护设施）需要按照船的计划，在其后面没有生产线的情况下安装一个精密的替换圆顶，”贾尼基在撰写本文时还在其网站上表示。 “Janicki 比次佳选择快了 24 个月，因为工作所需的一切都集中在一个屋檐下：适合半球的 5 轴铣床、证明这一点的计量方法以及形成双曲板的 1,000 吨压力机。”本文顶部的部分图片和下面的完整图片显示了 Janicki 专有的五轴铣床在圆顶上工作的情况。海狼级潜艇艏声纳导流罩的尺寸和复杂性怎么强调都不为过。这些船上的船首声纳阵列直径为 24 英尺。圆顶本身的结构必须按照非常严格的规格建造，以使声纳系统正常工作。海狼级潜艇上的艏声纳阵列，其艏穹顶被拆除。公共领域 过去的五角大楼预算文件和国会拨款法案已经强调了更换康涅狄格州弓形声纳罩的预期成本和复杂性。
2021 年，立法者批准了 1000 万美元专门用于圆顶的资金，以及 4000 万美元用于其他“紧急维修”。全部维修费用仍不得而知，但预计将远高于 5000 万美元。 在 2024 年发布的 2025 财年预算提案中，海军还概述了购买额外船首圆顶的计划，以防其任何一艘“海狼”级潜艇再次遭受类似的严重事故。 “海狼级潜艇的保障战略不包括提供替换潜艇

【原文 English Original】
TWZ has obtained new details about the ongoing repairs to the Seawolf class submarine USS Connecticut following collision with an underwater seamount in the South China Sea in 2021. The Navy had been looking at a roughly three-year timeline for the construction of a replacement bow sonar dome. In the end, it took just under a year for it to be built. The overall schedule for repairs to Connecticut has suffered delays, and we were the first to report that the boat is now not expected to return to service until next summer. Editor’s note: After this story was published, Janicki Industries reached out to us to ask that the image of the dome be taken down while an additional review is conducted. Out of courtesy, we agreed, and we will repost it if and when it is fully approved. Janicki Industries produced the new bow sonar dome in approximately 10 months and delivered it to the Navy in 2024, the company told us today. Janicki has a history of producing “sonar domes and precision machined hardware” for U.S. nuclear submarine programs, according to its website . It has also supported various high-profile aerospace programs, including the B-21 Raider bomber and F-35 Joint Strike Fighter . Connecticut ’s bow had initially remained attached, at least to some degree, following the collision five years ago, according to a heavily redacted Navy report on the accident . However, the entire bow structure subsequently broke away as the submarine limped to Guam . The boat then sailed to San Diego, California , and then to the Puget Sound Naval Shipyard & Intermediate Maintenance Facility (PSNS-IMF) in Washington State, where it has been ever since. USS Connecticut seen at the Puget Sound Naval Shipyard & Intermediate Maintenance Facility in 2023 with its bow dome prominently missing. USN “Puget Sound Naval Shipyard & IMF [Intermediate Maintenance Facility] needed a precision replacement dome with no production line behind it, on the boat’s schedule,” Janicki also says on its website at the time of writing . “Janicki delivered it 24 months faster than the next-best option because everything the job needed sits under one roof: 5-axis mills that fit a hemisphere, the metrology to prove it, and the 1,000-ton press that forms double-curved plate.” The picture seen in part at the top of this story and in full below shows one of Janicki’s proprietary five-axis milling machines at work on the dome. The size and complexity of the bow sonar dome on Seawolf class submarines cannot be overstated. The bow sonar arrays on these boats is 24 feet in diameter. The structure of the dome itself has to be built to very exacting specifications for the sonar system to work properly. A look at the bow sonar array on a Seawolf class submarine with its bow dome removed. Public Domain Past Pentagon budget documents and appropriations bills from Congress had already highlighted the expected costs and complexities of replacing Connecticut ’s bow sonar dome. In 2021, lawmakers approved $10 million in funding specifically for the dome, as well as $40 million for other “emergent repairs.” The full repair bill is still unknown, but is expected to be far steeper than just $50 million. In its Fiscal Year 2025 budget proposal , released in 2024, the Navy also outlined plans to acquire an additional bow dome in case any of its Seawolf class submarines suffered another similarly severe mishap. “The Seawolf Class submarines sustainment strategy did not include the provisioning of replacement bow domes; therefore, no replacement bow domes for these in-service submarines are within the Navy’s inventory,” the budget documents explained. “This program would procure one Seawolf Class bow dome for use in the event replacement is required. Funds in FY25 are to purchase a bow dome which has a three plus year lead time.” Note here the mention of a lead time of at least three years, which is in line with Janicki’s statement that the “next-best option” would have taken two years more to do this work. As TWZ has highlighted in years of reporting now, repairs to Connecticut , in general, were always set to be challenging and costly due to the small size of the Seawolf class and the design being long out of production. The Navy originally planned to acquire 29 of these boats, but ultimately bought just three as a result of post-Cold War drawdowns. In addition, shrinking the program of record so severely caused the unit price of each one to rise substantially, just over $10 billion in 2025 dollars. At the time of writing, they are still the most costly attack submarines ever built. The last of the Seawolf class submarines, the highly secretive USS Jimmy Carter , which entered service in 2005, is also a heavily modified sub-type optimized for underwater espionage missions . USS Connecticut at sea in 2009. USN It is also worth noting that the U.S. Navy, as well as some of its foreign counterparts , have repaired similarly severe damage to submarines by cannibalizing entire sections from decommissioned boats in the same class. However, this is not an option given the size of the Seawolf class and the still very high demand for them operationally . The core design offers advanced capabilities that make even USS Seawolf and USS Connecticut especially well suited to a variety of specialized tasks . This is clearly why the Navy has continued to invest so much in returning Connecticut to the fleet. As mentioned, repairs to Connecticut are now not expected to be finished until sometime in the summer of next year. This is the latest in a succession of schedule slips in recent years. The original goal had been for the boat to be back in service by September 2025. “The Navy’s target completion date for the availability is the summer of 2027. PSNS & IMF is dedicated to executing this work with the highest standards of safety, technical accuracy, and craftsmanship to ensure the ship returns to the fleet ready to take its place at the tip of the spear in defense of our nation’s interests,” a Navy official told TWZ in September. “Current work consists of structural and systems restoration and required lifecycle maintenance.” Earlier in the year, the Navy also revealed that it is now planning on sending Connecticut into retirement in 2031. This means the submarine has just four more years of service ahead of it if the current repair schedule holds. The Navy does have plans to acquire a new class of nuclear attack submarines, currently referred to as SSN(X). In the past, the service has described those future boats as more of a direct successor to the Seawolf class than the versions of the Virginia class it is buying now. A picture of the first-in-class USS Seawolf . USN “The analytical conclusion was unequivocal: to dominate high-end peer threats in the middle of this century, a clean sheet design is required. The Virginia class is a fantastic, unmatched world-class warship, and it will remain the backbone of our attack fleet for decades,” Navy Rear Adm. Andrew Miller said at the Naval Submarine League’s main annual conference last week, per USNI News . “As adversary capabilities evolve, we require expanded payload capacity, greater electrical and hydrodynamic margins and unprecedented architectural flexibility that simply cannot be backfitted into an existing hull form.” Miller is currently the head of the Undersea Warfare Division with the Office of the Chief of Naval Operations. In terms of desired key capabilities for SSN(X), the Navy wants “first, higher flank speed and tactical control speed. Two, improved operational availability. Three, decisive lethality. Four, superior stealth and layered survivability, and finally organic robotic and autonomous systems hosting and command and control,” Miller added. “We are redefining the role of the submarine from a standalone hunter-killer to a capital mothership. By launching uncrewed systems directly from submarine torpedo tubes and integrating unmanned [robotic] vehicles into our battle plans, we dramatically expand the tactical reach of our manned fleet.” The first SSN(X) submarines are not expected to begin entering service until the mid-2040s, at the earliest. The Navy will continue acquiring Virginia class submarines in the interim. This includes stretched Block IV and V versions with Virginia Payload Modules (VPM) that will now be categorized as guided-missile types (SSGN). There will also be a one-of-a-kind seabed warfare version of the Virginia , which could well take over for the USS Jimmy Carter. A briefing slide from General Dynamics Electric Boat detailing existing and future planned subvariants of the Virginia class nuclear submarine. The Block VI and V types have now been reclassified as nuclear-powered guided missile submarines (SSGN) rather than nuclear-powered attack submarines (SSN). General Dynamics Electric Boat When it comes to USS Connecticut , if there are no further delays, the fully repaired submarine with its new bow sonar dome should be back in service by the middle of next year. Contact the author: joe@twz.com The post New Bow Sonar Dome For Heavily Damaged Submarine USS Connecticut Seen For The First Time (Updated) appeared first on TWZ .

title: The Future of AI Is Not China
zh_title: 人工智能的未来不是中国
summary: 青少年科技神童内森·陈 (Nathan Chen) 是 Moonshot AI 的主要创新者，Moonshot AI 是中国几家顶级实验室之一，这在硅谷引发了人们对中国在人工智能霸主竞赛中取得进展的担忧。但上个月，陈在 X 上发帖表示，他已经离开了这家总部位于北京的公司。他现在就职于 Discovery Loop，这是一家位于帕洛阿尔托的新人工智能初创公司，拥有越来越稳定的知名人才。也许陈意识到人工智能领域最令人兴奋的进步并没有发生在中国——尽管该技术在美国的推出最近看起来比以往任何时候都更加麻烦。新电子
content:
青少年科技神童内森·陈 (Nathan Chen) 是 Moonshot AI 的主要创新者，Moonshot AI 是中国几家顶级实验室之一，这在硅谷引发了人们对中国在人工智能霸主竞赛中取得进展的担忧。但上个月，陈在 X 上发帖表示，他已经离开了这家总部位于北京的公司。他现在就职于 Discovery Loop，这是一家位于帕洛阿尔托的新人工智能初创公司，拥有越来越稳定的知名人才。也许陈意识到人工智能领域最令人兴奋的进步并没有发生在中国——尽管该技术在美国的推出最近看起来比以往任何时候都更加麻烦。新获得权力的民主党人在部分程度上由于公众对数据中心的反对而迎来了中期胜利，他们呼吁控制建设计划。英伟达（Nvidia）是一家美国芯片制造商，几乎凭借一己之力推动了人工智能的繁荣，其性丑闻，也可能是间谍丑闻，导致该公司前首席执行官黄仁勋丢掉了工作；引发美国金融市场动荡；并使整个人工智能经济陷入危机。但中国似乎仍然落后。中国人工智能公司缺乏所需的芯片——黄的倒台很可能会使这个问题变得更糟——而且它们无法筹集足够的资金来与富有的美国竞争对手竞争。
公众对这种可能会扼杀就业的技术的抵制似乎正在增长，而痴迷于安全的共产党一直看好人工智能解决中国日益严峻的经济挑战的潜力，最近似乎对人工智能可能对党的权力控制构成的威胁持谨慎态度。这种态度转变可能会进一步阻碍人工智能在中国的进步。新兴技术的支持者认为，人工智能将带来社会效益——提高经济生产力，快速推动科学进步，并增强军事能力。中国领导人宣称这项技术对于国家的持续崛起至关重要，而美国的科技高管和国家安全专家则将人工智能的追求视为一场争夺技术主导地位的生存竞赛，一场两国之间赢家通吃的竞争，将决定全球力量平衡。一些分析人士质疑人工智能的地缘政治是否完全是零和博弈，但如果人工智能的进步最终确实为最能利用这些工具的国家带来决定性的战略优势，那么中国领导人应该感到担忧。 Anthropic 定于本周进行的首次公开募股，展示了美国公司所享有的、而其中国竞争对手只能梦想的获得资本的方式。 Anthropic 预计将通过在纳斯达克首次亮相以及向包括谷歌和微软在内的投资者直接出售股票筹集超过 900 亿美元的资金。
相比之下，中国初创企业再爱科技 (Z.ai) 作为中国第一家在香港证券交易所上市的生成人工智能公司，于 1 月份筹集了 5.58 亿美元，并在随后的两次股票发行中筹集了 90 亿美元。对于付费客户来说，情况也是如此。 Anthropic 公布 2026 年上半年的收入超过 160 亿美元，而 Z.ai 的收入为 1.42 亿美元。中国企业偏爱的商业模式将很难缩小这一差距。大多数公司都将其标准模型开源，这意味着该技术可以免费使用和更新，并出售其最先进模型的使用权。但在中国拥挤的人工智能领域，对客户的激烈竞争正在压低费用。本月早些时候，中国科技巨头阿里巴巴聘请了直播主播李佳琦。

【原文 English Original】
Nathan Chen, a teenage tech prodigy, was a leading innovator at Moonshot AI, one of several top Chinese labs that have sparked fears in Silicon Valley that China is gaining ground in the race for AI supremacy. But last month, Chen posted on X that he had left the Beijing-based company. He is now at Discovery Loop, a new Palo Alto–based AI start-up with a growing stable of high-profile talent. Perhaps Chen sensed that the most exciting advances in AI were not happening in China—despite the fact that the technology’s rollout in the United States has lately looked more troubled than ever. Newly empowered Democrats, ushered to midterm victories thanks in part to public opposition to data centers, are calling to rein in construction plans. A sex scandal, possibly also a spy scandal, at Nvidia—a U.S. chipmaker that has almost single-handedly enabled the AI boom—has cost Jensen Huang, its former chief executive, his job; fomented turmoil in U.S. financial markets; and plunged the entire AI economy into crisis. But China still appears to be falling behind. Chinese AI firms are short of chips they need—a problem that Huang’s downfall might well make worse—and they can’t raise enough capital to compete with their wealthy American rivals. Public resistance to the potentially job-killing technology seems to be growing, and the security-obsessed Communist Party, which has been bullish on the potential for AI to fix China’s mounting economic challenges, has lately appeared wary of the threats it might pose to the party’s grip on power. This attitude shift could further hamper AI’s progress in the country. Proponents of the emerging technology argue that AI will bring societal benefits—boosting economic productivity, fast-tracking scientific advances, and strengthening military capabilities. China’s leaders have touted the technology as crucial to the country’s continued rise, and tech executives and national-security experts in the United States have framed the pursuit of AI as an existential race for technological dominance, a winner-takes-all competition between the two countries that will determine the global balance of power. Some analysts question whether the geopolitics of AI are so neatly zero-sum, but if advances do end up conferring a decisive strategic advantage to the country that best harnesses these tools, then China’s leaders should be worried. Anthropic’s initial public offering, scheduled for this week, demonstrates the kind of access to capital that American firms enjoy and their Chinese competitors can only dream of. Anthropic is expected to raise more than $90 billion from its Nasdaq debut and direct sale of stock to investors, including Google and Microsoft. By comparison, a Chinese start-up known as Z.ai raised $558 million as the country’s first generative-AI firm on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange, in January, and an additional $9 billion in two subsequent share offerings. The story is the same when it comes to paying customers. Anthropic posted revenues of more than $16 billion in the first half of 2026, compared with Z.ai’s $142 million . The business model preferred by Chinese firms will make it hard to close this gap. Most offer their standard models open-source, which means the tech is free to use and update, and sell access to their most advanced models. But in China’s crowded AI sector, fierce competition for customers is driving down fees. Earlier this month, the Chinese tech giant Alibaba tapped Li Jiaqi, a livestreamer and beauty influencer known as the “Lipstick King,” to pitch a temporary promotion in monthly membership fees for the company’s AI productivity platform, from 28 yuan down to .01 yuan—or .0015 cents. [ Matteo Wong: A $5.7 trillion face-plant ] Chinese firms are also at a serious disadvantage in computing power. Washington has imposed export restrictions on Nvidia’s most advanced chips to China, and China’s own chipmakers have yet to make a product that matches their power. Chinese companies have tried to evade these controls by tapping cloud services and data centers outside the country and smuggling in banned Nvidia chips. But Huang’s extramarital affair with an alleged Chinese spy will likely lead to the closure of at least some of these loopholes. Alice Huang, the woman at the center of the Nvidia scandal (no relation), was a top executive at Megaspeed, a Singapore-based cloud-computing firm that has been under investigation by the U.S. federal government for illegally funneling Nvidia chips to China. Lawmakers from both parties have announced plans in recent days to add measures tightening restrictions on chip exports to the defense package currently stalled in Congress. Chinese labs have demonstrated that they are able to build competitive AI models with less money and computing power than their U.S. rivals. But the advantages that America’s AI sector has in funds, infrastructure, and chips promise to compound over time. Chinese companies appear to have responded to this resource gap by devoting their energies to building lower-cost products for a wider user base, rather than trying to make the most intelligent cutting-edge models. “I don’t actually think at any point over the past two years that Chinese companies have been trying to beat the U.S. on intelligence,” Kendra Schaefer, a partner at the research firm Trivium China who specializes in Chinese AI, told me. “It has not been part of the strategy at all, because they know they can’t win.” Chinese AI engineers have instead set their sights on where they can aggressively compete. For example, China’s massive manufacturing base would seem to grant an advantage in developing embodied AI for operating robots and other hardware. But here, too, technology from America is leading the way. Last month, Wang Xingxing, the CEO of Unitree, a top Chinese developer of humanoid robots, gushed about the capabilities of OpenAI’s newly released ChatGPT-6 Astra model for advancing the movements and actions of intelligent machines. China might also seem to have an edge over the U.S. when it comes to the speed with which individuals and companies are adopting the technology. The Chinese government has an ambitious plan to spread AI through every aspect of its economy and society by 2035, and surveys find that Chinese people are far more optimistic than Americans about AI. This has raised concerns in the U.S. that China is doing a better job of realizing gains from the new technology. But Martin Chorzempa, a senior fellow at the Peterson Institute for International Economics, has found that in practice, American companies are integrating AI into their operations more extensively than Chinese companies, which means they “are able to get a lot more out of it,” he told me. He added that there is “zero” evidence that AI is spreading faster and deeper in China. China’s leaders seem to have also grown warier of AI and the risks it could pose to the country’s political and economic stability. Beijing’s spy chief, Chen Yixin, recently called for greater regulation of AI to prevent China’s adversaries from using the technology to spread misinformation or to launch cyberattacks on critical Chinese infrastructure. But Chinese authorities appear just as nervous about more prosaic uses of the technology. A recent editorial in the People’s Daily , the Communist Party’s mouthpiece, criticized some popular AI-generated videos that imagined a romance between two beloved characters from classic Chinese literature as “malicious alterations that ridicule heroes.” Chinese social-media companies duly scrubbed the short films from their platforms—in keeping with a wider government ban on AI-generated content that, in the eyes of the state, distorts Chinese history and culture and threatens to manipulate public opinion. In a country where the government seeks to control the national story, even the most innocuous AI creations can seem ominously subversive and worth suppressing. Public anxiety about AI’s effect on jobs is also spreading, which may pose some obstacles on Chinese companies that hope to use the technology to increase productivity and cut costs. One of the country’s most popular chili-sauce brands, Lao Gan Ma, came under fire last month after the company’s chief quality officer credited AI with reducing product-defect rates and increasing revenues. These comments quickly circulated online, along with reports that the technology had allowed Lao Gan Ma to lay off hundreds of workers—a claim that the company has denied. Some consumers have responded by calling for a boycott of the sauce. As one commenter wrote: “Their layoff is our future.” [ Liza Lin: China has no use for AI doomerism ] Despite efforts to encourage companies to adopt the technology, China’s leaders are also clearly worried about related job losses. The government released new guidelines last month for beefing up job training and support for workers displaced by AI. These new provisions also allow regulators to weigh the potential job losses from AI-related ventures that require state approval, such as an expansion of robotaxis, suggesting that the government may intervene to prevent large-scale layoffs. AI is meant to help companies become more productive by allowing them to cut staff, yet China appears willing to sacrifice some of these benefits if it means preserving the social order. In the U.S., the fragmented regulatory landscape for AI gives companies, developers, and employers a great deal of latitude for exploiting the technology’s benefits. Perhaps the very idea that China and the United States are engaged in a high-stakes race for AI dominance misunderstands the situation. China might simply be claiming a role in AI that the country has taken in so many other industries: as a low-cost producer, offering sufficiently capable services at cheap prices that complement rather than rival the superior products sold for higher fees in the U.S. As in other industries, the demand for AI products at both the high and low end should be strong. But if China’s government continues to block American AI models from operating in the country, these seemingly symbiotic market niches won’t end up serving the Chinese people, who will be largely doomed to the exclusive use of their country’s inferior products. If the Communist Party seeks to control what Chinese AI companies get to use and how they get to use it, then the United States will enjoy a monopoly not only on superior AI but also on the freedom to make the most of it.

title: USS Theodore Roosevelt Now in the Middle East, Lincoln’s Last Escorts Finally Home
zh_title: 西奥多·罗斯福号航空母舰现已抵达中东，林肯最后的护航终于回家
summary: 2026 年 11 月 15 日，西奥多·罗斯福号航空母舰 (CVN-71) 穿越印度洋。作为计划部署的一部分，该航母目前正在美国中央司令部责任区执行任务。美国海军照片 美国第三艘航空母舰及其护航舰现已抵达中东。西奥多·罗斯福号航空母舰 (CVN-71) 于周日加入美国第五舰队。随着美国和伊朗之间的紧张局势持续存在，西奥多·罗斯福号航母打击群的到来使美国在中东地区出现了三个航母打击群。周末，胡塞武装继续占领巴布埃尔附近地区。
content:
2026 年 11 月 15 日，西奥多·罗斯福号航空母舰 (CVN-71) 穿越印度洋。作为计划部署的一部分，该航母目前正在美国中央司令部责任区执行任务。美国海军照片 美国第三艘航空母舰及其护航舰现已抵达中东。西奥多·罗斯福号航空母舰 (CVN-71) 于周日加入美国第五舰队。随着美国和伊朗之间的紧张局势持续存在，西奥多·罗斯福号航母打击群的到来使美国在中东地区出现了三个航母打击群。周末，胡塞武装继续对曼德海峡（连接亚丁湾与红海的战略要道）周围地区提出主权要求，而伊朗军队则声称他们周五袭击了位于巴林的美国雷达。美国中央司令部否认了社交媒体网站 X 上发布的有关伊斯兰革命卫队在巴林发射两架单向无人机并被击落的说法。 2026 年 11 月 16 日，美国水兵在尼米兹级航空母舰西奥多·罗斯福号 (CVN-71) 的飞行甲板上使用分配给第 8 直升机海上作战中队 (HSC) 的 MH-60S 海鹰进行飞行作业。西奥多·罗斯福号被部署到美国第五舰队作战区域，以支持中东的海上安全与稳定。美国海军照片 西奥多·罗斯福预计将接替 8 月底抵达中东的乔治·华盛顿号航空母舰 (CVN-73)。
虽然 GW 最终接替了亚伯拉罕·林肯号航空母舰 (CVN-72)，但在安倍回国之前，这两艘航母都与乔治·H·W·布什号航空母舰 (CVN-77) 一起在中东执行任务大约一个月。目前尚不清楚 GW 将在 TR 抵达后在该地区停留多久。布什、GW和TR在中东的存在是以美国航母在印太地区的存在为代价的。安倍在部署 321 天后启程回国，而其两艘护航舰——迈克尔·墨菲号 (DDG-112) 和斯普鲁恩斯号 (DDG-111)——则留在了后方。迈克尔·墨菲 (Michael Murphy) 在服役 346 天后于周四返回家中，而斯普鲁恩斯 (Spruance) 在服役 357 天后于周六返回家中。斯普鲁恩斯的部署时间比安倍多了 36 天，创下了驱逐舰部署的记录。阿利·伯克级导弹驱逐舰斯普鲁恩斯号 (DDG-111) 于 2026 年 11 月 13 日返回圣地亚哥海军基地母港，结束了在美国第 3、第 7 和第 5 舰队作战区域为期 12 个月的战斗部署。美国海军照片 对于驱逐舰来说，长达近一年的部署是罕见的，它们通常会部署六到七个月。然而，海军警告水手和家属，随着海上服务试图满足政府的需求，部署将持续近一年。斯普鲁恩斯于 2025 年 11 月 21 日从加利福尼亚州圣地亚哥海军基地部署。
据海军发布的宣布该驱逐舰回归的消息称，该驱逐舰在第三、第五和第七舰队中服役，在整个部署过程中航行了超过 88,000 海里。 2026 年 11 月 13 日，海军水手和亲人欢迎阿利·伯克级导弹驱逐舰斯普鲁恩斯号 (DDG-111) 返回其母港圣地亚哥海军基地，结束了在美国第三、第七和第五舰队行动区为期 12 个月的战斗部署。美国海军照片 斯普鲁恩斯号在部署期间参与了史诗狂怒行动，在此期间，作为持续海上封锁的一部分，驱逐舰禁用了货船 M/V Touska。虽然新闻稿称该舰发射了战斧导弹，但没有详细说明

【原文 English Original】
USS Theodore Roosevelt (CVN-71) transits the Indian Ocean, Nov. 15, 2026. The aircraft carrier is currently operating in the U.S. Central Command area of responsibility as part of a scheduled deployment. US Navy photo A third U.S. aircraft carrier and its escorts are now in the Middle East. USS Theodore Roosevelt (CVN-71) chopped into U.S. 5th Fleet on Sunday. The arrival of the Theodore Roosevelt Carrier Strike Group makes three U.S. carrier strike groups in the Middle East, as tensions persist between the U.S. and Iran. Over the weekend, the Houthis continued to claim areas around the Bab el-Mandeb – the strategic chokepoint that connects the Gulf of Aden to the Red Sea – while Iranian forces claim they attacked a U.S. radar in Bahrain on Friday. U.S. Central Command denied the claim posting on social media site X that the Islamic Revolutionary Guards Corps launched two one-way drones at Bahrain, which were shot down. U.S. sailors conduct flight operations with an MH-60S Sea Hawk assigned to Helicopter Sea Combat Squadron (HSC) 8 on the flight deck of Nimitz-class aircraft carrier USS Theodore Roosevelt (CVN-71), Nov. 16, 2026. Theodore Roosevelt is deployed to the U.S. 5th Fleet area of operations to support maritime security and stability in the Middle East. US Navy photo Theodore Roosevelt is expected to relieve USS George Washington (CVN-73), which arrived in the Middle East toward the end of August . While GW ultimately relieved USS Abraham Lincoln (CVN-72), the two carriers both operated in the Middle East, along with USS George H.W. Bush (CVN-77), for about a month before Abe headed home. It is unclear how long GW will stay in the area with TR’s arrival. Bush , GW and TR’s presence in the Middle East comes at the cost of the U.S. carrier presence in the Indo-Pacific region. While Abe headed home after 321 days on deployment, two of its escorts – USS Michael Murphy (DDG-112) and USS Spruance (DDG-111) – stayed behind. Michael Murphy returned home Thursday after 346 days deployed, while Spruance returned home on Saturday after 357 days deployed. Spruance’s deployment came in at 36 days more than Abe and set a record for destroyer deployments. Arleigh Burke-class guided-missile destroyer USS Spruance (DDG-111) returns to its home port of Naval Base San Diego, Nov. 13, 2026, concluding a 12-month combat deployment across the U.S. 3rd, 7th, and 5th fleet areas of operations. US Navy photo Nearly year-long deployments are rare for destroyers, which usually go out for six to seven months. However, the Navy has warned sailors and families to expect deployments that approach a year as the sea service attempts to keep up the needs of the administration. Spruance deployed on Nov. 21, 2025, from Naval Base San Diego, Calif. The destroyer operated in the 3rd, 5th and 7th fleets, traveling more than 88,000 nautical miles throughout its deployments, according to a Navy release announcing the destroyer’s return. U.S. Navy sailors and loved ones welcome Arleigh Burke-class guided-missile destroyer USS Spruance (DDG-111) as it returns to its home port of Naval Base San Diego, Nov. 13, 2026, concluding a 12-month combat deployment across the U.S. 3rd, 7th, and 5th fleet areas of operations. US Navy photo While deployed, Spruance was part of Operation Epic Fury, during which the destroyer disabled cargo vessel M/V Touska as part of the ongoing maritime blockade. While the release said the ship launched Tomahawk missiles, it did not go into details about the Iranian military targets. The destroyer did take out 12 drones and four anti-ship cruise missiles while in the Middle East, according to the Navy release. The “Raptors” of HSM-71 embarked on Spruance and flew 190 sorties during the deployment, reads the release. Spruance received the Presidential Unit Citation and Combat Action Ribbon following its role in Operation Epic Fury. The destroyer has been busy over the past two years. Before its most recent deployment, the ship was part of U.S. Northern Command’s southern border operations, leaving San Diego in March 2025. Prior to that, Spruance spent five months in the Middle East as part of the U.S. response to Houthi attacks on commercial shipping, coming home on Dec. 19, 2024.

title: Navy Weapons Division to Make Tomahawk Components in 2027
zh_title: 海军武器部门将于 2027 年生产战斧部件
summary: 2026 年 2 月 28 日，阿利·伯克级导弹驱逐舰小弗兰克·E·彼得森号 (DDG-121) 在支持史诗狂怒行动的行动中发射战斧对地攻击导弹。美国海军照片 海军空战中心武器部门上周宣布，将于 2027 年 6 月开始制造战斧巡航导弹弹头的组件，届时一种新型炸药和推进剂混合器上线。 11 月 9 日，由 B&P Littleford 制造的新型 300 加仑搅拌机在加利福尼亚州中国湖推进实验室举行剪彩仪式。一旦混音器上线
content:
2026 年 2 月 28 日，阿利·伯克级导弹驱逐舰小弗兰克·E·彼得森号 (DDG-121) 在支持史诗狂怒行动的行动中发射战斧对地攻击导弹。美国海军照片 海军空战中心武器部门上周宣布，将于 2027 年 6 月开始制造战斧巡航导弹弹头的组件，届时一种新型炸药和推进剂混合器上线。 11 月 9 日，由 B&P Littleford 制造的新型 300 加仑搅拌机在加利福尼亚州中国湖推进实验室举行剪彩仪式。 NAWCD 在一份新闻稿中表示，一旦混合器上线，NAWCD 的弹头生产团队将努力在制造商雷神公司需要弹头之前准备好弹头，帮助确保连续、准时地将战斧交付给舰队。 8月，海军授予雷神公司一份价值229亿美元的合同，以加速战斧生产，目标是每年生产1000多枚导弹。在“史诗狂怒行动”之后，国防部一直在努力增加和加速导弹和弹药的生产，该行动导致弹药迅速消耗。五角大楼的努力还集中于扩大制造商和供应商的国防工业基础，建设产能和冗余。 2026 年 11 月 9 日，来宾聚集在大型混合湾，观看中国湖推进实验室剪彩后新型 300 加仑混合机的演示。
一旦在 2027 年 6 月左右上线，混合器将使海军空战中心武器部门的能量团队达到为舰队生产战斧弹头的生产率。美国海军照片推进和能量部门负责人瑞安·亨特在新闻稿中表示，更快的生产需要更大的弹头容量。中国湖的海军实验室和马里兰州海军水面作战中心印度司令部表示，他们可以进行弹头的生产工作。目前，雷神公司是战斧制造的主要承包商，而通用动力军械和战术系统公司负责加工弹头箱，而 L3Harris 则为其装载炸药。 9 月，L3Harris 和 NAWCWD 签署了一项多年的公私合作伙伴关系，以制造导弹部件。亨特说，根据该协议，NAWCWD 计划生产部分战斧弹头。一年前，当 NAWCD 能源团队从博物馆取出一个战斧弹头盒时，NAWCD 开始了拥有制造战斧弹头能力的过程。能源团队将炸药和火箭推进剂混合在一起，并将其装入海军武器中。 2026 年 11 月 9 日，中国湖推进实验室大型混合舱中，新型 300 加仑行星混合器的叶片位于混合碗上方。该混合器将于 2027 年 6 月左右投入使用，将使海军空战中心武器部门的能量团队达到舰队战斧弹头的生产率。
美国海军照片 该团队清理了箱子并混合了 PBXN-107 炸药并填充了 WDU-36/B 弹头。测试、成像和 X 射线证实该团队正确填充了它。经过这一努力，今年秋天，同一个团队填充了七个首件战斧弹头，这是新生产商建造的第一批用于检查的装置。能量处理部门负责人赞恩·戈德特表示，一旦通过，它们将成为“中国湖”的第一批生产弹头。弹头由中国湖运行了数十年的 150 加仑混合器填充，新的混合器将取代它。在演示构建过程中，团队还发现

Arleigh Burke-class guided-missile destroyer USS Frank E. Petersen Jr. (DDG-121) fires a Tomahawk Land Attack Missile during operations in support of Operation Epic Fury, Feb. 28, 2026. US Navy photo The Naval Air Warfare Center Weapons Division will begin making a component for Tomahawk cruise missile warheads in June of 2027 when a new explosive and propellant mixer comes online, the division announced last week. A new 300 gallon mixer, built by B&P Littleford was inaugurated in a ribbon cutting ceremony on Nov. 9 at the China Lake Propulsion Laboratory in California. Once the mixer is online, NAWCD’s warhead production team will work to have warheads ready before manufacturer Raytheon needs them, helping ensure continuous, on-time Tomahawk deliveries to the fleet, NAWCD said in a news release . In August, the Navy awarded Raytheon a $22.9 billion contract to accelerate Tomahawk production with a target of producing more than 1,000 missiles annually. The Department of Defense has been carrying out efforts to increase and accelerate productions of missiles and munitions following Operation Epic Fury, which has seen munitions rapidly expended. Pentagon efforts have also focused on expanding the defense industrial base of manufacturers and suppliers, building both capacity and redundancy. Guests gather in the large mix bay to watch a demonstration of a new 300-gallon mixer after its ribbon cutting at the China Lake Propulsion Laboratory, Nov. 9, 2026. Once online around June 2027, the mixer will let Naval Air Warfare Center Weapons Division’s energetics team reach production rate on Tomahawk warheads for the fleet. US Navy photo Faster production calls for more warhead capacity, said Ryan Hunter, head of the Propulsion and Energetics Division, in the release. Navy labs at China Lake and at Naval Surface Warfare Center Indian Head Division in Maryland said they could do the work to produce warheads. Currently, Raytheon is the prime contractor building Tomahawks while General Dynamics Ordnance and Tactical Systems machines the warhead cases and L3Harris loads them with explosives. In September, L3Harris and NAWCWD signed a multi-year public-private partnership to manufacture missile components. Under it, Hunter said, NAWCWD plans to produce a portion of the Tomahawk warheads. NAWCD began the process of having the capability to build Tomahawk warheads a year ago when the NAWCD energetics team pulled a Tomahawk warhead case out of a museum. The energetics team mixes explosives and rocket propellants and loads them into Navy weapons. The blades of a new 300-gallon planetary mixer rest above the mix bowl in the large mix bay at the China Lake Propulsion Laboratory, Nov. 9, 2026. Once online around June 2027, the mixer will let Naval Air Warfare Center Weapons Division’s energetics team reach production rate on Tomahawk warheads for the fleet. US Navy photo The team cleaned the case and mixed PBXN-107 explosive and filled the WDU-36/B warhead. Testing, imaging and X-rays confirmed the team filled it correctly. Following that effort, this fall, the same team filled seven first-article Tomahawk warheads, the first units a new producer builds for inspection. Once they pass, they become China Lake’s first production warheads, said Zane Goedert, head of the Energetics Processing Branch. The warhead was filled by a 150-gallon mixer China Lake has run for decades, which the new mixer will replace. During the demonstration build, the team also found the warhead specification needed a major update. Key parts and materials to address the issue can take up to a year to arrive, reads the NAWCD release. Patricia Hottowe, director of the Tomahawk Technical Project Office at NAWCWD, said in the release that the team spent much of the past year updating the specification and the approved supplier list. The Navy’s technical authority for the warhead must approve each new supplier and every future producer – Navy or industry – must build to that specification. NAWCWD also bought long-lead materials ahead of the multi-year contract, Hottowe said. A dozen new personnel have been hired to join the team, Goedert said. They will train under experienced technicians on safety, quality and procedures for about a year before working on their own. He added that loading the warhead is the easiest part while buying materials, bringing on people and getting answers are harder. Arleigh Burke-class guided-missile destroyer USS Delbert D. Black (DDG-119) fires a Tomahawk Land Attack Missile (TLAM) in support of Operation Epic Fury, Feb. 28, 2026. US Navy photo The branch has filled warheads for the AGM-84H/K Stand-off Land Attack Missile-Expanded Response (SLAM-E) missile since the mid-1990s. Goedert said his team routinely turns one-of-a-kind prototypes around on short timelines. That experience allowed the team to move faster on Tomahawk. According to Hunter, the challenge comes from a system built for fixed multi-year schedules. Now that system must move faster on a shorter clock. China Lake’s facilities will be able to meet that challenge due to its layout. “Because our plant is dispersed and because we will be curing the warheads in a different area than we’re casting them, we’re able to do simultaneous processes that will get higher throughput,” said Hunter. The plant’s newest buildings grew out of a rebuild as the July 2019 earthquakes destroyed three energetics compounds in the Salt Wells area of the China Lake Propulsion Laboratory, reads the release. Naval Facilities Engineering Systems Command broke ground on their replacements, known as the trio, in April of 2022. Goedert said the team designed the Motor Assembly Compound to cut handling. Large rocket motors risk damage each time crews move them after casting. The same layout will speed warhead work. Rear Adm. Eric Gardner, principal deputy for the Portfolio Acquisition Executive Munitions, spoke at the ribbon cutting and said the first-article warheads will lay the groundwork for China Lake to become an additional source of Tomahawk warhead production. “At PAE Munitions, we know that increasing weapons production takes more than contracts and funding,” Gardner said. “It takes people, infrastructure, materials, and strong partnerships across our Navy, our warfare centers and industry.”

该运动是在毛泽东领导下建立的，现在是中共确保基督教中国化的主要工具。国家主席习近平委婉地将中国化定义为“使宗教适应中国特色社会主义”。实际上，这意味着牧师必须禁止所有 18 岁以下的未成年人进入教堂、以习近平思想为中心讲道、监视会众，以及其他许多要求和限制。中国牧师以斯拉·金（Ezra Jin）和他的八位锡安大型教会牧师和领袖的例子就是这种模式的一部分。一年前，他们因拒绝在教堂安装政府监控摄像头并拒绝在网上讲道而被捕。金去年七月被唐纳德·特朗普总统救出，但其他八名锡安领导人仍因欺诈指控被监禁在中国，比如崔天凯。崔牧师的教堂很受欢迎。 2019年，北京的教会被禁止进入其礼拜场所，因为当局认为该场所太大。崔随后开始在不同地点举行小团体聚会，但据他的妻子报道，当局在 2023 年告诉他，他只能领导“一个人数少于 100 人的教会”。对于中共来说，这些镇压手段显然还不够。它决定完全关闭教堂，让牧师噤声，并通过援引道德败坏罪来玷污他的声誉。我询问金牧师的女儿格蕾丝（Grace）对崔被捕的看法。
她在一封电子邮件中评论说，“北京继续迫害基督徒并扼杀宗教自由，现在用刑法的语言来形容这种迫害。”   她指出，这项指控本身就是对基督教行为定罪的一种形式。她写道：“指控一名牧师欺诈其会众的奉献，将什一税定为犯罪，这是一种与教会本身一样古老的做法。当法律以这种方式使用时，它就不再是法律，而是成为一种武器。” Grace Jin 也看到了这些案例中的矛盾，她称之为“

China Unleashes a Sweeping Crackdown on Christians bbert@hudson.org Mon, 11/16/2026 - 10:24 SVG Commentary Nov 15, 2026 New York Post China Unleashes a Sweeping Crackdown on Christians Nina Shea Senior Fellow and Director, Center for Religious Freedom Nina Shea Commentary Caption Chinese founder of Zion Church Ezra Jin speaks during an interview in Cheverly, Maryland, on August 11, 2026. (Getty Images) Toggle Table of Contents Contents Contents Share to Twitter Twitter Share to Facebook Facebook Share to LinkedIn LinkedIn Share to E-mail E-mail Print Print The Chinese Communist Party has worked systematically to crush, suppress and co-opt all religious groups in China under its 2018 “Sinicization” campaign. Now it’s coming for Protestant Christians, China’s largest religious minority. Reports surfaced this week that Pastor Xianfeng Edward Cui, the founding leader of Beijing Jiaquan Church since 2006, was charged with fraud on Oct. 23. The charge, which typically carries a prison sentence, was based on his passing around the collection plate.    The 57-year-old house church leader was detained on Sept. 4 when some 100 police officers raided the house church, his wife Jin Young Gu, who lives outside China, told the Associated Press.  She said the operation was related to “church members’ offerings.” The real reason for Cui’s arrest is that he has resisted registering his church with the Three Self Patriotic Movement, which is directly under the CCP’s United Front Work Department. Established under Mao Zedong, the movement is now the CCP’s main instrument for ensuring the Sinicization of Protestant Christianity in China. President Xi Jinping euphemistically defines Sinicization as “adapting religion to socialism with Chinese characteristics.” In practice it means pastors must ban all minors under 18 years old from church, center sermons on Xi Jinping’s Thought, and spy on their congregations, among many other demands and restrictions. The cases of Chinese Pastor Ezra Jin and eight of his fellow Zion megachurch pastors and leaders are part of this pattern. They were arrested a year ago, after refusing the installation of government surveillance cameras in their churches and then for preaching online. Jin was rescued by President Donald Trump last July but the other eight Zion leaders remain imprisoned in China on fraud charges, like Cui.   Pastor Cui’s church is popular. In 2019, the congregation in Beijing was barred from its worship space because authorities thought it was too large. Cui then began meeting in smaller groups at various sites but authorities told him in 2023 that he could lead “only one church with fewer than 100 people,” his wife reported. These suppression tactics apparently weren’t enough for the CCP.  It decided to shut down the church completely, silence its pastor and taint his reputation by invoking a crime of moral turpitude. I asked Pastor Jin’s daughter, Grace, her thoughts on Cui’s arrest. She commented in an email that “Beijing continues to persecute Christians and choke off religious freedom, now dressing that persecution in the language of criminal law.”   She observes that the charge, itself, is a form of criminalizing Christian practice. She wrote: “Charging a pastor with fraud over his congregation’s offerings criminalizes tithing, a practice as old as the church itself. When law is used this way, it stops being law and becomes a weapon.” Grace Jin also sees a contradiction in these cases, which she calls a bitter irony: “For more than a century, Chinese Christians have worked to build churches that support themselves, free from reliance on foreign missions. Congregations like Pastor Cui’s, sustained by the gifts of ordinary Chinese believers, are the fruit of that effort. If any church in China is truly ‘sinicized,’ it is the house church. Crushing these congregations in the name of sinicization shows the campaign for what it is: not about making faith Chinese, but about making it obedient.” Sinicization impacts all religions in China. Protestant Christianity will be its biggest challenge since it counts 100 million or more among its members, most of whom worship with unregistered house churches, like Cui’s. Renowned Purdue University sociologist Fenggang Yang wrote in an Oct. 8 email that he accepts that number based on his calculations using a “strict measure of self-identification that excludes those who believe without belonging or practice without believing or belonging.” There could be more Protestants in China than members of the CCP, which is reported to also number 100 million.   Another consideration for the CCP is Christian influence within America, whose markets, investments and trade China depends on. While it works to suppress the Chinese house churches, the CCP faces a delicate balance of placating both its own booming Christian population and the American public.  It is using lawfare in kangaroo courts against the Christians, not the brutal tactics that it applies to crush the Tibetan Buddhists, Uyghur Muslims, or Falun Gong practitioners. It is persecution nonetheless. President Trump should speak up for Pastor Cui and the others persecuted in China when he meets with Xi later this month. Read in New York Post. Enjoyed this analysis? title: The Nvidia Scandal Exposes American Blind Spots
zh_title: 英伟达丑闻暴露美国盲点
summary: 华盛顿已经建立了一个复杂的出口管制和许可要求网络，以防止人工智能芯片进入中国。然而，英伟达创始人黄仁勋与被指控向北京传递信息的中国女商人黄爱丽之间明显的“美人计”事件，不仅仅是这些控制措施的盲点问题。它讲述了在全球化、互联的世界中关闭先进技术的困难，以及一家公司、监管机构和行政部门看到了警告信号却迟迟未采取行动。如果现有规则得到执行，Nvidia
content:
华盛顿已经建立了一个复杂的出口管制和许可要求网络，以防止人工智能芯片进入中国。然而，英伟达创始人黄仁勋与被指控向北京传递信息的中国女商人黄爱丽之间明显的“美人计”事件，不仅仅是这些控制措施的盲点问题。它讲述了在全球化、互联的世界中关闭先进技术的困难，以及一家公司、监管机构和行政部门看到了警告信号却迟迟未采取行动。如果现有规则得到执行，英伟达就不应该向总部位于新加坡的云计算公司 Megaspeed International 出售先进芯片。 Alice Huang 是 Megaspeed 的高管，该公司成为 Nvidia 的主要客户，并因可能违反美国出口管制而受到审查。英伟达董事会已聘请外部顾问来调查中国情报部门是否针对其前首席执行官，后者在其事务曝光后辞职。该公司坚称，没有理由相信其机密或国家安全受到损害。这个故事的核心是供应链的不透明性，而它始于 Megaspeed 错综复杂的所有权。该公司于2015年在新加坡注册成立，名称为第七大道国际，是中国网络游戏行业中的新兴企业。它于 2023 年采用现名。
同年晚些时候，Megaspeed 的股份通过一家在英属维尔京群岛注册的公司转让给另一家在新加坡注册的公司 Swiftdata。谁最终控制 Swiftdata 目前尚不清楚。错综复杂的注册流程并不能证明国家控制，中国投资也不等同于中国政府所有权。但中国的国有资本和私人资本经常通过子公司、控股公司和离岸工具进行流动。 Megaspeed 复杂的企业历史本应引发严格审查，审查谁控制该公司以及谁最终将从其购买美国芯片中受益。尽管存在警告信号，Megaspeed 仍成为 Nvidia 的官方云合作伙伴，并购买了价值数十亿美元的先进计算设备。其印度尼西亚子公司进口了最先进的 Nvidia 硬件。美国当局已调查Megaspeed是否也帮助中国客户获得Nvidia芯片。 Megaspeed 否认非法转让，也没有任何公开调查结果证实存在出口管制违规行为。但英伟达面临的问题从来不是违规行为是否得到证实；而是问题。问题在于具有这种特征的客户是否值得信任和访问。 2025 年 8 月，Nvidia 总法律顾问通过电子邮件向负责调查 Megaspeed 的部门特工发送电子邮件，称商务部高级官员已批准此次外展活动。调查已暂停并移交给司法部。
其他机构提议将 Megaspeed 添加到被认为对美国国家安全构成风险的外国企业和组织的实体名单中。商务部从未这样做过。官员们敦促商务部采取行动，国务卿马可·卢比奥 (Marco Rubio) 于 2026 年 5 月向商务部长霍华德·卢特尼克 (Howard Lutnick) 发送了一份有关 Megaspeed 的备忘录。据报道，财政部长斯科特·贝森特 (Scott Bessent) 最近与卢特尼克对质，问道：“Megaspeed 为何不在实体名单上？”商务部否认发生过交易。白宫收到警告。据报道，唐纳德·特朗普总统去年年底听取了简报和一份关于爱丽丝的机密备忘录

【原文 English Original】
Washington has built an elaborate web of export controls and licensing requirements to keep artificial intelligence chips from reaching China. Yet Nvidia founder Jensen Huang’s apparent “honeytrap” affair with Alice Huang, a Chinese businesswoman accused of passing information to Beijing, is about more than the blind spots of those controls. It is about the difficulty of shutting down access to advanced tech in a globalized, interconnected world — and about a company, a regulator, and an executive branch that saw warning signs and were slow act on them. Had existing rules been enforced, Nvidia should never have been selling advanced chips to the Singapore-based cloud computing company Megaspeed International. Alice Huang was an executive at Megaspeed, which became a major Nvidia customer, and attracted scrutin y over possible violations of American export controls. Nvidia’s board has retained outside counsel to investigate whether Chinese intelligence targeted their former CEO, who resigned after his affairs were revealed. The company maintains that it has no reason to believe its secrets or national security were compromised. At its core, the story is about the opacity of supply chains, and it begins with Megaspeed’s convoluted ownership. The company incorporated in Singapore in 2015 as 7Road International, emerging from the Chinese online gaming industry. It adopted its current name in 2023. Later that year, Megaspeed’s shares were transferred , through a company registered in the British Virgin Islands, to another Singapore-registered company, Swiftdata. Who ultimately controls Swiftdata remains unclear. Convoluted incorporation trails do not prove state control, and Chinese investment is not synonymous with Chinese government ownership. But state-linked and private Chinese capital often  moves  through subsidiaries, holding companies, and offshore vehicles. Megaspeed’s complex corporate history should have triggered rigorous scrutiny of who controlled the firm and who would ultimately benefit from its purchases of US chips.  Despite the warning signs, Megaspeed became an official Nvidia cloud partner and purchased billions of dollars’ worth of advanced computing equipment. Its Indonesian subsidiary imported cutting-edge Nvidia hardware. US authorities have investigated whether Megaspeed also helped Chinese customers obtain Nvidia chips. Megaspeed has denied illicit transfers, and no public finding has established an export-control violation. But the question for Nvidia was never whether a violation had been proven; it was whether a customer with this profile warranted trust and access. In August 2025, Nvidia’s general counsel  emailed  Department agents investigating Megaspeed, saying that a senior Commerce official had approved the outreach. The investigation was paused and transferred to the Justice Department.  Other agencies proposed adding Megaspeed to the entity list of foreign businesses and organizations that are deemed to pose a risk to US national security. Commerce never did. Officials  pressed  Commerce to act, and Secretary of State Marco Rubio sent Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick a memorandum on Megaspeed in May 2026. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent recently reportedly  confronted  Lutnik, asking: “How come Megaspeed isn’t on the entities list?” Commerce denies that the  exchange  took place. The White House was warned. President Donald Trump was reportedly briefed late last year and a classified memorandum on Alice Huang circulated among senior officials before his May visit to China. Apparently, no action was taken. Instead, Nvidia CEO Huang joined the presidential delegation to Beijing and, in September, attended the White House state dinner for Chinese President Xi Jinping. Jensen Huang’s own conduct compounded the failure. An executive with his access to the president and to sensitive policy discussions carries a responsibility that goes beyond his obligations to shareholders. A relationship with a foreign national linked to a customer under federal investigation was, at best, reckless. Washington depends on companies such as Nvidia to sustain its technological lead over China, expand domestic computing capacity, and support an increasingly AI-dependent defense posture. Yet these companies  remain  commercial enterprises that  are  accountable to shareholders and driven by incentives that might not always align with national security objectives.  Get the Latest Sign up to receive regular Bandwidth emails and stay informed about CEPA's work. Although enforcing existing export controls would have gone a long way to prevent this crisis, the case reveals a genuine gap. US export controls focus on where advanced chips are shipped, yet access to computing power no longer requires owning the hardware.  Renting “offshore” computing is often legal. A Chinese company banned from purchasing certain advanced US processors may be able to buy computing capacity from servers in another jurisdiction. Megaspeed reportedly  provided computing services to Chinese technology customers, including the Chinese e-commerce leader Alibaba. This gap risks widening as AI infrastructure expands across Southeast Asia, the Middle East, and other regions. The US needs to enforce existing rules and close the gaps. First, that means applying export controls consistently. When the evidence warrants, enforcement must be separated from corporate lobbying — and acted on. Second, add access to advanced computing power to export controls, not just the chips themselves. That means know- your-customer  requirements for cloud providers and close monitoring of overseas cloud infrastructure. Third, invest in systematic mapping of corporate ownership and financial networks. Screening named entities is insufficient when relationships extend across holding companies, investment vehicles, and multiple jurisdictions. Chipmakers should be expected to know who ultimately owns their customers. Fourth, establish clear security expectations and channels for intelligence-sharing with executives at the commanding heights of American technology. Congress is preparing to act. Top Republican and Democratic lawmakers hope to  include  three proposed measures toughening rules on exporting AI chips. Three House committee chairs have  demanded  a closed-door briefing from Huang.  His resignation should not end the inquiry. Congress should examine not only whether sensitive information was compromised, but how Megaspeed won Nvidia’s trust, why Commerce never acted, and why intelligence warnings to the executive branch failed to translate into meaningful action. The US has spent years building the tools to control what crosses its borders. But tools are only as strong as the institutions that wield them. title: First permanently assigned F-15EXs touch down at Kadena Air Base
zh_title: 第一架永久分配的 F-15EX 在嘉手纳空军基地着陆
summary: 日本空军基地成为美国在海外第一个接收两架永久分配的 F-15EX Eagle II 的基地，也是有史以来第二个部署该战斗机的空军基地。根据最近的一份军情发布，位于日本冲绳的嘉手纳空军基地周日接收了两架战斗机，因为空军正在努力增强美国在太平洋的空中力量，特别是在该基地继续更换其 F-15C/D 机队的情况下。 “[F-15EX] 增强了我们遏制侵略、应对新威胁以及与我们的盟友和伙伴一起保卫日本的能力，”第 18 联队指挥官 Bri
content:
日本空军基地成为美国在海外第一个接收两架永久分配的 F-15EX Eagle II 的基地，也是有史以来第二个部署该战斗机的空军基地。根据最近的一份军情发布，位于日本冲绳的嘉手纳空军基地周日接收了两架战斗机，因为空军正在努力增强美国在太平洋的空中力量，特别是在该基地继续更换其 F-15C/D 机队的情况下。 “[F-15EX] 增强了我们阻止侵略、应对新出现的威胁以及与我们的盟友和伙伴一起保卫日本的能力，”第 18 联队指挥官准将说。约翰·加勒莫尔将军在新闻稿中说道。他继续说道：“他们在嘉手纳的永久存在加强了我们对美日同盟的承诺，并确保我们继续为世界上最具战略意义的地区之一带来先进的作战能力。” 2022 年 11 月，该基地首次开始退役服役四十年后的旧版 F-15C/D 飞机。新闻稿称，过渡包括轮流部署第四代和第五代战斗机，以维持战斗机的存在，而维护人员、操作员和任务支持飞行员则寻求在新平台达到作战能力后立即利用新平台所需的专业知识。俄勒冈州空军国民警卫队收到 F-15EX 两年后，嘉手纳基地的 F-15EX 预计将增强该基地进行防空作战的能力，并增强该部队的前沿部署能力。
凭借先进的航空电子设备、现代化的电子战系统和增强的武器携带能力，这些飞机旨在与日本航空自卫队和其他地区合作伙伴一起支持双边战备。嘉手纳的第 44 和第 67 战斗机中队都计划使用 F-15EX。为了准备飞机的抵达，隶属于嘉手纳第 18 作战大队的第 67 战斗机中队的操作员前往佛罗里达州埃格林空军基地和俄勒冈州波特兰空军国民警卫队基地进行飞机资格培训。第 18 飞机维修中队的人员还与飞机制造商波音公司以及埃格林和波特兰的团队进行协调，以提高技术熟练程度。这些人员还为北卡罗来纳州西摩-约翰逊空军基地和爱达荷州芒廷霍姆空军基地的 F-15E 作战提供支持，以“保持他们的技能敏锐”。大约七个月前，空军公布了有关 F-15EX Eagle II 的新采购目标，作为空军 2027 财年预算请求的一部分，该战斗机抵达的消息传出，目标是将机队数量增加一倍以上，达到 267 架飞机，比之前计划的 129 架飞机有所增加。最近，美国空军授予波音公司一份价值 23.8 亿美元的合同，生产 22 架 F-15EX Eagle II 飞机，使该国防公司在 1 至 7 批次中生产的飞机总数达到 120 架。

【原文 English Original】
A Japan air base became the first American installation abroad to receive two permanently assigned F-15EX Eagle IIs and the second-ever Air Force location to field the fighter jet . Kadena Air Base , located in Okinawa, Japan, received two of the fighter aircraft Sunday as the Air Force strives to increase U.S. airpower in the Pacific, according to a recent service release , especially as the base continues to replace its F-15C/D fleet. “[F-15EXs] strengthen our ability to deter aggression, respond to emerging threats and defend Japan alongside our allies and partners,” 18th Wing Commander Brig. Gen. John Gallemore said in the release. “Their permanent presence at Kadena reinforces our commitment to the U.S.-Japan alliance and ensures we continue to bring advanced combat capabilities to one of the most strategically important regions in the world,” he continued. In November 2022, the base first began withdrawing its legacy F-15C/D aircraft after four decades of service. The transition included rotational deployments of fourth- and fifth-generation fighters to maintain a fighter presence while maintainers, operators and mission support airmen sought the expertise needed to utilize a new platform as soon as it reaches operational capability, the release says. Two years after the Oregon Air National Guard received theirs, the F-15EXs at Kadena are expected to increase the base’s ability to conduct counterair operations and boost the service’s forward-deployed capabilities. With advanced avionics, modernized electronic warfare systems and heightened weapons-carrying capacity, the aircraft are meant to support bilateral readiness alongside the Japan Air Self-Defense Force and other regional partners. Kadena’s 44th and 67th Fighter Squadrons are both slated to operate the F-15EXs. In preparation for the jets’ arrival, operators from the 67th Fighter Squadron, which is part of Kadena’s 18th Operations Group, traveled to Eglin Air Force Base, Florida, and Portland Air National Guard Base, Oregon, to conduct aircraft qualification training.  Personnel from the 18th Aircraft Maintenance Squadron also coordinated with Boeing, the jet’s manufacturer, and teams at Eglin and Portland to progress technical proficiency. The personnel also supported F-15E operations at Seymour-Johnson Air Force Base, North Carolina, and Mountain Home Air Force Base, Idaho, to “keep their skills sharp.” The news of the fighter’s arrival comes roughly seven months after the Air Force revealed their new acquisition goal regarding the F-15EX Eagle IIs as part of the service’s fiscal 2027 budget request, aiming to more than double the fleet to 267 aircraft, an increase from the previously planned 129 jets. More recently, the Air Force awarded Boeing a $2.38 billion contract to produce 22 F-15EX Eagle II aircraft, bringing the total number of aircraft to be manufactured by the defense company to 120 under Lots 1 through 7.

title: China’s rare earth giants double profits as prices soar
zh_title: 价格飙升 中国稀土巨头利润翻倍
summary: 由于供应控制收紧和价格上涨加强了中国对全球制造业至关重要的市场的控制，中国最大的两家稀土生产商的利润在 2026 年前 9 个月增长了一倍多。中国最大的轻稀土公司中国北方稀土（CNRE）（上交所股票代码：600111）公布的第三季度业绩显示，净利润为人民币 36.5 亿元（合 5.472 亿美元）。专注于重稀土的中国稀土资源科技有限公司（SZSE：000831）今年前九个月的销售额增长了一倍多，达到 4.08 亿元人民币（约合 6110 亿美元）
content:
由于供应控制收紧和价格上涨加强了中国对全球制造业至关重要的市场的控制，中国最大的两家稀土生产商的利润在 2026 年前 9 个月增长了一倍多。中国最大的轻稀土公司中国北方稀土（CNRE）（上交所股票代码：600111）公布的第三季度业绩显示，净利润为人民币 36.5 亿元（合 5.472 亿美元）。专注于重稀土的中国稀土资源科技有限公司（SZSE：000831）今年前九个月的收入增长了一倍多，达到4.08亿元人民币（6110万美元）。花旗分析师王安娜对路透社表示：“供给侧改革通过改善行业纪律来帮助支撑价格。”盈利增长突显了北京遏制供应过剩和巩固生产的努力如何使国内生产商受益，同时增强了中国对战略矿产供应链的影响力。由于美国制造商仍然严重依赖中国稀土，这些管制措施还使习近平主席在与美国总统唐纳德·特朗普的贸易谈判中拥有影响力。轻稀土化合物钕镨 (NdPr) 的价格较首次实施管制时上涨了 62%，达到 719,000 元人民币（107,793 美元）。这两家公司是中国在 2024 年获得生产配额的唯一企业，当时中国的配额从之前的配额减少到了 6 家。
2025年，中国对稀土开采和加工实施了更严格的控制，将配额制度扩大到包括进口材料，并要求公司定期报告战略矿产的流动情况。中国将稀土控制范围扩大到进口材料。随着整合和政府战略的实施，两家公司的全年利润都将超出分析师的预期。中国的长期游戏在看到供应过剩对其他行业造成的影响后，中国采用了生产配额和整合来确保稀土不会成为另一个受害者。对国防、电池和磁铁至关重要的矿物类别很容易出现剧烈的价格波动，从而挤压了生产商的供应和利润。由于对国内生产的控制更加严格，并受到高需求和高价格的支撑，中国将其作为与其他强国谈判的筹码。中国的出口管制涵盖了几种利基中重稀土以及含有它们的磁体。随着特朗普和习近平本周再次会面，美国总统几乎没有空间对中国征收更多关税。尽管对该行业进行了数百万美元的投资，但美国的关键矿产项目仍然只停留在纸面上，距离投产还有数年时间。在习近平会谈之前，特朗普的矿产推动尚未放松中国的控制（路透社文件）

【原文 English Original】
China’s two largest rare earths producers more than doubled their profits in the first nine months of 2026 as tighter supply controls and rising prices strengthened the country’s grip on a market critical to global manufacturing.  The country’s biggest light rare earth firm, China Northern Rare Earth (CNRE) (SSE: 600111), reported net profit of 3.65 billion yuan ($547.2 million), based on third-quarter results.  China Rare Earth Resources and Technology (SZSE: 000831), which focuses on heavy rare earths, more than doubled through the first nine months of the year to 408 million yuan ($61.1 million).  “Supply-side reforms have helped support prices by improving industry discipline,” Citi analyst Anna Wang told Reuters .  The earnings gains highlight how Beijing’s efforts to curb oversupply and consolidate production are benefiting domestic producers while reinforcing China’s influence over strategic mineral supply chains. The controls also give President Xi Jinping leverage in trade negotiations with US President Donald Trump, as American manufacturers remain heavily dependent on Chinese rare earths.  Prices for light rare earth compound neodymium-praseodymium (NdPr) are up 62% from when the controls were first introduced, to 719,000 yuan ($107,793).   The two companies were the only ones given production quotas by China in 2024, when the country downsized from giving quotas to six previously.  In 2025 China introduced tighter controls on the mining and processing of rare earths by extending the quota system to include imported materials and requiring companies to report on the flow of strategic minerals regularly. China extends rare earth controls to imported material With the consolidation and government strategies, both companies are set to beat analysts’ estimates for their full-year profit.  China’s long game   After seeing what oversupply can do to other industries, China has used production quotas and consolidation to make sure rare earths would not become another victim. The group of minerals critical for defence, batteries and magnets have been prone to aggressive price swings that have squeezed supply and profits for producers.  With a tighter grip on domestic production, and supported by high demand and prices, China uses that as leverage in negotiations with other powerful countries.   China’s export controls cover several niche medium and heavy rare earths and the magnets that contain them.  As Trump and Xi meet again this week, the American President will have little room for imposing more tariffs on China.   Even with multi-million dollar investments in the sector, critical minerals projects in the US are still only on paper, years away from production.  Trump’s minerals push has yet to loosen China’s grip ahead of Xi talks (With files from Reuters)

title: Commerce moves to place new restrictions on sale of AI chips abroad
zh_title: 商务部对人工智能芯片海外销售实施新限制
summary: 美国商务部正急于制定新的出口规则，阻止美国公司利用其他国家的第三方数据中心交易来逃避人工智能芯片销售的限制。周一，工业与安全局宣布了一项长达 132 页的临时最终规则，限制美国芯片制造商向国外第三方数据中心出售人工智能芯片的能力。该规则对出口、再出口和转移到美国武器禁运国家的海外数据中心增加了新的限制。该名单目前涵盖20多个国家，包括中国、古巴、伊朗、
content:
美国商务部正急于制定新的出口规则，阻止美国公司利用其他国家的第三方数据中心交易来逃避人工智能芯片销售的限制。周一，工业与安全局宣布了一项长达 132 页的临时最终规则，限制美国芯片制造商向国外第三方数据中心出售人工智能芯片的能力。该规则对出口、再出口和转移到美国武器禁运国家的海外数据中心增加了新的限制。该名单目前涵盖 20 多个国家，包括中国、古巴、伊朗、利比亚、朝鲜和苏丹。最终临时规则指出：“这些限制将削弱总部位于相关国家的公司使用美国先进的超级智能（SI）半导体来训练先进的 SI 模型的能力。” “数据中心、外国代工厂和芯片出口商必须对其客户进行严格的尽职调查，包括[这些国家]人员的任何直接或间接所有权或控制权，作为遵守这一新控制措施的一部分。”该规则还要求向不在武器禁运名单上的其他五个国家销售先进人工智能芯片需要新的许可证：印度尼西亚、马来西亚、新加坡、泰国和巴西。商务部长霍华德·卢特尼克已确定，这些国家存在芯片被转移到世界其他地区的“高于正常风险”。
即将或正在进行芯片销售的公司有 90 天的时间获得新许可证，其中对海外芯片设计者的豁免将减少。“临时最终”指定允许商务部绕过大部分正常的联邦规则制定程序。根据非营利组织美国行动论坛的说法，这一指定通常是为“紧急情况和其他需要的时候”保留的。商务部援引《2018 年出口管制改革法案》的授权，在不事先通知和发表评论的情况下实施这些变更。美国立法者一直将美国在半导体行业的主导地位视为相对于中国等竞争对手的关键优势，中国正在努力建设自己的国内人工智能芯片行业。一些专家敦促联邦政府进一步收紧此类芯片的全球销售，以防止它们被外国敌对势力转移或购买。将人工智能芯片列入武器禁运清单反映出人们对人工智能系统在黑客攻击和生物武器设计等领域带来的危险日益担忧。该规定是在美国芯片巨头英伟达前首席执行官黄仁勋因与员工和一名中国商业伙伴发生多起婚外情的报道而辞职几天后发布的。这位同事是中国公司 Megaspeed 的 Alice Huang，她作为潜在的中国政府资产而受到美国政策制定者的审查。报道还称，她帮助促成了 Megaspeed 和 Nvidia 之间价值 120 亿美元的人工智能芯片交易，其中一些可能已运往中国。
商务部对人工智能芯片海外销售实施新限制的消息首先出现在 Cyber​​Scoop 上。

【原文 English Original】
The Department of Commerce is rushing to put in place new export rules that prevent American companies from using third-party data center deals in other countries to evade restrictions on AI chip sales. On Monday, the Bureau of Industry and Security announced a 132-page interim final rule that limits the ability of American chipmakers to sell AI chips to third-party data centers abroad. The rule adds new restrictions on exports, reexports and transfers to overseas data centers in countries under U.S. arms embargoes. That list currently covers more than 20 nations, including China, Cuba, Iran, Libya, North Korea, and Sudan. “These restrictions will undermine the ability of companies headquartered in countries of concern from using U.S. advanced Super Intelligence (SI) semiconductors to train advanced SI models,” the final interim rule states. “Data centers, foreign foundries, and chip exporters are required to perform robust due diligence on their customers, including any direct or indirect ownership or control by persons [in those countries], as part of complying with this new control.” The rule also requires new licenses for sales of advanced AI chips to five other countries not on the arms embargo list: – Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Brazil. Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick has determined these countries present a “higher-than-normal risk” of chips being diverted to other parts of the world. Companies with pending or ongoing chip sales have 90 days to obtain the new licenses, which will contain fewer exemptions for overseas chip designers. The “interim final” designation allows Commerce to bypass much of the normal federal rulemaking process. According to the nonprofit American Action Forum, that designation is often reserved for “emergencies and other times of need.” Commerce cited its authority under the 2018 Export Control Reform Act to impose the changes without prior notice and comment. Lawmakers in the U.S. have consistently cited American dominance in the semiconductor industry as a key advantage over rivals like China, which is working to build out its own domestic AI chip industry. Some experts have urged the federal government to further tighten global sales of such chips to keep them from being diverted or purchased by hostile foreign powers. Placing AI chips on an arms embargo list reflects growing concern about the dangers AI systems bring in areas like hacking and bioweapon design. The rule was issued days after Jensen Huang, former CEO of American chip giant Nvidia, stepped down following reports of multiple affairs with staffers and a Chinese business associate. That associate, Alice Huang of Chinese company Megaspeed, is under scrutiny from U.S. policymakers as a potential Chinese government asset. Reports also say she helped broker $12 billion in deals between Megaspeed and Nvidia for AI chips, some of which may have been sent to China. title: U.S. Navy Cuts Submarine Maintenance Delays by 40% as Output Surges
zh_title: 随着产量激增，美国海军将潜艇维护延误时间减少了 40%
summary: 高级军种领导人在海军潜艇联盟 2026 年年度研讨会上报告称，随着美国潜艇工业基地改革取得进展，美国海军已将潜艇维护延误时间缩短了 40%，并在过去 12 个月内归还或交付了 10 艘潜艇。戈谢中将演讲中的“让船只投入使用”幻灯片展示了美国造船厂在加速潜艇建造方面取得的进展。海军新闻图片。潜艇部队司令里克·赛义夫中将在开幕致辞中概述了海军和工业界为缩短维护可用性而做出的联合努力
content:
高级军种领导人在海军潜艇联盟 2026 年年度研讨会上报告称，随着美国潜艇工业基地改革取得进展，美国海军已将潜艇维护延误时间缩短了 40%，并在过去 12 个月内归还或交付了 10 艘潜艇。戈谢中将演讲中的“让船只投入使用”幻灯片展示了美国造船厂在加速潜艇建造方面取得的进展。海军新闻图片。潜艇部队司令里克·赛义夫中将在开幕致辞中概述了海军和工业界为缩短现役潜艇的维护时间、同时扩大新造潜艇交付量而做出的联合努力。这一举措是在做出具有里程碑意义的采购承诺之后做出的，其中包括 7 月份价值 766 亿美元的合同，采购 5 艘哥伦比亚级 Build II 级潜艇和 9 艘弗吉尼亚级 Block VI 潜艇，以及 50 亿美元的工业基础投资。 Seif 指出，过去 12 个月内有 10 艘潜艇投入使用或重新服役。这一总数包括 2026 年初服役的两艘新建的 Block IV 弗吉尼亚级快速攻击潜艇——马萨诸塞号 (SSN-798) 和爱达荷号 (SSN-799)，以及两艘完成试航后可用性 (PSA) 的潜艇和六艘完成预定的海军作战部长 (CNO) 基地维护可用性的潜艇。 “10艘船返回，所有这些船都已做好战斗增援准备。
每一次可用性的完成都代表着一艘战斗船体重新回到舰队指挥官手中，以做好战斗准备。” – 潜艇部队司令里克·赛义夫中将。潜艇项目主任兼五角大楼潜艇直接报告组合经理罗布·高彻中将强调了接下来两艘 Block IV 潜艇的进展：即将进行海上试验的未来阿肯色号 (SSN-800) 和即将进行快速测试的未来犹他号 (SSN-801)巡航。这两艘船计划在两个月内交付，并于 2027 年春季投入使用。阿肯色州和犹他州的按时交付将标志着 14 个月内将有四艘新建的弗吉尼亚级交付。缩短维护周期来自戈谢少将的演讲，详细介绍了预期的年终目标，所有这些目标都有望在规定的时间内完成。海军新闻图片。戈谢详细介绍了公共和私人造船厂的并行进展，宣布珍珠港海军造船厂和朴茨茅斯海军造船厂目前正在维护的每艘快速攻击潜艇都已按计划或提前完成。约翰·华纳号 (SSN-785) 和伊利诺伊号 (SSN-786) 等船只代表了关键的救援案例；尽管相对于最初的基线有所延迟，但目前预计两者都将提前返回舰队。部署后维护窗口也被压缩。
爱荷华号航空母舰 (SSN-797) 在大约六个月内完成了 PSA 任务，而通常的时间为 8 到 12 个月，这使得该船能够提前执行增援任务。 高彻还指出，马萨诸塞号航空母舰 (SSN-798) 的正式 PSA 被放弃，转而由亨廷顿英格尔斯工业公司 (HII) 纽波特纽斯造船厂协助进行码头工作，从而避免了干船坞期并加速了舰队准备工作。 “我们必须首先做出承诺，消除我们自己的障碍，并增加整个企业的能力。没有任何一个组织能够独自解决这个问题。这需要共同承诺来满足国家的需求。” – 罗布·高彻中将，潜艇项目总监。穿过

【原文 English Original】
The U.S. Navy has cut submarine maintenance delays by 40% and returned or delivered 10 submarines over the past 12 months, senior service leaders reported at the Naval Submarine League’s 2026 Annual Symposium as U.S. submarine industrial base reforms gain traction. Getting Boats into Service Slide from Vice Admiral Gaucher’s Presentation showcasing the progress made in accelerating submarine construction in U.S. shipyard. Naval News image. Throughout his opening remarks, Vice Adm. Rick Seif, Commander, Submarine Forces, outlined joint Navy and industry efforts to shorten maintenance availabilities for active submarines while scaling new-construction deliveries. That push follows landmark procurement commitments, including July’s $76.6 billion contract package for five Columbia-class Build II and nine Virginia-class Block VI submarines, alongside $5 billion in industrial base investments. Seif noted that 10 submarines either entered or returned to service over the past 12 months. That total comprises two new-build Block IV Virginia-class fast-attack submarines commissioned in early 2026— USS Massachusetts (SSN-798) and USS Idaho (SSN-799)—alongside two boats completing Post-Shakedown Availabilities (PSAs) and six completing scheduled Chief of Naval Operations (CNO) depot maintenance availabilities. “10 boats returned, all those boats are combat surge ready. Each availability completed represents a combat hull put back into the hands of fleet commanders to generate combat readiness.” – Vice Admiral Rick Seif, Commander, Submarine Forces. Vice Adm. Rob Gaucher, Director, Submarine Programs and the Pentagon’s Submarine Direct Reporting Portfolio Manager, highlighted progress on the next two Block IV boats: the future USS Arkansas (SSN-800), which is on the precipice of sea trials, and the future USS Utah (SSN-801), which is nearing its fast cruise. Both boats are scheduled for delivery within two months and commissioning in Spring 2027. On-time delivery of Arkansas and Utah would mark four new-build Virginia-class deliveries within a 14-month span. Shortening Maintenance Periods Slide from Rear Admiral Gaucher’s speech detailing prospective end of year goals, all of which are on track for completion within the allotted time frame. Naval News Image. Gaucher detailed parallel progress in public and private shipyards, announcing that every fast-attack submarine currently in maintenance at Pearl Harbor Naval Shipyard and Portsmouth Naval Shipyard is either on or ahead of schedule. Boats such as USS John Warner (SSN-785) and USS Illinois (SSN-786) represent key recovery cases; although delayed relative to their original baselines, both are now projected to return to the fleet ahead of their adjusted schedules. Post-deployment maintenance windows have also compressed. USS Iowa (SSN-797) completed its PSA in roughly six months compared to the typical eight-to-12-month window, making the boat available for surge tasking ahead of schedule. Gaucher also pointed to USS Massachusetts (SSN-798), whose formal PSA was waived in favor of pierside work facilitated by Huntington Ingalls Industries’ (HII) Newport News Shipbuilding, avoiding a drydocking period and accelerating fleet readiness. “We must commit first, remove our own barriers, and add capacity across our enterprise. No one organization can solve this by themselves. It requires a shared commitment to deliver what the nation needs.” – Vice Admiral Rob Gaucher, Director, Submarine Programs. Across the enterprise, cumulative days of maintenance delay fell from 1,400 days in FY24 to 800 days in FY25, before dropping another ~40% to 500 cumulative days in FY26 to date, with further reductions expected. At the same time, total submarine construction hours rose to nearly 29 million in 2026, up from 22 million the previous year—tracking toward a targeted ~30% year-over-year increase. Acquisition and Supplier Reforms A Virginia-class submarine under construction at General Dynamics Electric Boat. (Image GDEB). The effect of drastically reducing delay backlogs and the amount of time taken to produce or retrofit submarines come from a dedicated effort and sweeping reform, especially as it relates to how the Navy, funding bodies, and industry interact and work together to solve issues. In particular, Gaucher noted that reforms such as prior investments into Virginia -class parts and ensuring a stock of spare material over the past 3 years yielded dramatically positive effects on ensuring maintenance continued even through potential issues. Part of ensuring availability of materials also stems from Gaucher’s efforts to remove administrative bottlenecks for a supplier base totaling ~27,000 separate suppliers through responding efficiently to industry feedback. Eliminating administrative barriers remains a high priority, with reduction in vendor certification times by up to %60 in some areas, nearing the %75 reduction originally ordered by Gaucher. Rapid funding mechanisms also helped to improve prospects, as 11 Other Transaction Authority agreements were implemented in the past year, with Gaucher noting the increased speed of getting necessary funds to suppliers and contractors over legacy contract systems. Consolidation of contract has also have had a measurable effect, as contractors that may have received 100s of separate contracts now get a handful of contracts covering the same items , allowing for easier access, a tally of needed parts, and easier management across program offices, with the goal of consolidation of work into master contracts most suppliers. Other reforms include the establishment of 41 priority suppliers, the establishment of facilities to construct sub-components outside of prime shipyards enabling greater focus on work only larger contractors can do, working personally with major yards to shore up behind schedule programs, pay increases for workers, and increasingly digitized infrastructure at suppliers/yards/contractors. Program Scorecards, Torpedoes, and Weapons Infrastructure Sailors assigned to the Virginia-class fast-attack submarine USS Minnesota (SSN 783) guide a Mark 48 ADCAP (Advanced Capability) torpedo during a weapons offload onboard Naval Base Guam, Feb. 3, 2025. (U.S. Navy photo by Mass Communication Specialist 1st Class Nikita Custer). Gaucher also underscored the impact of a new internal “scorecard” tracking individual submarine programs across production milestones. Early warning indicators prompt direct engagement with prime contractor executives before schedule slippage compounds. Under the current assessment, two submarine shipbuilding programs are ahead of schedule, six are on schedule, and only one is behind. Beyond hull construction and maintenance, Seif announced that the U.S. Navy’s torpedo inventory grew by up to 200 Mk 48 ADCAP heavyweight warshots, supporting full loadout availability across the submarine force. Additionally, construction of support facilities and weapons programs designed to outfit submarines notably increased within the past 12 months, with Naval News reporting on the construction of new hypersonic weapons facility near Naval Station Norfolk , the progress of the Mk-58 Compact Rapid Attack Weapon , and the Navy’s need for the new lower-cost RAPTOR heavyweight torpedo . The post U.S. Navy Cuts Submarine Maintenance Delays by 40% as Output Surges appeared first on Naval News .

title: Launch Preview: Ariane 6 to launch Amazon satellites, Falcon 9 to launch government missions
